items.title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
items.details: Junchao Huang, Guian Fang, Shengju Qian, Xianghao Kong et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: SolarWM introduces a novel framework for building interactive video world models that integrates a reconfigurable multi-source data engine and a backbone-native adaptation system, addressing challenges in training with heterogeneous data sources. It processes 1.43 million clips from 10 datasets into a unified format, enabling the training of four models (5B–33B parameters) with real-time interaction capabilities over long rollouts, significantly improving reproducibility and extensibility in the field. The framework, along with its data, recipes, and weights, is fully open-sourced to facilitate further research in interactive world models.
items.judge: This work introduces SolarWM, a foundation for building interactive video world models, aligning with generative video and world models.

items.title: Thinking in Pictures: A Systematic Benchmark for Reasoning-driven Image Generation
items.details: Yutong Liu, Nan Huang, Xu Cao, James M. Rehg · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces RIG-BENCH, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate Reasoning-driven Image Generation (RIG) across four challenging domains, highlighting a significant reasoning-generation gap in current unified generative models (UGMs). With 2000 curated samples, RIG-BENCH aims to diagnose the limitations of existing models, which often produce locally plausible yet globally illogical outputs, thereby guiding the development of more logically grounded generative systems. This benchmark addresses the underexplored area of high-level visual reasoning, crucial for advancing generative intelligence in image synthesis.
items.judge: This paper presents a benchmark for reasoning-driven image generation, which is pertinent to generative image models.

items.title: RoGe: Novel View Synthesis via End-to-End Implicit Reconstruction and Generation
items.details: Xiaolei Lang, Ze Kang, Zehao Huang, Naiyan Wang · cs.CV
items.summary: RoGe introduces an end-to-end framework for novel view synthesis that integrates implicit reconstruction and generation without relying on explicit 3D representations, improving temporal coherence in synthesized videos from sparse input views. It outperforms existing methods on the DL3DV dataset in both image-level metrics and video-level temporal consistency, demonstrating that jointly trained ray-queried implicit features provide superior conditioning compared to traditional approaches. Notably, the model eliminates the need for lossy projections, allowing for more accurate scene representation and generation.
items.judge: The paper discusses novel view synthesis, which is relevant to generative image and 3D generation.

items.title: Multi-Tool Image Editing Attribution in Facial Forgery
items.details: Sheng Liu, Qiang Sheng, Danding Wang, Yu Li et al. · cs.CV cs.MM
items.summary: The paper introduces Multi-Tool Image Editing Attribution (MIEA), a novel method designed to identify multiple editing tools used in facial image edits, addressing the limitations of existing single-tool attribution methods. The authors present a new dataset, MultiEdit, comprising over 500,000 edited facial images, and propose DPEC, which utilizes locality-aware traces from both spatial and frequency domains, achieving superior performance compared to nine baseline methods in multi-tool scenarios. The method demonstrates significant improvements in attribution accuracy for images edited with up to five different tools.
items.judge: The paper addresses multi-tool image editing attribution, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: InceptionGS: Generative Bootstrapping for Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting under Unstructured View Sampling
items.details: Tianheng Lu, Guangyu Wang, Ruqi Huang, Lu Fang · cs.CV
items.summary: InceptionGS introduces a novel approach to Gaussian splatting that effectively addresses the challenges of unstructured view sampling in large-scale scene digitization by balancing reconstruction and generation. The method enhances the quality of rendered scenes by repairing problematic regions caused by view scarcity while maintaining fidelity in well-covered areas, demonstrating significant improvements in handling unstructured imagery and boosting high-fidelity Gaussian splatting. Extensive experiments validate its effectiveness across various real-world large-scale scenes.
items.judge: The work on Gaussian splatting for scene digitization is relevant to 3D generation and image generation.

items.title: Generating Medical Image Counterfactuals using Causal Explanations
items.details: David A. Kelly, Tom Yaacov, Nathan Blake, Sander Beckers et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The authors present a novel framework for generating medical image counterfactuals that eliminates the need for auxiliary generative models, relying instead on causal evidence extracted directly from the classifier. This deterministic approach allows for controllable edits in specified regions of interest and demonstrates superior fidelity to the original images compared to existing generative methods, effectively enhancing explainability in medical image diagnosis. Experiments indicate that the method successfully alters classifier predictions while maintaining closer alignment with the original images than generative baselines.
items.judge: The paper discusses generating counterfactual medical images, which is a form of generative image modeling.

items.title: Genesis: A Generative Engine for Hierarchical Satellite Image Synthesis
items.details: Subash Khanal, Yangzhi Cui, Daniel Cher, Eric Xing et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Genesis, a generative engine designed for multi-scale tile completion in satellite imagery, addressing the limitation of existing models that operate along a single axis of resolution or scale. Genesis combines a vertical super-resolution model and a horizontal mask-based outpainting model to synthesize globally consistent quadtree structures from sparse seed tiles, achieving state-of-the-art results in both tasks. The authors also present the dense500 dataset for benchmarking, which includes a fully observed multi-scale pyramid of satellite imagery.
items.judge: The paper discusses a generative model for satellite imagery, which aligns with generative image modeling.

items.title: GDB-Reward: From Evaluation Metrics to Training Rewards for Graphic Design
items.details: Adrienne Deganutti, Purvanshi Mehta, Simon Hadfield, Andrew Gilbert · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces GDB-Reward, a novel framework that converts diverse graphic design evaluation metrics into a unified reinforcement learning reward, enabling effective optimization for text-to-image models without the need for fine-tuning. Experiments show that GDB-Reward significantly enhances adherence to design specifications in terms of perceptual quality, rendering fidelity, and spatial accuracy, while keeping the image generator frozen. This approach demonstrates the potential of using non-differentiable metrics as active optimization objectives in scenarios lacking differentiable supervision.
items.judge: The paper addresses reward functions for graphic design in text-to-image models, relevant to generative image tasks.

items.title: ZipTok3D: High-Fidelity 3D Tokenization with Compact Token Prefixes
items.details: Mingda Lin, Weijie Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Bowen Cui et al. · 19 HF upvotes
items.summary: ZipTok3D introduces a novel 3D tokenization method that significantly enhances reconstruction fidelity from extremely short token sequences by organizing object geometry into informative global-token prefixes. This approach allows for high-quality reconstructions using only one token on ShapeNet and four tokens on TRELLIS, achieving 32x and 8x reductions in token sequence length compared to the 32-token COD-VAE baseline. The method employs nested dropout during training to prioritize essential geometric information, enabling efficient decoding through a shared Transformer block without requiring a separate generative sampling stage.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel 3D tokenizer aimed at improving generation quality.

items.title: Kirin: Animal Motion Generation from In-the-Wild Video
items.details: Brian Nlong Zhao, Zhuoyang Pan, James M. Rehg, Jiajun Wu et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: Kirin introduces a novel framework for animal motion generation from in-the-wild video, addressing the scarcity of high-quality motion data for animals. It reconstructs 3D motion sequences and creates AiM3D, the first large-scale dataset of aligned video-text-motion tuples for quadrupeds, enabling realistic motion generation conditioned on both text and images. The framework also automates the rigging and animation of 3D meshes, facilitating ready-to-render animated assets, thus significantly advancing the field of animal motion modeling and animation.
items.judge: The paper introduces a framework for animal motion generation from video, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: NeoMME: A Single-Tower Multimodal-Native Multilingual Foundation Encoder for Efficient Fine-Tuning and Inference
items.details: Aurélien Lac, Tony Wu · 19 HF upvotes
items.summary: NeoMME introduces a novel family of multimodal and multilingual bidirectional encoders with 260M and 800M parameters, designed to efficiently process multilingual text and raw image patches within a single Transformer architecture. The models achieve state-of-the-art performance on the ViDoRe v3 benchmark, with the 800M variant reaching an nDCG@10 score of 0.556, while also demonstrating approximately 2x throughput improvement over ColModernVBERT for 2048x2048 image inputs. Notably, NeoMME employs hierarchical token pooling and asymmetric quantization, achieving a 255x compression of multimodal document embeddings while maintaining over 95% of the baseline performance.
items.judge: The paper presents a multimodal foundation model relevant for efficient fine-tuning and inference.

items.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
items.details: Irina Proskurina, Guillaume Metzler, Antoine Gourru, Julien Velcin · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: Debias-SparseGPT introduces a novel post-training pruning method that mitigates bias amplification in Large Language Models (LLMs) caused by weight sparsification techniques like SparseGPT. The method employs representational debiasing through a second-order term based on demographically contrasting inputs, achieving consistent reductions in pruning-induced bias while maintaining model perplexity and zero-shot accuracy across various sparsity levels (25%, 50%, and structured 2:4). Notably, under the stringent 2:4 structured sparsity, augmenting the calibration set with long-context examples enhances both performance and fairness, thus improving the bias-performance trade-off in sparse models.
items.judge: The paper discusses pruning techniques for LLMs, relevant for inference acceleration.

items.title: SnapBench: Benchmarking Snap-and-Ask Multimodal Retrieval for Mobile Interactions
items.details: Zirong Chen, Fuda Ye, Kuan Zhang, Enjun Du et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: SnapBench introduces the first paired benchmark for robust snap-and-ask multimodal retrieval, featuring 1,145 queries and 9,085 gallery items across 53 controlled corruption conditions. The evaluation of 16 multimodal retrievers reveals that image corruptions significantly degrade retrieval performance, while text corruptions primarily affect text-only retrieval. The study also proposes MOOR (Modality-anchored, Outlier-aware, Optimal Reweighting), an adaptive fusion method aimed at improving reliability in multimodal interactions.
items.judge: The introduction of a benchmark for multimodal retrieval is relevant to generative media.

items.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Image Captioning with SimLoss
items.details: Suryaansh Jain, Rahasya Barkur, Vishal G, Ryan Rossi et al. · 13 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces SimLoss, a novel reference-free embedding-space objective for single-pass fine-grained image captioning, which significantly improves inference speed and precision. The fully differentiable fine-tuning variant, SimLoss FFT, achieves the highest precision while running approximately 20 times faster than traditional multi-stage systems, and nearly matches their F1 score. The reward-based variant, SimLoss GRPO, excels in recall, demonstrating that embedding-space supervision can effectively enhance caption quality without the latency associated with multi-stage approaches.
items.judge: The paper discusses fine-grained image captioning, which relates to vision-language models.

items.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation
items.details: Run Yang, Runpeng Dai, Jie Sun, Jielei Zhang et al. · 14 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Influence-Directed Adaptive On-Policy Distillation (IDA-OPD), which addresses the diversity bottleneck in sampled-token on-policy distillation by preserving entropy-expanding updates while replacing entropy-contracting ones with divergence-adaptive advantage shrinkage. This method improves pass@k performance, effectively inheriting the teacher's diversity, while maintaining pass@1 levels and achieving these results at a lower computational cost compared to existing teacher-informed methods, without requiring full-vocabulary teacher information.
items.judge: This paper discusses a distillation technique that could be relevant to generative media.

items.title: magnitudedev/magnitude
items.details: 1,828★ · 130 stars today
items.summary: The repository "magnitudedev/magnitude" presents an open-source inference server designed to optimize the deployment of local models based on the user's hardware specifications. It supports integration with various agents, including Pi, OpenCode, and Claude Code, facilitating efficient model inference without the need for extensive reconfiguration. Notably, the server aims to streamline the process of running generative models across diverse platforms, enhancing accessibility for ML researchers and practitioners.
items.judge: This item is an open-source inference server that could be useful for generative media.

items.title: SpatialGuard: Harness-Guided Verifiable Spatial Reasoning for Text-to-Image Generation
items.details: Ziyun Qian, Zizhi Chen, Yizhou Liu, Mingyang Sun et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: SpatialGuard introduces a structured layout-guided framework for 3D text-to-image generation, enhancing spatial reasoning by integrating a Spatial Layout Architect, Visual Realizer, and Visual Alignment Critic to ensure consistency among prompts, layouts, and images. This approach transforms the generation process into a verifiable sequence of planning, realization, validation, and repair, significantly improving spatial faithfulness compared to existing methods. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that SpatialGuard achieves state-of-the-art performance in complex spatial layout generation, addressing issues of object relations and visibility that persist in prior models.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for improving controllability in text-to-image generation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
items.details: Danze Chen, Zeqing Wang, Ziyue Lin, Xingyi Yang et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: H3-World introduces a novel framework that enhances the 33B MiniMax-H3 video generator by enabling precise, temporally grounded control through natural language instructions, without the need for dedicated action modules. By employing temporal attention routing and reusing semantic representations from large-scale video pretraining, H3-World achieves effective character and camera control with only 8,000 gameplay samples and 10,000 LoRA optimization steps, while maintaining high generation quality and generalizing to unseen scenarios. This approach demonstrates a significant advancement in transforming the control capabilities of large video generators into interactive world models.
items.judge: Introduces a framework for interactive world modeling using a video generator.

items.title: Revisiting Cross-View Completion: Self-Supervised Pre-Training via Reconstruction Error Comparison
items.details: Thibaut Loiseau, Guillaume Bourmaud, Vincent Lepetit · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Gekko, a self-supervised network that enhances cross-view completion by leveraging reconstruction error comparisons to improve feature learning for 3D vision. Gekko achieves up to 6 times higher accuracy in zero-shot correspondence estimation and a 22% reduction in end-point error on the ETH3D dataset compared to the CroCo method, while also eliminating the need for 3D preprocessing by enabling training directly from raw videos. The model's ability to detect co-visibility in unseen scenes further strengthens its performance, and the authors provide code and pre-trained models for public use.
items.judge: The paper presents a self-supervised method for 3D vision, directly relevant to generative 3D models.

items.title: TempCloze: Can Video-LLMs Identify the Missing Middle?
items.details: Wenqi Pei, Henry Hengyuan Zhao, Yilai Liu, Jiahao Meng et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces TempCloze, a novel video cloze benchmark designed to evaluate visual temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs by requiring models to identify the missing middle segment of a video from four candidates. This benchmark, comprising 1,521 filtered videos, minimizes linguistic shortcuts by focusing on semantic, alignment, and progression dimensions, revealing that alignment is a significant bottleneck for current models. Evaluations of 31 Video-LLMs indicate that while models perform well on semantic content and event progression, they struggle with temporal alignment, highlighting areas for further improvement in model design and training.
items.judge: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating visual temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs, relevant to video generation.

items.title: CameraEditor: Camera-Controlled Image Editing via Video-Prior Sequential Modeling
items.details: Xin Shen, Chengyou Jia, Keshuo Xing, Zifeng Zhu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: CameraEditor introduces a novel framework for camera-controlled image editing by reformulating the task as a temporal sequence prediction problem, significantly improving control over geometric parameters during large perspective shifts. By integrating a geometric perception module and a dynamic reference routing mechanism, it achieves state-of-the-art precision in camera control and source identity preservation, outperforming existing models. The approach is validated on a dataset of 5,760 instances and includes the CamEditor-Bench, a model-agnostic evaluation suite with 462 test cases.
items.judge: Addresses camera-controlled image editing, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Gaussian Core LoRA: Distribution-Aware Dynamic Adaptation for Broad Concept Erasure
items.details: Qinghui Gong, Xunlei Chen, Yu-Xuan Zhang, Hua Meng et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Gaussian Core LoRA, a distribution-aware low-rank adaptation framework that enhances concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models by employing a Gaussian mixture model to better capture the latent semantic prototypes within target concepts. This approach allows for prototype-adaptive erasure, significantly improving performance metrics: it reduces the average Attack Success Rate (ASR) by 7.95%, lowers the COCO Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by 14.72%, and increases the CLIP Score by 4.98% compared to existing methods. The framework demonstrates robustness to adversarial prompts and scalability for multi-identity and multi-style erasure, while maintaining compatibility with models like SDXL and FLUX.
items.judge: This work on concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models is highly relevant to generative image models.

items.title: What, Where, and How: Probing Spatiotemporal Representations in Video Foundation Models
items.details: Sharon S. Musa, Fereshteh Forghani, Harrish Thasarathan, Sonia Joseph et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: This paper presents a systematic analysis of spatiotemporal representations in video foundation models V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAE-v2, revealing that both models effectively encode camera motion with over 90% ROC AUC at 60-70% network depth, while achieving moderate anomaly detection (>60% ROC AUC) but struggling with intuitive physics tasks. The authors introduce geometry-aware spline-based steering for interpolating camera motion in latent representations, resulting in smoother video trajectories and improved temporal coherence compared to linear interpolation.
items.judge: The paper analyzes spatiotemporal representations in video foundation models, relevant to generative video.

items.title: DualDiff3D: Dual Structure-Appearance Diffusion Priors for Reliability-Enhanced 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.details: Qian Wang, Yu Wang, Weiqi Li, Xinhua Cheng et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces DualDiff3D, a novel framework that employs dual diffusion priors with a Structure-Appearance Attention (SAA) module to enhance 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by improving the quality of novel views rendered from limited input. By separating the extraction of structural information and appearance consistency into two diffusion branches, the method effectively reduces artifacts and blurriness, achieving superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in inference-only scenarios. The authors provide their code and pre-trained weights in an open-source repository.
items.judge: The paper discusses enhancing 3D Gaussian Splatting using diffusion priors, relevant to 3D generation.

items.title: ZimaBlue: Evolving Generalizable World Action Models through Scalable Video Pre-training
items.details: Xionghao Wu, Yijun Yang, Shiyang Zhou, Haoze Sun et al. · 38 HF upvotes
items.summary: ZimaBlue introduces a scalable framework for learning generalizable World Action Models (WAMs) from large-scale egocentric videos, significantly improving robotic manipulation capabilities. By leveraging a three-stage training curriculum and an asynchronous Slow-Fast dual-system architecture, the model achieves a zero-shot success rate increase from 36.1% to 77.8% when trained on over 120,000 hours of embodied video. This approach enhances real-time control and generalization across diverse tasks, particularly for unseen scenarios.
items.judge: The paper focuses on evolving world action models through video pre-training, directly related to generative video.

items.title: RECAP-Forcing: Retaining Content Appearances for Long Video Generation
items.details: Haiyang Xu, Zheng Ding, Zhuowen Tu · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces RECAP-Forcing, a novel memory organization technique for long autoregressive video generation that prioritizes appearance novelty over recency, allowing models to retain key visual content as it first appears. This approach enhances long-range consistency and visual quality without additional learnable parameters, outperforming existing memory methods across multiple strong baselines. The method employs an attention sink for initial scenes and an optical-flow-based novelty bank for evolving content, effectively addressing the limitations of traditional temporal memory organization.
items.judge: The proposed RECAP-Forcing method addresses memory challenges in long video generation.

items.title: Learning Where Outcomes Change:Credit-Addressable Reasoning for Multimodal Geometry
items.details: Jiani Guo, Junjie Wang, Jie Wu, Pengxiang Zhao et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces credit-addressable reasoning for multimodal geometry, enhancing visual language models (VLMs) by allowing semantic units to define learning comparisons and credit assignment. The proposed method, instantiated as Code-CoT and CE-GRPO, achieves an average accuracy of 76.04 across nine geometry benchmarks, surpassing Qwen3-VL-8B and trajectory-level GRPO by 8.09 and 3.43 points, respectively. This approach demonstrates improved performance in long, dependency-heavy reasoning tasks by integrating representation and optimization design.
items.judge: Involves VLMs in geometry reasoning, relevant to multimodal reasoning.

items.title: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
items.details: Venus Team, Zhuohan Cai, Haoxing Chen, Jiaxuan Chen et al. · 53 HF upvotes
items.summary: UI-Venus-2 introduces a general-purpose foundation GUI agent that significantly enhances the deployment of multimodal agents across over 170 multilingual mobile apps and native desktop operating systems. It improves task automation by employing a deep-research pipeline for function-grounded instruction generation and implements robust verification mechanisms, including trace-level evaluators and multi-model voting, to ensure reliable reinforcement learning signals. This open-source framework aims to create more generalizable and verifiable agents for practical applications in real-world environments.
items.judge: The paper presents a multimodal GUI agent, which has some relevance to generative models.

items.title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving
items.details: Xin Zhou, Zongchuang Zhao, Zhibo Yang, Mingsheng Li et al. · 334 HF upvotes
items.summary: Qwen-Drive-1.0 introduces a vision-language foundation model tailored for autonomous driving, integrating 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning into a unified architecture. It features a bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception head for 3D object detection and scene segmentation, enhancing the model's interpretability of 3D structures. The training methodology combines driving supervision with general vision-language data, yielding strong performance in 3D perception and motion planning while maintaining general vision-language capabilities.
items.judge: The vision-language model integrates 3D perception, relevant to generative tasks.

items.title: EM^2Mem: Event-Centric Multimodal Memory for Large Language Models
items.details: Yijun Chen, Yaqi Zheng, Yanya Li, Boyi Xiao et al. · 8 HF upvotes
items.summary: EM^2Mem introduces an event-centric multimodal memory framework that enhances long-video question answering by binding heterogeneous evidence to event anchors, allowing for more coherent and contextually relevant memory retrieval. This approach improves average accuracy over existing memory baselines by 2.0 to 3.7 points across three benchmarks, increases strict event-level Top-5 evidence recall by 7.0 points, and significantly reduces per-query latency by 4.67 times while decreasing total inference tokens by 63.66%. The implementation will be integrated into the LightMem repository on GitHub.
items.judge: The paper discusses a multimodal memory framework relevant to long-video question answering.

items.title: ReFlowSET: Representation-Aligned Latent Flow Matching for SAR-to-EO Image Translation
items.details: Jeonghyeok Do, Seungchul Lee, Munchurl Kim · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: ReFlowSET introduces a novel conditional latent flow-matching framework for SAR-to-EO image translation that improves reconstruction fidelity by selecting codecs through a joint SAR-EO reconstruction audit, rather than relying on pretrained codecs. The method employs a smaller conditional DiT trained from scratch, utilizing dual-stream SAR conditioning and semantic alignment with a frozen vision foundation model, achieving state-of-the-art performance on QXS-SAROPT and SAR2Opt datasets. The code and pretrained weights are available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The work on SAR-to-EO image translation involves generative image techniques.

items.title: CoVA-SFT: A Large-Scale Dataset for Chain of Visual Abstractions
items.details: Tsung-Han Wu, Heekyung Lee, Anya Ji, Haoming Chen et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces CoVA-SFT, a large-scale dataset comprising 51.9K samples and over 222K multimodal reasoning steps designed to enhance chain-of-thought reasoning in multimodal language models. It demonstrates that models fine-tuned on CoVA-SFT achieve over 2x improvement on the CoVA-Bench benchmark compared to existing interleaved chain-of-thought baselines, although they still lag behind text-only chain-of-thought models. This dataset addresses the lack of structured resources for teaching models to integrate visual and textual reasoning effectively.
items.judge: The dataset aims to improve visual reasoning in models, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam
items.details: `python` · 96,450★ · 226 stars today
items.summary: The repository "hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam" introduces a real-time face-swapping and one-click video deepfake solution that operates using only a single image of the target face. This approach streamlines the deepfake creation process, significantly reducing the input requirements compared to traditional methods that often necessitate multiple images or extensive training data. The implementation focuses on efficiency and user accessibility, making it suitable for rapid deployment in various applications.
items.judge: This project involves real-time face swap and video deepfake generation.

items.title: 3b1b/manim
items.details: `python` · 92,829★ · 432 stars today
items.summary: The repository "3b1b/manim" is an animation engine designed specifically for creating explanatory math videos. It allows users to generate high-quality animations programmatically, facilitating the visualization of mathematical concepts. Notable design choices include a modular architecture that supports custom scene creation and a focus on mathematical accuracy in visual representations.
items.judge: This is an animation engine for creating explanatory math videos.

items.title: WebLLM: high-performance in-browser LLM inference engine
items.details: 21 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49536411)
items.summary: WebLLM is an in-browser inference engine for large language models that achieves high performance by leveraging WebAssembly and SIMD optimizations, enabling efficient execution of LLMs directly in web environments. The repository includes a modular architecture that allows for easy integration of various model architectures and supports quantization techniques to reduce memory usage while maintaining inference speed. Notably, it demonstrates significant improvements in latency and throughput compared to existing browser-based LLM solutions.
items.judge: The in-browser LLM inference engine may have implications for generative media applications.

items.title: DreamX-Creator: Democratizing Native Audio-Video Generation at 2K Resolution
items.details: Jiashu Zhu, Yanhao Zheng, Ruitian Tian, Rujing Dang et al. · cs.CV cs.SD
items.summary: DreamX-Creator 1.0 introduces a compact 7B generator for joint audio-video generation, achieving synchronized output at 2K resolution through a novel Gated Cross-Modal Attention mechanism. The system processes audio and video streams independently before coupling them, and employs a progressive training approach that includes audio-video reinforcement learning for enhanced quality. This framework not only matches the performance of leading open-source systems but also aims to democratize access to high-quality audio-video generation tools for further research.
items.judge: The paper introduces a joint audio-video generation system, which is highly relevant to generative media.

items.title: BRF-GS: Hyperspectral Bidirectional Reflectance Factor Modeling and Image Generation Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.details: Yiling Yao, Wenjuan Zhang, Bowen Wang, Bocheng Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces BRF-GS, a novel framework for hyperspectral bidirectional reflectance factor (BRF) modeling and image generation that leverages 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). It enhances the representation of complex directional reflectance through a hybrid BRDF-driven kernel and employs a two-stage training strategy that separates geometry optimization from spectral modeling, resulting in improved spatial and spectral fidelity in generated images. The framework is validated on the newly constructed AIR-BRF dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately reproducing view-dependent BRF responses in remote sensing applications.
items.judge: The paper discusses 3D Gaussian Splatting for image generation, aligning with generative image models.

items.title: BLARM: Animating 3D Objects from Video via Blending Latent Rigid Motion Primitives
items.details: Pradyumn Goyal, Yizhak Ben-Shabat, Hsueh-Ti Derek Liu, Haomiao Jiang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: BLARM introduces a novel feed-forward method for animating 3D meshes from monocular video, achieving temporally coherent animations without the need for traditional rigging or high-dimensional vertex motion regression. By utilizing a compact set of learned, time-varying rigid motion components and a factorized spatial-temporal attention mechanism, BLARM significantly reduces the complexity of the deformation space while maintaining accuracy and stability in animations. The model is trained using trajectory reconstruction and motion-aware contrastive learning, resulting in interpretable motion structures derived from video input.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for animating 3D objects from video, directly related to generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: Identity-Conditioned Latent Consistency Distillation for Face Synthesis
items.details: Tiago Kienen Chaves, Bernardo Biesseck, David Menotti · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel identity-conditioned face synthesis method using a latent Consistency Model that achieves a 4.36× speed-up in inference time (0.4819 seconds per image) compared to the Arc2Face diffusion model (2.102 seconds), without sacrificing image quality. By distilling knowledge from Arc2Face and adapting its pipeline to use ArcFace identity embeddings instead of textual prompts, the proposed model maintains competitive FID scores, achieving near-parity on CelebA and outperforming Arc2Face on WebFace42M. The implementation is available at https://github.com/UFPR-IPASP-PR/FaceRec-IdentityConsistency.
items.judge: The work discusses identity-conditioned face synthesis using diffusion models, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Audio-Driven Adversarial Defense for 3D Talking Face Generation with totally Visual Fidelity Preservation
items.details: Rui-Qing Sun, Chen-Hao Cui, Hui-Yang Zhao, Tian Lan et al. · cs.CV cs.MM
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel audio-driven defense mechanism for 3D talking face generation that shifts protective measures from the visual to the audio domain, utilizing psychoacoustic masking to embed perturbations within perceptually masked frequency regions of speech. This approach effectively degrades the quality of generated 3D faces while maintaining high visual fidelity, outperforming traditional visual perturbation methods that compromise image quality. Experimental results indicate significant improvements in privacy protection without perceptual distortion, marking a promising advancement in safeguarding against identity misuse in generative models.
items.judge: This work focuses on 3D talking face generation, which is a significant aspect of generative media.

items.title: MR-JEPA: A General Purpose Video Foundation Model for Cardiac MRI
items.details: Athira J. Jacob, Puneet Sharma, Dorin Comaniciu, Daniel Rueckert · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: MR-JEPA introduces a self-supervised video foundation model specifically designed for cardiac MRI, enhancing the processing of multi-sequence data (cine, LGE, mapping) through innovative tubelet tokenization and spatiotemporal masking. It significantly outperforms existing models on five regression tasks, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.79% for LV ejection fraction and 1.87 for GLS, with reductions of 21-27% over baselines, while maintaining competitive performance in disease detection with a macro AUG of 0.868. This model demonstrates the efficacy of a unified video encoder for comprehensive cardiac analysis without the need for annotations.
items.judge: The paper introduces a video foundation model for cardiac MRI, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
items.details: Yi Ding, Ruqi Zhang · cs.LG cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA), a novel supervision-free method that enhances learning in on-policy distillation by using entropy-adaptive negative advantages, which improves performance by redistributing probability mass among high-entropy tokens. OPSA achieves a 35.41 point increase in Avg@32 on AIME24, representing a 263% relative gain over the base model Qwen3-1.7B, and outperforms traditional on-policy distillation by 16.77 points. The findings suggest that effective learning can occur without reliance on noisy teacher supervision, focusing instead on suppressing low log-probability tokens.
items.judge: The paper analyzes on-policy distillation, which has implications for generative media training.

items.title: MNIST-PRO: MNIST is Back as a Partially Observable World for AI Agents
items.details: Vernon Toh, Navonil Majumder, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen et al. · cs.AI cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces MNIST-PRO, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to construct and interpret perceptual states in partially observable environments by transforming MNIST digit recognition into a sequential, glimpse-based search task. The authors assess ten multimodal models across various memory representations and identify significant performance gaps under partial observability, highlighting three key bottlenecks: challenges in integrating fragmented glimpses, premature exploration cessation, and difficulties in revising incorrect beliefs. This work emphasizes the necessity for agents to not only gather visual evidence but also to effectively build and update their perceptual states.
items.judge: The MNIST-PRO benchmark relates to agent perception in a controlled environment, relevant to world models.

items.title: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
items.details: Jiajun Wu, Jian Yang, Yaxin Du, Wei Zhang et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: WebWorld introduces a novel framework that leverages a browser as a deterministic world model to enhance the self-improvement of web code by VLMs. This approach significantly improves performance, achieving a 5.3-point increase on HTMLBench-400 and a 14.9-point increase on MiniAppBench-Val compared to Raw-27B, matching the capabilities of leading systems like Kimi-K2.6 and GPT-5.4 in interactive HTML generation. The design choice to use browser-backed admission is critical, as ablation studies indicate that without this mechanism, performance gains diminish substantially.
items.judge: This work presents a browser as a world model for web code, directly relating to generative media.

items.title: Chat-Edit-3D++: Interactive 3D and 4D Scene Editing via Large Language Models
items.details: Shuangkang Fang, Yufeng Wang, Yi-Hsuan Tsai, Wenrui Ding et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces the Hash-Atlas network and CE3D++, a novel framework for interactive 3D and 4D scene editing that leverages large language models (LLMs) to allow arbitrary textual input for user-driven edits. This approach decouples 2D editing from 3D reconstruction, enhancing flexibility and usability, and enables the scheduling of up to 30 visual tools through a fine-tuned LLM. Experimental results indicate significant improvements in scene comprehension and multi-round dialog capabilities, making it a robust tool for generative scene manipulation. The source code is available at https://github.com/Fangkang515/CE3D.
items.judge: The paper discusses interactive 3D scene editing using vision-language models, aligning with generative media.

items.title: Matrix-Game 3.5: Enhancing Real-Time Streaming Interactive World Models with Patch Memory
items.details: Runjia Qian, Zile Wang, Jihai Zhang, Kai Zou et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: Matrix-Game 3.5 introduces a unified geometry-aware memory framework and a static-dynamic disentangled world representation, enabling real-time interactive world generation with improved long-horizon consistency and camera control without adding learnable parameters. The model achieves significant advancements in scene recall and subject identity preservation during extended interactions, demonstrating strong performance across diverse environments such as Unreal simulations and open-world games. Notably, it employs a two-stage progressive real-time distillation process to convert a bidirectional diffusion model into a few-step causal generator, facilitating minute-long interactive generation.
items.judge: Discusses interactive world models for video generation, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: GenFirst: Generation Before Reconstruction for Stable End-to-End Latent Generative Modeling
items.details: Guangting Zheng, Yiyuan Zhang, Tao Yang, Yunpeng Chen et al. · 56 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces GenFirst, a novel approach for direct end-to-end training of latent generative models that mitigates latent collapse by employing a generation-before-reconstruction strategy. This method leverages insights about the importance of entropy in the Kullback-Leibler divergence and the asymmetric learning dynamics between reconstruction and generation, achieving a gFID of 0.97 on ImageNet-256 with CFG and a GenEval score of 0.90 for text-to-image generation. The framework is versatile, extending to shared visual latents for both generation and representation learning, as well as unified text-image generation.
items.judge: The paper addresses generative modeling techniques, specifically in latent generative models.

items.title: ContextBias: Controlled Evaluation of Bias Persistence Under Context Shift in Text-to-Image Models
items.details: Shaghayegh Kolli, Sina Emami, Moreno D'Incà, Pouyan Nejadi et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces ContextBias, a controlled evaluation framework and benchmark (ContextBench) for assessing bias persistence in text-to-image models across varying contexts, featuring 92 roles and 1,656 prompts. Evaluations of four state-of-the-art models on 66,240 images reveal that role-linked visual attributes persist even in semantically unrelated contexts, with a notable increase in cross-role attribute concentration (pooled BI +0.047), underscoring the inadequacy of context-free evaluations in bias assessment. The findings emphasize the importance of incorporating contextual variation in bias benchmarking to better understand stereotypical persistence.
items.judge: The paper evaluates bias in text-to-image models, which is crucial for understanding generative image outputs.

items.title: Keep-or-Drop? Adaptive Tokenizer for Compact Video Representation
items.details: Yeonkyeong Lee, Hyunsung Go, Jongmin Kim, Sewoong Lim et al. · 9 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces KATok, a transformer-based VAE that employs an adaptive token selector for video representation, allowing for data-dependent compression by evaluating token content-richness to discard uninformative tokens. This approach improves reconstruction and generation quality while achieving a state-of-the-art compression ratio by effectively reducing spatio-temporal redundancy. The authors also address potential spatial misalignment issues caused by token dropping through two novel position-prediction strategies, ensuring spatial consistency in the generated video outputs.
items.judge: The paper discusses an adaptive tokenizer for video representation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: SpanCalib-VLM: Calibrated Hallucination Span Detection in Vision-Language Models
items.details: Amanuel Gizachew Abebe, Yasmin Moslem · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: SpanCalib-VLM introduces a hybrid dual-system for detecting hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) by combining a multimodal sequence tagger with a fine-tuned generative VLM. This approach improves span detection accuracy, achieving a Pearson calibration correlation of 0.41 and an overall IoU of 0.39, while maintaining a high clean-response IoU of 0.91 and an overall detection accuracy of 70.7%. The model weights and code are publicly available, facilitating further research and application in the field.
items.judge: The focus on hallucination detection in VLMs is relevant to the evaluation of generative models.

items.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation
items.details: Shaoan Wang, Aocheng Luo, Fei Huang, Jingyi Xu et al. · 24 HF upvotes
items.summary: LightNav-0 introduces a compact generalist embodied navigation model that leverages the spatial intelligence of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) without relying on task-specific components. It achieves state-of-the-art monocular success rates across all 10 public navigation simulation settings and demonstrates zero-shot generalization across various robot embodiments and environments. The model utilizes a unified token interface for diverse navigation tasks, incorporating advanced techniques such as temporally aware visual history compression and reinforcement learning, trained on a corpus of over 2,000 scenes and 4,000 hours of navigation data.
items.judge: The paper discusses VLMs for embodied navigation, which has some relevance to generative models.

items.title: noonghunna/club-3090
items.details: `python` · 2,145★ · 9 stars today
items.summary: The repository "noonghunna/club-3090" provides community-driven configurations for deploying large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA RTX 3090, 4090, and 5090 GPUs, supporting multiple engines such as vLLM, llama.cpp, and ik_llama. It includes optimized setups for Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B, Gemma 4 26B, and Gemma 4 31B models, tailored for both single and dual GPU configurations, enhancing accessibility and performance for researchers working with these high-capacity models.
items.judge: This project provides community recipes for serving LLMs, relevant to inference acceleration.

items.title: Ring Forcing: Towards Precise Long-Term Memory for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
items.details: Bowen Xue, Brandon Y. Feng, Chenguo Lin, Yuchen Lin et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Ring Forcing, an autoregressive video diffusion framework that enhances long-term memory in video generation by addressing object permanence and memory capacity. The proposed ring-structured training strategy allows for effective retrieval from distant history, achieving minutes-long coherence and significantly improving object permanence compared to state-of-the-art methods. The framework also incorporates a compression and timestep composition strategy, extending the effective historical span while maintaining generative diversity.
items.judge: The paper addresses long-term memory in video generation, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: LayerRecall: A State-Conditioned Memory Router for Long-Horizon Consistency in Video Generation
items.details: Yixuan Ding, Jiahao Kong, Wei Huang, Ruijie Quan et al. · 24 HF upvotes
items.summary: LayerRecall introduces a state-conditioned memory router that enhances long-horizon consistency in video generation by selectively retrieving and injecting relevant historical key/value states into specific memory-sensitive layers of the model, while maintaining local attention in others. This approach, combined with Cross-Horizon Prediction Matching (CHPM), allows for improved long-range recovery in video generation tasks, achieving superior performance on MemoBench and MovieBench, and matching backbone performance on VBench-Long across 100 multi-shot evaluation prompts. The method demonstrates effective memory-guided self-correction, ensuring continuity of local attributes without disrupting ongoing motion or scene structure, with minimal inference overhead.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for improving consistency in video generation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Video Generative Models as Geometry Learner
items.details: Haosen Yang, Jifei Song, Zhensong Zhang, Xiatian Zhu et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces GeoNeXt, a novel framework that repurposes pretrained video generative models for geometry estimation, specifically targeting zero-shot monocular depth and surface normal estimation. By formulating the task as next-frame prediction, GeoNeXt achieves superior performance compared to both task-specific and unified generative models, using significantly less training data—outperforming state-of-the-art discriminative methods trained on over 100 times more data across various benchmarks.
items.judge: The paper explores generative models for geometry estimation in video, directly related to generative video models.

items.title: Generative Semantic Scene Completion
items.details: Shi Chen, Weifeng Ge · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Generative Semantic Scene Completion (GSSC), a novel approach that utilizes a discrete-diffusion framework to enhance outdoor LiDAR semantic scene completion (SSC). It achieves a state-of-the-art mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) score of 38.8% on the SemanticKITTI hidden test, surpassing the previous best by 2.1 percentage points without requiring base retraining or test-time adaptation. The method includes three components: paired sparse-dense scene synthesis, semantic-guided generative scene completion, and structured source discrete diffusion, effectively addressing class imbalance and improving completion accuracy.
items.judge: The paper focuses on generative semantic scene completion, which is relevant to 3D generation and evaluation.

items.title: GGSS: Geodesic-Gated Spherical Steering for Inference-Time Debiasing of Generative Vision-Language Models
items.details: Yiqun Sun, Junyu Chen, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence B. Hsieh · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces GGSS (Geodesic-Gated Spherical Steering), a novel method for debiasing generative vision-language models (VLMs) during inference. GGSS effectively identifies and corrects demographic biases by steering visual tokens along geodesic arcs in a counterfactual bias subspace, achieving the lowest average bias across four generative VLMs while maintaining model accuracy within ±0.6 percentage points of the unsteered baseline. The implementation is available at https://github.com/dukesun99/GGSS.
items.judge: The paper proposes a debiasing method for generative vision-language models, relevant to inference and distillation.

items.title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
items.details: Hanyang Wang, Yimo Cai, Weiliang Chen, Jiawei Chi et al. · 38 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces the Code-as-World paradigm, which enhances physical reasoning by representing physical worlds as executable code, allowing for compact and generalizable world representations. This approach employs an agentic discovery loop that iteratively proposes, executes, and refines hypotheses based on multimodal observations, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the QuantiPhy benchmark and outperforming leading proprietary models. The framework provides a scalable method for training vision-language models with quantitative physical reasoning, emphasizing the importance of explicit representations of physical mechanisms.
items.judge: Introduces a paradigm for physical reasoning that could relate to world models but does not focus on generative aspects.

items.title: Act with Intent: Distilling Behavior Intent for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.details: Sangoh Lee, Sangwoo Mo, Wook-Shin Han · 22 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Intention Distillation (INDI), a novel approach that enhances Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by explicitly modeling behavior-level intent during action prediction. By leveraging a frozen teacher VLM to distill intent from multimodal inputs, INDI achieves significant performance improvements, raising success rates on SimplerEnv-Bridge from 64.3% to 84.7% and on RoboCasa Kitchen from 64.1% to 70.3%. Additionally, real-world task success rates increase from 62.0% to 68.7%, with notable gains on longer-horizon tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of intent modeling in action decoders.
items.judge: The paper addresses behavior intent in vision-language-action models, relevant to multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Agentic Artifact Creation: Systems, Evaluation, Principles, and Opportunities
items.details: Tianfu Wang, Zhezheng Hao, Xilin Xia, Lixin Liu et al. · 49 HF upvotes
items.summary: This survey presents a comprehensive analysis of agentic artifact creation, defining it as a stateful process where AI systems construct or revise deliverables based on natural-language prompts, with feedback mechanisms that influence subsequent actions. The authors reviewed 259 works, identifying 230 systems and 29 benchmarks, and highlighted key challenges in artifact construction related to modality, decision coupling, and failure visibility. They propose principles for enhancing accountability and coherence in AI-generated artifacts, emphasizing the importance of explicit commitments and targeted feedback for effective repair and validation.
items.judge: The paper surveys generative models for various content types, relevant to multimodal applications.

items.title: jingyaogong/minimind
items.details: 55,894★ · 472 stars today
items.summary: The repository "jingyaogong/minimind" introduces a method to train a 64M-parameter language model from scratch in just 2 hours, significantly reducing the time required for LLM training. Notable design choices include optimized training algorithms and efficient data handling, which contribute to this rapid training capability. This approach may enhance accessibility for researchers with limited computational resources.
items.judge: This project involves training a large language model, which is relevant to generative models.

items.title: unclecode/crawl4ai

It facilitates the efficient collection of web data for training and fine-tuning LLMs, emphasizing modular design and ease of integration with existing ML workflows. Notably, it supports customizable scraping strategies and adheres to ethical web scraping practices.
items.judge: This project is an open-source web crawler that can be useful for LLM data collection.

items.title: PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored

It integrates abliterated LLMs with ComfyUI in a single installer, eliminating the need for Docker or cloud services, which enhances accessibility and privacy for users.
items.judge: This project includes image and video generation capabilities in a local AI studio.

items.title: vercel-labs/vgpu
items.details: `typescript` · 1,034★ · 203 stars today
items.summary: The repository vgpu by Vercel Labs introduces a modular cross-runtime WebGPU library designed for shaders, 3D scenes, GPU tensors, neural networks, and mathematical visualizations. Its notable design choice is the emphasis on modularity, allowing for flexible integration across different environments, which can enhance performance and usability in generative models. This could significantly streamline the development of GPU-accelerated applications in the fields of image and video generation.
items.judge: The library supports 3D scenes and neural networks, which can be applicable to generative media.

items.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
items.details: Xingyu Shen, Huishuai Zhang, Peng Li, Yinchun Wang et al. · cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel method for enhancing Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) in large language models (LLMs) by incorporating weak-model guidance, which preserves generative diversity and mitigates entropy collapse. By utilizing partial reasoning trajectories from smaller, weaker models, the approach encourages exploration of diverse reasoning paths, leading to significant improvements in reasoning coverage, particularly as the number of reasoning steps ($k$) increases. Empirical results demonstrate that this method consistently outperforms traditional RLVR approaches across various mathematical benchmarks without the need for additional supervised fine-tuning or complex reward structures.
items.judge: The paper discusses reinforcement learning techniques that could be applicable to generative models.

items.title: Retrieval Heads Meet Vision: Uncovering How VLMs Locate and Extract Visual Information
items.details: Chanho Park, Daehyeon Choi, Jihyun Lee, Minhyuk Sung · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Visual Retrieval Heads (VRHs) in vision-language models (VLMs), identifying a small subset of attention heads (1.7-2.6%) that are crucial for grounding text descriptions to specific image regions. By employing a novel head-scoring method, the authors demonstrate that masking the top 20 VRHs can reduce grounding accuracy by up to 80 percentage points, while random head masking has minimal impact. The findings reveal that VRHs generalize across various visual reference tasks and maintain functional specificity, indicating a shared architectural mechanism across different VLMs with similar LLM backbones.
items.judge: This work on vision-language models explores visual retrieval, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
items.details: Siye Wu, Kai Yang, Yuchen Cai, Xin Xu et al. · cs.CL
items.summary: The paper presents a comparative analysis of three fusion paradigms for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR): Merge, Mix RL, and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD). While the average performance across these methods varies by at most 1.4 points, significant domain-level differences are observed, with a maximum gap of 8.6 points on specific benchmarks. The study provides practical guidelines for selecting the appropriate fusion method based on the presence of existing experts, the need for domain-specific gains, and the importance of training efficiency.
items.judge: The paper discusses reinforcement learning techniques that may benefit generative models.

items.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation
items.details: Mayank Singh, Michele Stoppa, Alvise Memo, Rui Yu et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: Luce introduces a novel 3D representation that integrates geometry and physically based rendering (PBR) materials within a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud, utilizing dedicated Gaussian primitives for each modality. This approach, enhanced by a variational autoencoder and a rectified-flow transformer, achieves state-of-the-art performance in single-image-to-3D generation on the Toys4K dataset, improving the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by 28% over the best baseline and enhancing the CLIP image-alignment score to 0.8519. Luce effectively generates relightable and materially accurate 3D assets, maintaining fine details such as text and logos.
items.judge: This work on 3D asset generation is directly relevant to generative media.

items.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models
items.details: Pengfei Zhou, Hexin Wang, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Yixing Ma et al. · 132 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Reinforcement Learning with Human-Engine Verification (RLHEV), a novel post-training paradigm that enhances world models by integrating dense reward signals from game engines with implicit human feedback. This approach addresses the inefficiencies of traditional scaling methods that rely on crawled video and fuzzy proxies like CLIP scores, proposing a more effective framework for generating grounded reward signals and long-horizon trajectory data for reinforcement learning. The authors argue that this method significantly improves the quality of reward signals, facilitating better training outcomes for spatial world models.
items.judge: Discusses scaling world models with a focus on video, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
items.details: Yuandong Pu, Le Zhuo, Sayak Paul, Gabriel Jorge Menezes et al. · 82 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces PAWBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate video generators as stochastic samplers of world dynamics, addressing the gap in current evaluations that focus solely on individual-video plausibility rather than distributional accuracy. The authors formalize probabilistic alignment as a criterion for world models and demonstrate that, across 50 scenarios and eleven existing systems, no model consistently recovers the correct distribution of possible behaviors. They also explore the impact of language prompts, initial noise sampling, and model training on predictive distributions, laying groundwork for advancements in probabilistically aligned world modeling.
items.judge: Addresses probabilistic alignment in world modeling for video generation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: CaRGo-T: Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought improves Multimodal Humor Comprehension
items.details: Abhilash Nandy, Rahul Seetharaman, Aman Bansal, Rounak Saha et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces CaRGo-T (Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought), a novel framework that enhances multimodal humor comprehension by representing causal and contextual relationships in a graph-based structure. This approach improves humor understanding by 1-20% and humor detection by 1-3% over existing reasoning baselines when evaluated across four diverse datasets. The framework's reasoning representations yield more relevant information for predictions, and the implementation is available at https://github.com/abhi1nandy2/CaRGo-T.
items.judge: Explores humor comprehension in VLMs, relevant to multimodal reasoning but not generative media.

items.title: bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
items.details: 12,239★ · 1,870 stars today
items.summary: The repository "bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view" provides a browser-based spy satellite simulator that utilizes real spatial intelligence data to render a photorealistic 3D globe. This tool can be valuable for researchers in generative models by offering a realistic environment for testing and visualizing spatial data applications.
