items.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
items.details: Kechen Liu, Ola Shorinwa · cs.RO cs.AI cs.CV
items.summary: CLAP introduces a novel framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation, enabling zero-shot physical simulation across diverse robot and human embodiments. By reconciling disparate action representations through end-effector poses and language instructions, and employing a curriculum-based learning approach, CLAP achieves performance that approaches or surpasses state-of-the-art single-embodiment models in complex environments like DROID. The framework is open-sourced, providing a comprehensive suite of action-conditioned video world models adaptable to various robot morphologies.
items.judge: This work on cross-embodiment video models is directly related to generative video and world models.

items.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models
items.details: Frederik Berenz · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces Successive Capacity Growth (SCG), a method for dynamically expanding Vision Transformer encoders in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) based on task complexity. SCG starts with a minimal encoder and incrementally adds width or depth, achieving a 20.3% reduction in prediction loss on a 60-dimensional multi-object dynamics task and a 23% improvement on a 2D navigation task compared to fixed models, while maintaining 56 times greater parameter efficiency. This approach allows for adaptive encoder growth, enhancing compute and data efficiency without compromising representation quality.
items.judge: The paper proposes a method for improving world models using Vision Transformer encoders, directly related to generative media.

items.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
items.details: Yuandong Pu, Le Zhuo, Sayak Paul, Gabriel Jorge Menezes et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces PAWBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate video generators as stochastic samplers of world dynamics, addressing the gap in current evaluations that focus solely on individual-video plausibility rather than distributional accuracy. The authors formalize probabilistic alignment as a distribution-level criterion and present PAWEval, a protocol that converts repeated video rollouts into empirical distributions, revealing that none of the eleven tested models consistently match reference probabilities or capture the full range of valid behaviors. This work lays the groundwork for advancing probabilistically aligned world modeling in video generation.
items.judge: This paper addresses probabilistic alignment in video generation models, relevant to world models.

items.title: R2M-Bench: Evaluating Revisit Memory via Relative Consistency in Interactive Video World Models
items.details: Qiwen Gu, Bingjie Gao, Rui Chen, Geng Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces R2M-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate revisit memory in interactive video world models by measuring observable revisit-selective consistency. It introduces two metrics: MemoryGain (MG) and Normalized Memory Ratio (NMR), which help differentiate revisit-specific consistency from generic temporal stability, achieving a Spearman correlation of 0.547 with human judgments across seven models. Notably, DreamX-World-Memo achieved the highest Overall NMR, demonstrating the effectiveness of relative calibration in improving revisit memory evaluation.
items.judge: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating memory consistency in interactive video world models.

items.title: Sidecar: Training-Free Semantic Reuse for Character-Consistent Free-form Visual Storytelling
items.details: Sibo Dong, Sarah Adel Bargal · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Sidecar, a training-free semantic augmentation module designed to enhance character consistency in free-form visual storytelling by preserving and injecting missing identity-related semantics into later prompt embeddings. Evaluated on FreeStoryBench, Sidecar demonstrates significant improvements in prompt-image alignment and character consistency across various SDXL- and FLUX-based models, all while maintaining negligible computational overhead. This approach allows for more coherent narrative generation without requiring modifications to existing diffusion model architectures.
items.judge: The paper addresses character consistency in visual storytelling, linking to image generation and editing.

items.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models
items.details: Xiaoxiao Lu, Yunlong Dong, Jiahao Shi, Ye Yuan · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces the Latent Evolution Operator Network (LEON), which enhances World Action Models (WAMs) by modeling latent state transitions through context-modulated operator-based propagation and additive forcing, rather than relying solely on Transformer-based predictors. LEON demonstrates improved closed-loop performance and robustness in two WAM formulations, establishing a significant architectural advancement in latent transition realization that effectively integrates predictive representation with policy coupling. The approach is validated through controlled dynamical systems, highlighting the importance of operator structure in latent evolution.
items.judge: The paper discusses world action models, which are relevant to world models in generative contexts.

items.title: Vision-centric generative AI models: A software-hardware perspective
items.details: Eleni Tselepi, Cristian Sestito, Shady Agwa, Themis Prodromakis · cs.CV cs.AR
items.summary: The paper presents a software-hardware co-design approach for vision-centric generative AI models, emphasizing the need for models that are optimized for edge applications with strict hardware constraints. It quantifies the parameter cost and energy efficiency of various generative models across different accelerator platforms, advocating for a design strategy that aligns model capabilities with specific deployment environments to enhance sustainability and accessibility. The authors map four generative model families to seven real-world application domains, highlighting the importance of integrating hardware considerations early in the development process.
items.judge: The paper discusses vision generative AI models and their applications, aligning with multimodal generation.

items.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
items.details: Kairong Luo, Jiarui Cui, Yaorui Yin, Shengqi Chen et al. · cs.CL cs.LG
items.summary: The paper presents Puro-2B, an open-source pretraining recipe for language models that significantly reduces training costs, achieving performance comparable to Qwen2.5-1.5B for under $6.9K using consumer-grade RTX 5090 GPUs. Key innovations include low-precision training, hyperball optimization, and a structured data curriculum, which collectively enable training on up to 1.4 trillion tokens. The authors also introduce a Puro Cost Scaling Law that suggests a budget of approximately $4.4K can achieve similar performance to Qwen2-1.5B, and they provide the complete training pipeline, including data and model weights, under Apache 2.0.
items.judge: This paper discusses an open-source pretraining recipe for LLMs, relevant to the generative media field.

items.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming
items.details: Zhiyuan Li, Chi-Man Pun, Peng-Tao Jiang, Bo Li et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: EditaLive introduces a novel framework for real-time character video editing in live streaming, addressing the limitations of conventional methods that struggle with human-centric content. By leveraging a pretrained image animation model and implementing a two-step sampler with aligned self-rollout distillation, EditaLive achieves state-of-the-art editing performance while maintaining facial expression fidelity and enabling low-latency inference. The framework significantly improves real-time interaction capabilities, making it suitable for live streaming applications.
items.judge: The proposed framework for real-time video editing in live streaming is highly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Thinking on Shots: Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing with Agentic Reasoning
items.details: Chenyang Wu, Fuchen Long, Binyuan Huang, Xinlong Sun et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces the Multi-Instruction Multi-Shot Long-Video Editing (MMLVE) task, addressing the challenges of editing long videos with multiple instructions by proposing an agentic editing framework that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs). This approach significantly improves cross-shot editing consistency and reduces editing hallucinations, outperforming existing closed-source state-of-the-art methods like Seedance 2.0. The authors also present MMLVE-Bench, a dataset designed to evaluate the new task, featuring complex spatiotemporal dynamics and high-density heterogeneous instructions.
items.judge: Addresses challenges in long-video editing, contributing to generative video models.

items.title: Magpie: Real-Time World Renderer for Interactive Games
items.details: Xiaoyu Zhan, Xinyu Wang, Xiaohong Zhang, Huanjie Zhu et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: Magpie introduces a novel real-time generative world-rendering system for interactive games, effectively decoupling gameplay execution from visual generation. This architecture allows designers to define scenes and rules within a game engine while an independent Render Server generates visuals from white-box frames, enhancing the flexibility and efficiency of game prototyping by reducing reliance on complete visual assets. The system aims to improve the development cycle by enabling stable and reproducible gameplay alongside high-quality visual output.
items.judge: The paper presents a real-time world renderer for interactive games, closely related to 3D generation and video models.

items.title: Procedura: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control
items.details: Youtian Lin, Yikang Yang, Zhanpeng Hu, Mengqi Zhou et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: Procedura introduces a novel framework for 3D modeling that leverages LLMs to generate parametric programs representing objects as procedural assemblies, significantly improving the quality and editability of generated 3D models. It outperforms existing native 3D generators and prior 3D-code agents on the P3D-Bench and MechBench-36 benchmarks, achieving sharper edges and producing outputs that are structured and editable. The framework employs a decoupled vision critic for iterative refinement, ensuring that each part meets connectivity and compatibility checks before final assembly.
items.judge: Introduces a novel framework for 3D modeling that enhances user control over generated objects.

items.title: Aphanta: Diagnosing Task-Aligned Image-Edited Intermediates for Multimodal Reasoning
items.details: Hengyuan Xu, Wei Cheng, Yumeng Ji, Xuanyang Zhang et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: Aphanta introduces a diagnostic framework for evaluating the effectiveness of image editors in multimodal large language model (MLLM) pipelines, focusing on task-aligned visual intermediates. The framework assesses the utility of image transformations across 20 tasks, revealing that performance gains are highly task-dependent, with the Qwen pipeline achieving a mean task score improvement from 0.343 to 0.445 (+10.2 points; +29.7% relative). This work positions image editing as a specialized tool for visual reasoning rather than a universal solution, providing a reusable protocol for assessing task-representation alignment and editor effectiveness.
items.judge: Presents a framework for multimodal reasoning with image editing, linking to generative tasks.

items.title: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
items.details: Yuncheng Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Weijia Li · 35 HF upvotes
items.summary: GameWAM introduces the first World-Action Model (WAM) designed for native closed-loop gameplay and GUI control in video games, improving the generation of future visual observations and executable actions through parallel generative processes. It employs block-causal conditioning and flow matching, achieving competitive task success with fewer executed actions compared to existing agents. The model also addresses heterogeneous control by predicting gameplay modes at each action step and incorporates long-horizon interaction strategies, revealing insights into action source sensitivity through Low-Frequency Action Source Imprinting (LASI).
items.judge: Explores world-action models in video games, relevant to video generation and modeling.

items.title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
items.details: Jiaming Zhou, Qihang Zhang, Gangwei Xu, Cunxin Fan et al. · 16 HF upvotes
items.summary: Zero-WAM introduces a novel causal video-action model that enables zero-shot cross-task generalization in robotic manipulation by leveraging human videos as task specifications. It achieves a 47.0% average success rate on seven unseen tasks in the RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, marking a significant improvement of 29.5 percentage points over existing video-action baselines. The approach includes an innovative automatic pipeline for generating a dataset of 74.2K human-robot in-context learning pairs and employs an in-context future chunk prediction objective to enhance task learning from video prompts.
items.judge: The paper discusses a novel approach to task generalization in robotic manipulation, which relates to world models.

items.title: Self-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models without Teacher
items.details: Shiyi Zhang, Mushui Liu, Yunze Tong, Wanggui He et al. · 55 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Self-OPD, a novel teacher-free on-policy distillation framework for flow matching models that eliminates the need for task-specific teacher models, thereby reducing computational costs and mitigating compounding errors from distribution discrepancies. By leveraging the student's own self-exploration for step-wise supervision and optimizing the velocity field with a pull-push objective based on normalized advantages, Self-OPD demonstrates superior performance on single and mixed reward benchmarks compared to existing reinforcement learning and OPD methods.
items.judge: The paper addresses on-policy distillation techniques, which can be relevant for generative media models.

items.title: huggingface/transformers
items.details: `python` · 164,564★ · 50 stars today
items.summary: The Hugging Face Transformers library provides a comprehensive framework for defining and implementing state-of-the-art models across text, vision, audio, and multimodal domains, facilitating both training and inference. Notable design choices include a modular architecture that supports various model types and tasks, extensive pre-trained model availability, and integration with popular deep learning frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow. This repository is crucial for researchers looking to leverage cutting-edge generative models in their work.
items.judge: This framework supports multimodal models, including those for generative tasks.

items.title: RefVideo-6M: A Reliable Reference-Based Dataset for Instructional Video Editing
items.details: Bojia Zi, Xiaoyan Yang, Yu Zhou, Ruijie Sun et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces RefVideo-6M, a large-scale reference-guided dataset for instructional video editing, comprising 5 million video and 1 million image editing samples. It addresses limitations of existing datasets by using artifact-free real videos as targets and providing around 6 million visual references, which enhances the reliability of supervision and allows for fine-grained visual correspondence learning. The dataset has been shown to significantly improve the performance of the reference-guided video editing model, Ref-MoT, in terms of visual quality, controllability, and reference consistency compared to prior datasets.
items.judge: Presents a dataset for instructional video editing, directly relevant to video generation.

items.title: Uncertainty-Guided Latent Diffusion Models for Faithful Super Resolution
items.details: Ren Wang, Yung-Yu Chuang · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces UGDiff, a novel diffusion guidance paradigm that enhances the perception-distortion balance in single-image super-resolution (SR) by estimating reconstruction uncertainty of latent features. This method selectively restores high-frequency details in high-uncertainty regions while preserving fidelity elsewhere, reducing reliance on high-fidelity images during sampling. Experimental results show that UGDiff outperforms existing state-of-the-art diffusion-based SR methods, improving fidelity without compromising perceptual quality.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel approach to super-resolution using diffusion models, relevant to generative image tasks.

items.title: 4DGS-WAM: Bridging Past and Future with an Object-Centric World Action Model based on 4D Gaussian Splatting
items.details: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces 4DGS-WAM, an object-centric world action model that enhances traditional 2D WAMs by utilizing a 4D Gaussian Splatting representation to separately model dynamic objects and static backgrounds. This approach allows for the reuse of previously observed static content in future predictions, significantly improving efficiency in short-horizon predictions and past reconstructions on the KITTI-MOT dataset. The model's design emphasizes the reduction of redundant processing by focusing on dynamic object evolution while maintaining a persistent 4D representation.
items.judge: This work introduces a 4D Gaussian Splatting model for world action modeling, relevant to generative 3D media.

items.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
items.details: Yiwen Chen, Guosheng Lin, Chi Zhang · cs.CV cs.AI cs.CL
items.summary: The Code World Model introduces a novel framework that integrates language models' reasoning and coding capabilities with video models' generative priors, enabling a coding agent to maintain persistent world states and facilitate coherent evolution through executable code. This approach utilizes a proxy representation to connect executable states with visual generation, allowing for high-fidelity visual observations while adhering to spatiotemporal constraints. The framework shows promise in enhancing open-ended world models by effectively combining rule-consistent evolution with rich visual dynamics, as demonstrated through fine-tuning on aligned gameplay data.
items.judge: Introduces a framework for world models that separates evolution from visual reality, relevant to generative video and world modeling.

items.title: TAU-Agent: An Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Traffic Anomaly Understanding
items.details: Yuqiang Lin, Yan Shi, Sam Lockyer, Harish Tayyar Madabushi et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: TAU-Agent introduces a novel retrieval-augmented framework for Traffic Anomaly Understanding, leveraging a central retrieval agent to integrate a Video Captioning Tool and an Open-Vocabulary Tracking Tool for enhanced evidence selection. This approach improves the model's ability to detect and reason about anomalies in transportation videos, achieving competitive scores of 0.6779, 0.3998, and 67.9275 on various benchmarks from the AI City Challenge 2026. The implementation is available in an open-source repository at GitHub.
items.judge: Proposes a framework for understanding traffic anomalies in videos.

items.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
items.details: Junxiang Xu, Ruisi Wang, Fanyi Pu, Maijunxian Wang et al. · cs.CV cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: VBVR-Pro introduces a scalable and verifiable framework for native visual reasoning, featuring 300 procedurally generated tasks that enhance model training and evaluation. It provides deterministic, task-specific reward scorers that align closely with human judgments, improving reinforcement learning outcomes across visual reasoning benchmarks. The framework also facilitates controlled studies of over 30 generative modalities, revealing that video generation excels in tasks requiring spatiotemporal tracking, while interleaved generation offers a more efficient alternative. All data, models, scorers, and code are publicly available.
items.judge: Introduces a testbed for visual reasoning, relevant to generative media.

items.title: A Visual Dependence-Aware Framework for Multimodal Unsupervised Continual Post-Training
items.details: Kaichen Li, Zhilin Zhu, Jianhao Huang, Zhengqin Lai et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces a Visual Dependence-Aware (VDA) framework for Multimodal Unsupervised Continual Post-Training (MU-CPT), addressing the challenge of cross-modal catastrophic forgetting in deployed MLLMs. By employing Visually Constrained Optimal Transport (VC-OT) and Visually Modulated Adaptation (VMA), the framework effectively maintains stability in old tasks while enhancing adaptability to new tasks, significantly improving performance in continual learning scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in mitigating visual dependence-related issues, although specific quantitative improvements are not detailed in the abstract.
items.judge: Explores continual post-training for multimodal models, applicable to generative media.

items.title: PlanSightRAG: A Visual-First Multimodal RAG for Automating Question Answering and Compliance Checking for Civil Standard Plans
items.details: Nabaraj Subedi, Shuvo Dip Datta, Ahmed Abdelaty, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar · cs.IR cs.CL cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces PlanSightRAG, a Visual-First Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework that automates question answering and compliance checking for civil standard plans by directly indexing and reasoning over plan imagery. It achieves a Recall@5 of 91.47% in zero-shot retrieval and demonstrates 100% verdict accuracy on synthetic compliance drawings when provided with pre-resolved rule thresholds, significantly outperforming a non-VLM OCR baseline which achieves 76.4%. The framework incorporates a ColNomic-3B multi-vector retrieval system and an agentic Planner-Retriever-Auditor-Synthesizer, enhancing the interpretation of complex visual data in civil engineering contexts.
items.judge: Presents a multimodal framework for compliance checking, relevant to visual reasoning.

items.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
items.details: Nan Duan, Haoyang Huang, Weiyang Jin, Haoran Li et al. · 19 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces JoyAI-Echo-1.5, a unified audio-visual generation system that enhances long-form narrative and interactive world generation through two specialized variants. The long-video variant employs a composable cross-shot memory for improved character consistency and voice identity, while the world-model variant utilizes a geometry-aware conditioning pathway for flexible navigation and interaction. JoyAI-Echo-1.5 outperforms existing long-video models in cross-shot consistency, visual quality, text alignment, and speech fidelity, achieving a top score of 81.7 on WBench and leading metrics on SANA-WM-Bench.
items.judge: The paper presents a system for long-horizon audio-visual generation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Stream4D: 4D-Consistency for Streaming Autoregressive Diffusion Video Models
items.details: Yuanhao Ban, Jiaqi Feng, Hengguang Zhou, Xiaohuan Pei et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: Stream4D introduces a novel approach to autoregressive diffusion video models by implementing a feed-forward 4D reconstruction reward that captures scene dynamics, addressing the limitations of static critics that lead to geometric drift and unnatural motion. This method enhances 4D reconstruction quality and preserves coherent motion, resulting in improved human-aligned preference across various video generation backbones and horizons. The integration of a motion prior further refines motion magnitude and quality, reducing jitter and non-rigid artifacts.
items.judge: Introduces a method for improving long-horizon video generation, directly related to video generation models.

items.title: VGI-BENCH: Probing Visual Intelligence in Video Generation Models
items.details: Xuan He, Cong Wei, Yuhao Cheng, Linrui Ma et al. · 118 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces VGI-bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the visual reasoning capabilities of video generation models through 27 tasks and 810 instances, organized by a two-level taxonomy. The evaluation reveals that even the best-performing model, Seedance 2.0, achieves only 51.0% accuracy, highlighting significant limitations in current generative systems' reasoning abilities. The authors also analyze failure modes and sensitivity to input conditions, suggesting that improvements in self-correction mechanisms are necessary for future model development.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating video generation models, aligning with generative media.

items.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios
items.details: Hongbo Liu, Peixian Chen, Sihan Liu, Peiyuan Zhang et al. · 14 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Video-IFBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the instruction-following capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in video understanding scenarios. It features a comprehensive instruction taxonomy with four templates and 32 task types, addressing the gap in existing benchmarks that primarily focus on task accuracy rather than adherence to user-specified constraints. The authors demonstrate that current MLLMs struggle with complex instructions, particularly those involving multiple constraints, highlighting the need for improved models in this area.
items.judge: This work evaluates instruction following in multimodal LLMs for video understanding, relevant to generative media.

items.title: FIRM-Video: Check Before You Score for Reliable Text-to-Video Reward Modeling
items.details: Peiyuan Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Hongbo Liu, Xiaoxing Hu et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: FIRM-Video introduces a novel checklist-driven framework for text-to-video reward modeling that enhances evaluation accuracy while maintaining inference efficiency. By employing a check-before-score principle, it constructs dimension-specific checklists that verify criteria against temporal visual evidence, resulting in a dataset of 88,044 instances and a benchmark with 750 human annotations. The Qwen3-VL-based model achieves the lowest mean absolute error on the benchmark and outperforms other models in multiple evaluation metrics, demonstrating significant improvements in reward modeling for text-to-video tasks.
items.judge: The paper discusses a framework for reliable text-to-video reward modeling, relevant to video generation.

items.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation
items.details: Zihao Wu, Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Huizhong Song et al. · 103 HF upvotes
items.summary: WarpSAC introduces a regime-aware approach to off-policy reinforcement learning, significantly improving performance by adapting stabilizers to data availability. It achieves a 4.5% increase in normalized score-step AUC over FlashSAC in CPU-scale environments and a 23.1% improvement in GPU-parallel settings. Notably, WarpSAC increases the success rate on the UnitreeG1TransportBox-v1 task from 19.8% to 96.4% and enhances sim-to-real deployment speed by 36.4%.
items.judge: Explores reinforcement learning techniques that could be applicable to generative media inference.

items.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.details: Shulin Tian, Minglun Li, Yuhao Dong, Hao Ding et al. · 12 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Visual Rubrics-Based Reinforcement Learning (V-Rubrics), which enhances vision-language models by addressing credit-assignment failures in multimodal post-training. By decomposing responses into atomic propositions and scoring them based on Visual Faithfulness, Reasoning Consistency, and Instruction Following, V-Rubrics provides structured partial credit and improves model performance on knowledge-oriented and visually grounded reasoning benchmarks, achieving significant gains over traditional fine-tuning methods. The approach is validated using a newly constructed dataset, V-Rubrics 50K, comprising over 50,000 examples from various visually grounded sources.
items.judge: Addresses visual grounding in vision-language models, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: D^3-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
items.details: Zechen Sun, Zhiwei Zhang, Fei Zhao, Juntao Li et al. · 21 HF upvotes
items.summary: D^3-MOPD introduces an adaptive dynamic domain scheduling mechanism for multi-teacher on-policy distillation, significantly improving performance by closing 97% of the student-to-teacher performance gap, compared to 63% with traditional methods. This approach utilizes an off-process watcher to dynamically adjust domain sampling ratios based on real-time KL divergence trajectories, achieving peak performance with approximately three times fewer rollout steps. The method scales effectively with the number of domains, leveraging diverse convergence patterns to enhance training efficiency.
items.judge: The paper addresses multi-teacher distillation, which has potential applications in generative media.

items.title: andrewyng/aisuite
items.details: `python` · 16,179★ · 12 stars today
items.summary: The repository "andrewyng/aisuite" provides a unified interface for interacting with multiple generative AI providers, streamlining the integration process for developers. This design choice enhances usability by allowing seamless access to various models without the need for extensive modifications to existing codebases. The project aims to simplify the workflow for researchers and practitioners in the generative AI space.
items.judge: This item provides a unified interface to generative AI providers, relevant to multimodal applications.

items.title: TurboT2VA: Fast Large-Scale Text-to-Video-Audio Generation via Score-Regularized Consistency Distillation
items.details: Xiaoda Yang, Yuxiang Liu, Kaiwen Zheng, Yuan Liu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: TurboT2VA introduces a novel distillation and inference framework for a 19B-parameter joint text-to-video-audio model, achieving a 20.1× speedup in generator latency from 50.52s to 2.51s at a resolution of 512×768, while maintaining high visual quality and audio fidelity. The framework employs a progressive curriculum for consistency training and an architecture-aware inference stack that optimizes performance through techniques like modality-aware sparse attention. At a higher resolution of 1024×1792, the complete stack further reduces latency from 318.74s to 5.83s, resulting in a 54.67× speedup.
items.judge: This work presents a distillation framework for efficient text-to-video-audio generation, a key area in generative media.

items.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
items.details: Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic et al. · cs.CV cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: LAION-BVD introduces a large-scale open video dataset comprising 80 million videos totaling 10 million hours, sourced from 1.3 billion URLs via CommonCrawl, aimed at enhancing multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities. The dataset employs content-aware scene detection for clip extraction and synthetic caption generation, leading to competitive performance improvements on video-text and audio-text benchmarks, particularly as model scale increases. Additionally, the dataset's unique scene-changing frames provide a distinct visual distribution for image-text retrieval tasks, outperforming standard web image corpora.
items.judge: It presents a large-scale open video dataset designed for multimodal pre-training.

items.title: LeFlow: Generative Latent Flow Planning for World Models
items.details: Hsiang-Wei Huang, Jianxu Shangguan, Junbin Lu, Jenq-Neng Hwang · cs.CV
items.summary: LeFlow introduces a novel approach to action planning in latent world models by learning a reusable latent trajectory prior, which significantly reduces planning time by an order of magnitude compared to traditional iterative optimization methods. This method employs a rectified-flow model for conditional latent trajectory generation and an inverse dynamics decoder for action chunking, achieving improved success rates across four major goal-conditioned pixel-control benchmarks. The work emphasizes the potential for latent world models to facilitate not only prediction but also efficient, reusable planning.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel approach to generative latent flow planning in world models.

items.title: Game2World Engine: Unlocking In-the-Wild Gameplay Videos for World Model Training
items.details: Wenxuan Shen, Dongna Jin, Dongping Chen · cs.CV
items.summary: The Game2World Engine introduces a novel framework for extracting and removing gameplay UI elements from in-the-wild video game footage, significantly enhancing the quality of training data for world models. The framework includes GameCleaner, a mask-free model that improves UI removal accuracy, achieving an average AAR of 95.36 on synthetic videos—57.3% better than the best mask-based method—and a real-world AAR of 80.05 with 99.8% background preservation. This approach enables the creation of the Game2World dataset, which contains 96K synthetic paired videos and 1,079 real gameplay clips, facilitating improved training for video world models with a 6.83% increase in VideoReward performance.
items.judge: The paper discusses a framework for training world models using gameplay videos, directly linking to generative video models.

items.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
items.details: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo et al. · cs.RO cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces WorldEcho, a diagnostic framework for evaluating action-conditioned world models, revealing that they perform well with expert actions but falter with off-expert trajectories, often ignoring commands or generating invalid outputs. To address these shortcomings, the authors propose WorldSync, which enhances action following through improved distributional coverage, representational grounding, and intervention-effect alignment, resulting in significant improvements on RoboTwin benchmarks and real-robot tasks, leading to higher success rates in policy learning.
items.judge: The paper addresses the effectiveness of action-conditioned world models, relevant to generative video and simulation.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models
items.details: Wei Zhou, Xiongwei Zhu, Lingdong Kong, Bo Chen et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces DiffusionOPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework for diffusion models that effectively converts image-level reward guidance into explicit targets for clean-output predictions. This method achieves up to a 44.0% performance improvement over the strongest competing method across 20 reward-matched settings, while also reducing training GPU hours by 40% on SD 3.5-M and 63% on Z-Image-Turbo. The framework allows for separate measurement of target construction and realization, enhancing the efficiency and diagnosability of alignment in diffusion models.
items.judge: The paper discusses self-distillation in diffusion models, relevant to generative media.

items.title: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Longitudinal Patient Representation and Scalable Insight Generation in Oncology
items.details: Eugene Vorontsov, Yi Kan Wang, Alican Bozkurt, Adam Casson et al. · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces the oFM, a multimodal foundation model designed for longitudinal patient representation in oncology, trained on a dataset of 1.67 million cancer patients. It integrates clinical trajectories with molecular data and pathology images, achieving a significant improvement in prognostic benchmarks, with an AUC for overall survival increasing from 0.563 to 0.774. Additionally, the oFM embeddings demonstrated a three-fold increase in treatment-benefit AUTOC across 11 cohorts, enhancing prognostic discrimination and enabling mechanism discovery through an evidence-grounded temporal graph.
items.judge: The paper presents a multimodal foundation model for oncology, which has implications for multimodal generation.

items.title: Image Difference Quantification Using Autoencoder-Based Latent Representations
items.details: Manish Sharma, Timothy Yim, Clifton Forlines · cs.CV
items.summary: This paper introduces a convolutional autoencoder-based framework for quantifying image differences using cosine similarity in latent space, offering a semantically grounded alternative to traditional pixel-based metrics like MSE and SSIM. The method demonstrates robust differentiation between visually distinct images, achieving 98.4% of dog-cat image pairs with similarity scores below 0.5, and shows a positive correlation with human Mean Opinion Scores on the TID2013 dataset. This approach enhances perceptual quality assessment and content-based retrieval by leveraging high-level semantic information encoded in compact embeddings.
items.judge: The paper proposes a method for quantifying image differences using autoencoders, relevant to image generation.

items.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs
items.details: Yunheng Li, Guohong Mu, Hao Li, Shengsheng Qian et al. · 80 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces OraRL, a novel reinforcement learning method that enhances the sample efficiency and scalability of post-training for video multimodal large language models (MLLMs). By leveraging annotations as oracle rollouts and employing a decoupled advantage estimator, OraRL achieves significant performance improvements, raising temporal mIoU from 62.5 to 66.0 and reducing decoding time from 4,780 ms to 130 ms for the Video-ORA-9B model, while requiring only 2.2x the step time of supervised fine-tuning (SFT). This method effectively addresses the challenge of advantage inversion and scales efficiently with model size and data.
items.judge: The paper addresses reinforcement learning for video multimodal large language models, relevant to generative video.

items.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
items.details: Junjie Zhou, Ke Mei, Lei Li, Tianyi Wang et al. · 54 HF upvotes
items.summary: WeMM-Embedding introduces a family of universal multimodal embedding models (2B, 4B, and 9B parameters) that effectively integrate text, images, videos, and visual documents into a shared representation space. The 2B variant surpasses the previous 8B open-source baseline on the MMEB-v2 benchmark, while the 9B variant achieves a new state-of-the-art score of 80.6. The models are trained in a two-stage process involving large-scale multimodal alignment and refinement with curated data, and they have been successfully deployed in various WeChat applications, demonstrating significant performance improvements across multiple tasks.
items.judge: The report presents a multimodal embedding model that supports various content types, relevant to generative media.

items.title: GigaBrain-0.7: Scaling Embodied Foundation Models to Emergent Capabilities with a Three-System Architecture
items.details: GigaBrain Team, Angen Ye, Axiang Sun, Can Jin et al. · 87 HF upvotes
items.summary: GigaBrain-0.7 introduces a three-system architecture that enhances generalization across diverse robot embodiments by unifying understanding, prediction, and action. It scales pretraining to over 37,000 hours of heterogeneous data and employs one-stage alignment training, resulting in significant improvements in zero-shot capabilities, language-conditioned instruction following, and task success rates compared to previous models. The model demonstrates strong adaptability in both home and industrial scenarios, with all training code and pretrained weights to be released.
items.judge: The paper discusses embodied foundation models, relevant to multi-modal generative capabilities.

items.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
items.details: Yibo Peng, Long Lian, David Wagner, Sizhe Chen · 36 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD), a novel approach to mitigate adaptive prompt injections in LLMs by providing token-level feedback during defensive fine-tuning. This method significantly reduces the attack success rate (ASR) from 94.0% with the previous state-of-the-art (Meta-SecAlign) to 9.0% for the Qwen3.6-27B model against PISmith adaptive prompt injections, demonstrating improved robustness even in unseen domains with a 4.7% ASR in agentic tool calling. The code and model are accessible via GitHub and Hugging Face.
items.judge: The paper addresses prompt injection threats in AI agents, relevant to LLMs and training.

items.title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models
items.details: Xiang Li, Yupeng Zheng, Songen Gu, Huailiang Ma et al. · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces LAWA, a novel world action model architecture that utilizes compact latent actions to represent future intentions, significantly improving efficiency in future imagination during robot control. LAWA achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 65.6% and 80.8% in few-shot and full data settings, respectively, surpassing the Fast-WAM baseline by 9.6 and 4.5 points while reducing inference latency by 42.9%. This approach retains the benefits of future imagination without the need for generating future observations, demonstrating enhanced performance and generalization in both few-shot and zero-shot scenarios.
items.judge: The paper introduces a world action model architecture relevant to future observation generation.

items.title: TorchMorph: CUDA-accelerated Morphological Transforms
items.details: Kai Zhao · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: TorchMorph is a new PyTorch extension that provides 22 CUDA-accelerated morphological transform operators, significantly improving performance for shape and mask processing in GPU training loops. It achieves up to 1,100x throughput over the CPU-based scipy.ndimage for greyscale morphology and 350x for exact Euclidean distance transforms, while maintaining high accuracy with float-valued operations within 1.8e-6 absolute error. The API is designed to closely mirror scipy.ndimage, facilitating easy integration into existing pipelines.
items.judge: The paper discusses CUDA-accelerated morphological transforms, which can enhance inference for generative tasks.

items.title: ai-dynamo/aiperf

It provides standardized metrics for assessing model efficiency and throughput, enabling researchers to compare different implementations and optimize their deployment strategies. The tool's modular design allows for easy integration with existing workflows and supports multiple model types.
