items.title: Z.ai confirms Ox Alpha is a new GLM-series model and will release its weights
items.details: 357 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49446422)
items.summary: Z.ai has announced the Ox Alpha, a new model in its GLM-series, designed to compete with existing generative models like DeepSeek. The model reportedly improves upon previous iterations in terms of efficiency and output quality, although specific performance metrics have not been disclosed. Z.ai plans to release the model's weights, facilitating further research and development in the open-source community.
items.judge: This confirms the release of a new GLM-series model, relevant to open-source LLMs.

items.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: A New Architecture, Towards Ultimate Cost-Efficiency
items.details: 330 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49448210)
items.summary: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next introduces a novel architecture aimed at enhancing cost-efficiency in generative models, achieving a 30% reduction in computational costs while maintaining performance levels comparable to existing state-of-the-art models. The design emphasizes modular components and optimized training protocols, allowing for faster convergence and lower resource requirements. This advancement is particularly relevant for researchers focused on scaling generative image and video models in resource-constrained environments.
items.judge: This discusses a new architecture for cost-efficiency, relevant to LLMs.

items.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
items.details: Zhifei Chen, Luozhou Wang, Guibao Shen, Dongyu Yan et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: ReWorld introduces an interactive world model that effectively balances short-horizon control and long-horizon memory by separating these aspects during training and constraining them at inference. It employs mixed per-head attention with global heads for historical context and a bounded KV cache for efficient memory retrieval, achieving superior performance with a rotation error of $11.95^\circ$ and enhanced camera-motion consistency across various environments. The model demonstrates its capability by regenerating starting views in minute-long rollouts, outperforming six recent interactive world models in both control fidelity and generation quality.
items.judge: This work on an interactive world model with long-horizon memory is relevant to generative video and world modeling.

items.title: FixAnything: 3D-Consistent Rendering Refinement via Video Generative Priors
items.details: Khiem Vuong, Deva Ramanan, Srinivasa Narasimhan · cs.CV
items.summary: FixAnything introduces a unified model for refining rendering artifacts across various 3D representations, leveraging a pretrained video generative model with minimal modifications. It employs a binary mask to guide the preservation of clean pixels and utilizes camera pose accuracy as a reward signal for direct preference optimization, resulting in consistent improvements in rendering quality across four distinct 3D formats. This approach allows for the replacement of multiple specialized refinement pipelines with a single, adaptable framework, facilitating the integration of future video models without extensive architectural changes.
items.judge: This work on 3D-consistent rendering refinement using video generative priors is highly relevant to generative image and video models.

items.title: Correcting a learned physical invariant improves world-model rollouts
items.details: Richard Bao · cs.AI
items.summary: The paper presents a method for correcting learned physical invariants in world models, demonstrating that projecting latent states back toward their initial levels significantly reduces rollout error across three conservative models. This approach reveals that while world models can learn physical constraints from visual data, they may still violate these constraints during forward predictions, highlighting a critical failure mode in generative modeling. The findings suggest that incorporating invariant corrections can enhance the reliability of world model rollouts.
items.judge: The paper investigates world models and their predictive capabilities in video generation.

items.title: Photorealistic Novel View Synthesis of Human Faces using Next-Scale Transformers
items.details: Federico Stella, Fei Jiang, Zhongshi Jiang, Zohar Barzelay et al. · cs.CV cs.LG
items.summary: The paper presents a novel approach to photorealistic novel view synthesis of human faces using a next-scale autoregressive model, achieving improved image resolutions and multi-view outputs without the need for 2D pre-training. This method allows for stronger cross-view consistency and faster convergence with smaller, more realistic training datasets, resulting in enhanced perceptual fidelity and coherence across views. The authors also integrate their model with a transformer-based framework for pixel-aligned 3D Gaussian lifting, producing accurate 3D representations of human faces.
items.judge: Addresses photorealistic view synthesis of human faces, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
items.details: Nan Duan, Haoyang Huang, Weiyang Jin, Haoran Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces JoyAI-Echo-1.5, a unified audio-visual generation system that significantly enhances long-form narrative and interactive world generation. It features a long-video variant with a composable cross-shot memory for maintaining character consistency and a world-model variant that translates navigation inputs into calibrated 6-DoF trajectories, achieving a top score of 81.7 on WBench. The model employs a causal few-step generator with advanced training techniques, resulting in improved cross-shot consistency, visual quality, text alignment, and speech fidelity compared to existing baselines.
items.judge: The paper presents a unified audio-visual generation system for long-form narratives, aligning with generative video models.

items.title: Controllable blind deblurring with diffusion models
items.details: Imane Si Salah, Emile Cribelier, Thomas Veit, Wolf Hauser et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces SuperSharpen, a diffusion-based method for controllable blind deblurring that allows explicit adjustment of restoration strength through a blur measure. By comparing a ControlNet-style adapter with full finetuning of the diffusion model, the authors demonstrate that finetuning yields higher fidelity and fewer hallucinations, achieving improved perceptual quality on both synthetic and real-world blurred images. This approach addresses the challenge of generating photo-realistic details in the presence of unknown isotropic blur.
items.judge: The paper discusses controllable blind deblurring using diffusion models, relevant to generative image editing.

items.title: ChebBooster: A Training-Free Approach for Efficient Diffusion Transformer Inference via Chebyshev-Inspired Extrapolation
items.details: Chengjie Lu, Tianchi Deng, Zhengqi He, Chengwen Luo et al. · cs.LG cs.AI
items.summary: ChebBooster introduces a training-free extrapolation framework for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) that leverages Chebyshev polynomial theory to enhance inference efficiency and stability. By employing a Barycentric formulation, it achieves up to 3.68× latency speedup and 5.12× reduction in FLOPs during the sampling process, significantly improving visual quality and outperforming existing training-free methods across multiple DiT models. The approach decouples the extrapolation into an offline weight precomputation phase and a lightweight online application stage, optimizing computational resources during inference.
items.judge: Proposes an efficient inference method for diffusion transformers, relevant for generative image models.

items.title: Investigating Relational Reasoning in VLMs
items.details: Adhithya Laxman Ravi Shankar Geetha, Aulia Kharis Rakhmasari, Haleema Ramzan, Xander Yap · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper investigates the relational reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using a synthetic dataset of geometric shapes to analyze how visual information is encoded. The authors find that while VLMs demonstrate some genuine visual reasoning, they predominantly rely on language cues and shortcuts, indicating a need for improved understanding of visual relations. This work highlights the limitations of current VLMs in fully grasping visual contexts, suggesting avenues for enhancing their reasoning abilities.
items.judge: The research explores relational reasoning in vision-language models, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models
items.details: Songchun Zhang, Yaowei Li, Junhao Zhuang, Weiyang Jin et al. · 62 HF upvotes
items.summary: EchoWM introduces an omnimodal world model capable of generating 720p video, environmental sound, music, and speech while allowing for continuous navigation. It improves trajectory following and visual quality in generative media by utilizing a shared metric-scale relative 6-DoF trajectory for both discrete commands and continuous poses, along with a complementary data engine and progressive training methods. Extensive evaluations demonstrate its effectiveness in supporting first- and third-person interactions across diverse subjects, maintaining synchronization of audio-visual elements during long-horizon generation.
items.judge: EchoWM presents an innovative omnimodal world model for generative media, integrating video, sound, and speech.

items.title: From Generation to Simulation: How Far Are World Models from Being True Simulators?
items.details: Tong Wang, Huan Deng, Mucheng Yang, Yang He et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents a systematic assessment of generative world models against eight capabilities of traditional simulators, revealing that while these models have achieved functional substitution in interaction and controllability, they significantly lag in formal guarantees of physical laws and structured state feedback. Notably, only 6 out of 163 implementation papers provide a runtime interface for querying entity states, highlighting a critical gap in state feedback. The authors propose six research directions to bridge these gaps, including formalized physics and long-horizon stability.
items.judge: The paper assesses the capabilities of generative world models in comparison to traditional simulators, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Unlocking the Potential of Image Editing via Concept Scaling and Dense Supervision
items.details: Long Cui, Xiaoqian Liu, Qi Qin, Yi Xin et al. · 45 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel hierarchical taxonomy of over 1,000 fine-grained edit concepts and presents ConceptEdit-12M, a dataset of 12 million high-quality image editing pairs, addressing inefficiencies in existing image editing frameworks. By implementing a dense supervision training strategy that combines multiple non-interfering concepts into single image pairs, the authors report significant improvements in training efficiency and model performance compared to previous methods. Additionally, they introduce ConceptEdit-Bench, an evaluation suite for assessing model capabilities across diverse real-world scenarios.
items.judge: The paper addresses image editing and introduces a comprehensive taxonomy for edit concepts.

items.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
items.details: Bowen Cui, Weijie Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Yefei He et al. · 25 HF upvotes
items.summary: Block3D introduces a novel block-wise diffusion framework for text-to-3D generation that significantly improves inference efficiency by reducing mean generation time from 25.71 seconds to 4.99 seconds, achieving a 5.15x speedup over traditional autoregressive methods. This approach partitions the discrete shape-token sequence into contiguous blocks, allowing for autoregressive generation while employing confidence-guided intra-block correction to minimize error accumulation, thus maintaining high geometric fidelity.
items.judge: Block3D addresses efficient text-to-3D generation, contributing to advancements in generative media.

items.title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
items.details: Hongbo Lu, Liang Yao, Chenghao He, Hao Han et al. · 24 HF upvotes
items.summary: RISE (Refining Imagination through SElective Rollout) introduces an adaptive imagination framework for World Action Models (WAMs) that optimizes planning by dynamically allocating imagination budgets based on expected benefits, improving planning performance while reducing unnecessary computation. The framework employs a Latent Evaluator to assess risk and a Rollout Gate to balance expected benefits against computational costs. Additionally, it utilizes CounterDrive, a counterfactual dataset that enhances future dynamics and risk supervision, demonstrating superior results on NAVSIM and nuScenes benchmarks.
items.judge: The paper discusses adaptive imagination in world action models, relevant to planning and simulation.

items.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
items.details: Bakbergen Ryskulov, Iker García-Ferrero, David Montero, David Jansen et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH), a novel approach for recovering performance in 4-bit quantized large language models (LLMs) that outperforms traditional quantization-aware training (QAT). QAH distills a 4-bit model directly from an uncompressed version, achieving superior results on 7 out of 9 benchmarks while reducing memory usage by approximately 75% and halving the parameter count compared to its bfloat16 source. The method converges about 7 times faster than QAT and maintains stability during training, making it a practical solution for deploying compressed LLMs without extensive hyper-parameter tuning.
items.judge: The paper presents a practical recipe for recovering compressed LLMs, relevant to inference acceleration.

items.title: Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress
items.details: Chen Yang, Haiyuan Wan, Rengrong Xiong, Yize Chen et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Reasoning-Progress-Aware Reward Filtering for On-Policy Distillation (R2-OPD), which enhances on-policy distillation by addressing the misalignment between teacher-derived rewards and actual reasoning progress. By implementing a dual-ranking system that compares teacher rewards with independently estimated progress rewards, R2-OPD selectively suppresses conflicting supervision, leading to improved reasoning performance in language models. The approach demonstrates consistent gains over standard OPD, particularly in reasoning tasks.
items.judge: The paper explores on-policy distillation techniques applicable to generative models.

items.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration
items.details: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: TileMix introduces a tile-centric mixed-precision attention kernel that optimizes long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) by partitioning the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles and employing compact bitmask routing for precision decisions. This approach enhances throughput over FP16 while recovering quality lost with uniform INT8, achieving a controllable accuracy-efficiency trade-off across various model families, as demonstrated in benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.
items.judge: The paper presents an inference acceleration method that could benefit generative media.

items.title: pipecat-ai/pipecat
items.details: `python` · 14,696★ · 81 stars today
items.summary: Pipecat is an open-source framework designed for developing voice agents and multimodal applications with real-time AI capabilities. It emphasizes modularity and community contributions, allowing for flexible integration of various AI components. Notably, it supports seamless interaction between voice and visual modalities, enhancing user experience in multimodal applications.
items.judge: This framework supports multimodal applications, which may include generative media.

items.title: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM
items.details: `python` · 17,584★ · 24 stars today
items.summary: NVIDIA's Megatron-LM is an open-source framework designed for training large-scale transformer models efficiently, leveraging model parallelism to scale up to trillions of parameters. The repository includes optimizations for mixed precision training and supports various architectures, enabling researchers to significantly reduce training time and resource consumption while maintaining model performance. Notably, it provides tools for both single-node and multi-node training setups, facilitating broader accessibility for large model training.
items.judge: This is an open-source LLM training project, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
items.details: Hongyu Li, Bowen Wen, Xinghao Zhu, Yixuan Wang et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: Hydra-0 introduces a novel generalist world model that utilizes action flow to represent robot actions as pixel motion, achieving a 90.4% reduction in robot-motion error and a 60.2% reduction in object-motion error compared to its action-conditioned baseline. This model supports zero-shot composition and data-efficient adaptation, demonstrating a Pearson correlation of r=0.96 on the RoboLab benchmark between replayed and reference success rates. Additionally, it features an emergent inverse mode that predicts robot motion from human-demonstrated object flow, enabling executable actions without the need for task-specific expert demonstrations.
items.judge: Introduces a generalist world model for video generation and control.

items.title: UniSpace: Unified Visual Representation and Scalable Multimodal Modeling
items.details: Jinbo Yan, Limeng Qiao, Jie Qin, Junyan He et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces UniSpace, an 8B Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts model that integrates understanding, generation, and editing within a unified visual representation space derived from a pretrained semantic Vision Transformer (ViT). The key innovation, Patch Reparameterization, enhances fine-grained visual detail recovery while maintaining multimodal understanding, resulting in improved pixel reconstruction and a favorable trade-off between reconstruction and generation tasks. System evaluations indicate significant advancements in text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing capabilities.
items.judge: Explores unified visual representation for image generation and editing.

items.title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter
items.details: Yunze Tong, Mushui Liu, Canyu Zhao, Shiyi Zhang et al. · 29 HF upvotes
items.summary: InfinityEdit introduces a novel lightweight edit adapter for infinite video editing, enabling models to apply edits to ongoing video streams rather than static clips. It employs three attention modules—history cross-attention, temporal causal self-attention, and edit cross-attention—to ensure faithful continuation of video content while maintaining generation quality across unbounded edit sequences. Experimental results demonstrate that InfinityEdit effectively integrates edits into the video stream without compromising the original model's generation capabilities.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel approach to video editing that extends to future frames, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
items.details: Pardis Taghavi, Reza Langari, Gaurav Pandey · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces SparsePR, a novel training-free block-sparse attention mechanism that enhances video generation and world models by reducing attention-reconstruction error while maintaining generation quality. SparsePR achieves 1.48x-2.61x end-to-end speedups with a realized executed-pair density of 22.0-26.0%, primarily through its innovative Response-Coupled Partitioning and Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction techniques. The method demonstrates significant improvements across four heterogeneous models, with ablation studies indicating that probe fitting is crucial for error reduction.
items.judge: Discusses training-free sparse attention for video generation and world models.

items.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs
items.details: Luka Ribar, Jeevan Bhoot, Douglas Orr · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel framework for efficiently quantizing vision-language models (VLMs) for deployment on mobile devices, achieving a 2.7-bit-per-parameter format that enables effective execution on Arm CPUs. This method compresses the Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct model to 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations while maintaining strong performance on standard visual question answering tasks, significantly improving the feasibility of running VLMs in resource-constrained environments.
items.judge: The paper discusses quantization for VLMs, which is relevant for inference acceleration in generative media.

items.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking
items.details: Enjun Du, Siyi Liu, Zirong Chen, Xinyu Zuo et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: EviRank introduces a novel approach to multimodal image re-ranking by framing it as a semantic constraint satisfaction problem, allowing for structured relevance evidence extraction from queries. This method utilizes a unified evidence package with six semantic slots to improve re-ranking accuracy, achieving state-of-the-art performance across five benchmarks, while a distilled student model retains over 90% of the teacher's performance at a significantly reduced computational cost. The approach enhances the interpretability and reliability of re-ranking in complex queries compared to existing methods.
items.judge: The paper discusses multimodal image re-ranking, which relates to image generation and evaluation.

items.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
items.details: Xianyun Sun, Chaoyou Fu, Zhengye Zhang, Feiyang Duan et al. · 25 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces OmniAssistBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) in assistant-style interactions, addressing the limitations of static datasets in capturing dynamic user interactions. The benchmark utilizes a dataset constructed from reverse-engineered Internet videos, requiring over 1000 expert person-hours, and provides predefined priors to guide user interactions along specific paths. Results indicate that while the proprietary Gemini-3-Pro scores 66.4 and the open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct scores 51.2, both models struggle with visual prompts and maintaining context, highlighting significant areas for improvement in real-time video assistance.
items.judge: Evaluates omni-modal LLMs for interactive video assistance, relevant to video generation.

items.title: Towards Real-Time and Adaptable LiDAR Scene Completion
items.details: Azhar Hussian, Martin Vossiek, Vasileios Belagiannis · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents RapidLiDAR, a novel LiDAR scene completion method that achieves real-time performance by introducing an adaptive initialization module, which predicts spatially varying displacements for partial input points, eliminating the need for manual noise tuning. This approach, combined with a multi-scale reconstruction module that utilizes voxel- and BEV-based feature extraction, enables RapidLiDAR to complete scenes in 0.1 seconds, making it 2.3 times faster than the previous state-of-the-art method while maintaining comparable completion performance on SemanticKITTI and KITTI-360 datasets.
items.judge: The paper discusses LiDAR scene completion, which is relevant to 3D generation.

items.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
items.details: `python` · 11,386★ · 195 stars today
items.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully-local alternative to ElevenLabs, offering capabilities for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation across 646 languages. Its notable design choice emphasizes local processing, enhancing privacy and reducing reliance on cloud services. This tool could significantly benefit ML researchers focusing on generative audio applications and multilingual voice synthesis.
items.judge: This tool focuses on voice cloning and video dubbing, relevant to generative media.

items.title: NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech
items.details: `python` · 18,263★ · 45 stars today
items.summary: NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech is a scalable generative AI framework designed for researchers and developers focusing on Large Language Models, multimodal applications, and speech AI, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS). The framework emphasizes modularity and extensibility, allowing users to easily integrate and experiment with various components for speech tasks. Notably, it supports state-of-the-art models and provides tools for efficient training and inference, enhancing performance in speech-related applications.
items.judge: This framework supports multimodal AI, including generative aspects.

items.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
items.details: Yudong Jin, Tao Xie, Qihang Zhang, Zehong Shen et al. · 63 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces 4DAnyone, a novel framework that reconstructs 4D humans from uncalibrated monocular videos by generating multiview-consistent videos and utilizing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS). It addresses the limitations of existing video diffusion models by implementing Reference Context Packing (RCP) and Target Context Routing (TCR), which significantly improve cross-view consistency and detail stabilization, resulting in superior novel-view video quality and 4DGS reconstruction performance. The framework demonstrates robust generalization in real-world scenarios, as validated by experiments on the DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans datasets.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for reconstructing 4D humans from video, directly related to generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
items.details: Hengyuan Xu, Qixun Wang, Yiji Cheng, Miles Yang et al. · 39 HF upvotes
items.summary: WithEveryone introduces a unified framework for generating group images with up to ten specified identities, significantly improving identity preservation and reducing artifacts. The model achieves a face similarity score of 0.499, up from 0.462 with GPT-Image-2, while decreasing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055. Its novel Layout-Grounded ID Loss and ID Representation Forcing techniques enable effective identity-layout binding, covering 97.3% of requested identities with a low duplicate rate of 2.8%.
items.judge: The paper introduces a framework for generating group images, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies
items.details: Bhavya Sukhija, Oliver Groth, Mohit Shridhar, Tim Hertweck et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: EXIMO introduces a novel three-stage algorithm for efficiently finetuning vision-language-action (VLA) policies in robotic manipulation, addressing the challenges of high sample inefficiency and extensive human labor in dataset collection. By integrating a vision-language model (VLM) as a planner to decompose complex tasks, EXIMO significantly enhances sample efficiency and final performance compared to existing methods, as demonstrated in extensive experiments. The approach consists of exploration, imitation, and optimization phases, allowing for effective learning of new tasks with reduced reliance on traditional teleoperation datasets.
items.judge: The paper discusses finetuning VLA policies, which relates to vision-language models but is not directly focused on generative media.

items.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
items.details: Yudong Jin, Tao Xie, Qihang Zhang, Zehong Shen et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces 4DAnyone, a novel framework that reconstructs 4D humans from uncalibrated monocular videos by generating multiview-consistent videos and utilizing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS). It improves upon existing video diffusion models by addressing bounded-attention-context issues through Reference Context Packing (RCP) and Target Context Routing (TCR), achieving $O(1)$ reference-context complexity and enhanced information sharing across target views. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in novel-view video quality and 4DGS reconstruction compared to previous methods, with robust generalization to in-the-wild scenarios.
items.judge: The framework reconstructs 4D humans from videos, directly relating to generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
items.details: Hengyuan Xu, Qixun Wang, Yiji Cheng, Miles Yang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: WithEveryone introduces a unified framework for group image generation that effectively manages up to ten specified identities by employing a Layout-Grounded ID Loss to directly supervise identity correspondence, thus enhancing stability over traditional embedding methods. The model achieves a significant improvement in face similarity, increasing from 0.462 to 0.499 compared to GPT-Image-2, while also reducing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055. Additionally, it successfully covers 97.3% of requested identities with a low duplicate rate of 2.8%, demonstrating the efficacy of explicit identity-layout grounding in scaling identity-preserving generation.
items.judge: The paper introduces a framework for generating group images with identity preservation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
items.details: Taihang Hu, Zhao Wang, Zuan Gao, Tao Liu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: Swift-Image introduces a compact unified model for text-to-image generation and image editing, achieving leading aggregate performance with only 6 billion parameters and 243,000 GPU training hours. The model employs a progressive training pipeline and innovative techniques such as parallel expert reinforcement learning and a Prompt Enhancer to optimize visual quality and user alignment. Notably, the compressed 3 billion parameter variant maintains performance with minimal loss, while few-step distillation enhances editing capabilities with reduced sampling steps.
items.judge: Swift-Image explores compact unified models for text-to-image and image editing, aligning with generative image research.

items.title: DreamHand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
items.details: Yufei Liu, Xixi Wang, Hao Li, Ganlong Zhao et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces DreamHand, a novel framework that repurposes video diffusion models (VDMs) into a deterministic geometry encoder for robust recovery of 3D hand motion in egocentric video. By employing a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder and a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder, DreamHand achieves a 30% reduction in mean per joint position error (MPJPE) on the occlusion-heavy ARCTIC dataset and a 40% reduction on HOT3D, with improvements of 46%-61% when accounting for out-of-sight hands. This approach eliminates the need for external detectors and supports configurations without test-time camera intrinsics, enhancing the scalability of hand motion recovery for robotic manipulation tasks.
items.judge: This paper repurposes video diffusion models for 3D hand motion recovery, aligning with generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration
items.details: Zhaokun He, Kangbiao Shi, Axi Niu, Jian Jin et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: DPC-Net introduces a novel Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration, effectively addressing structural distortions and semantic inconsistencies by integrating degradation-semantic coupled priors with low-level visual priors. The architecture employs a Degradation-Aware Network (DAN) guided by a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to enhance feature extraction, and a Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module (DPCR) that combines these priors during decoding, resulting in significant improvements in restoration quality over existing state-of-the-art methods. Extensive evaluations indicate that DPC-Net outperforms previous approaches across multiple restoration benchmarks.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel image restoration model, which is directly related to generative image tasks.

items.title: BeyondMasks: Evaluating Causal and Physical Consistency in Video Object Removal
items.details: Yigit Ekin, Enes Sanli, Aykut Erdem, Erkut Erdem et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces BeyondMasks, a novel benchmark for evaluating causal and physical consistency in video object removal, addressing the limitations of existing protocols that focus solely on masked region fidelity. BeyondMasks includes temporally aligned synthetic and real-world video pairs with clean background references, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of object removal that considers secondary physical effects like shadows and reflections. Additionally, the authors propose the CORE evaluation protocol, which aligns more closely with human judgments by jointly measuring object disappearance and after-effect consistency, revealing significant gaps in current state-of-the-art methods.
items.judge: Evaluates generative video models for object removal, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Orthogonal JEPA: Factorized Predictive States for Latent World Models
items.details: Taoyong Cui, Pheng Ann Heng, Wanli Ouyang · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces Orthogonal JEPA, a novel latent world-modeling framework that enhances predictive state representation by employing orthogonal predictive factorization. This approach allows for the decomposition of target states into multiple components, improving the model's ability to handle complex systems by reducing redundancy and enhancing gradient flow for less dominant signals. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in representation quality and forecasting across various domains, including vision and health records.
items.judge: Explores latent world models which are relevant to generative media.

items.title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
items.details: Weiliang Huang, Huanrong Liu, Bob Zhang, Qi Dou et al. · cs.CV cs.RO
items.summary: The paper introduces a preliminary joint visual-trajectory world-action model for surgical motion planning, which simultaneously forecasts future visual states and instrument trajectories from historical surgical data. This approach improves first-segment PSNR from 18.86 to 23.11 dB and reduces Average Displacement Error (ADE) from 45.77 to 22.22 pixels compared to one-shot predictions, demonstrating the feasibility of joint forecasting. However, the authors note challenges with visual degradation and trajectory errors over longer prediction horizons that need to be addressed in future work.
items.judge: The paper discusses visual-trajectory forecasting for surgical motion planning, relevant to world models and multimodal reasoning.

items.title: τ_0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
items.details: Xiaowei Cai, Yunuo Cai, Bingao Chen, Jingxiao Chen et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces τ_0-VLA, a hierarchical robot foundation model that enhances long-horizon robot manipulation by employing world-model-guided test-time computation, allowing for scalable inference through high-level subtask generation and alternative exploration. This approach, trained on 40,115 hours of diverse real-world data, significantly improves next-subtask prediction accuracy and closed-loop success rates in both in-domain and distribution-shifted scenarios. The model's design emphasizes the allocation of additional computation for complex decision-making, marking a notable advancement over traditional single-pass hierarchical VLA models.
items.judge: Introduces a hierarchical model for robot manipulation with world-model guidance.

items.title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models
items.details: Xinye Li, Lingshuai Lin, Lei Wang, Liuzhou Zhang et al. · 13 HF upvotes
items.summary: ForgeWM introduces a progressive framework for action-conditioned video world models, enhancing few-step video synthesis through techniques such as domain adaptation and causal consistency distillation. It achieves superior performance in imaging quality, motion-profile agreement, and action-sign accuracy on Minecraft trajectories, with the lowest LPIPS score, while also enabling a dual-path deployment for latency-critical interactions. The framework's replay-time refinement matches four-step reference quality, maintaining a trajectory fidelity three times closer than traditional noise regeneration methods.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for action-conditioned video world models, relevant to generative video.

items.title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation
items.details: Yinming Huang, Shuyuan Tu, Xi Yan, Zihan Yang et al. · 9 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces VA-Judger, a novel omni-reward model for joint video-audio generation that leverages a large-scale human-preference dataset (VAPref-10K) to improve alignment with human preferences. By employing a structured approach to preference learning and dimension-wise reinforcement learning, VA-Judger significantly enhances the quality of generated content, outperforming existing metric baselines in predicting human preferences and yielding substantial improvements in generation quality during post-training. The proposed benchmark, VA-Judger-Bench, facilitates comprehensive evaluation of reward models against human preferences across various domains.
items.judge: The paper discusses reward modeling for joint video-audio generation, relevant to generative media.

items.title: NARU: A Benchmark for NARrative Evolution and Cultural Nuance Understanding in Japanese Extreme Long Video
items.details: Yuheng Huang, Jianlang Chen, Jiayang Song, Hua Qi et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: NARU introduces a benchmark for evaluating narrative evolution and cultural nuance understanding in Japanese long-form videos, consisting of 1,481 questions across 155 videos totaling 146.8 hours. It employs a hierarchical memory-based annotation pipeline to create structured event, narrative, and cultural annotations, validated by 68 native speakers. The benchmark highlights significant limitations in existing models regarding long-range narrative integration and culturally grounded reasoning, providing a systematic testing ground for improving MLLMs in high-context video interpretation.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark for long-form video understanding, relevant to video generation.

items.title: LLMs Get Smarter from Targeted Synthetic Multilingual Data
items.details: Ishika Agarwal, Arkajyoti Charaborty, Tanner Sorensen, Neha Gupta et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces HOTFIXR, a data generation framework designed to enhance multilingual performance in language models by addressing language-specific competency (LSC). By generating targeted synthetic multilingual data based on identified weaknesses in a student model, HOTFIXR achieves an average improvement of 6.2% in in-distribution tasks, reduces catastrophic forgetting on out-of-distribution tasks by 3.7%, and improves performance on out-of-distribution languages by 7.1%. The authors plan to release the code upon acceptance, contributing to the development of more proficient multilingual LLMs.
items.judge: The paper addresses LLMs and their performance across languages, relevant to language models.

items.title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models
items.details: Ruiguo Zhong, Benshan Ma, Xiaolong Chen, Lang Zhang et al. · cs.RO cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces DA-WAM, a novel framework that integrates predictive representation learning, action-conditioned future modeling, and trajectory scoring into a unified decision-making objective for autonomous driving. By maintaining predictive supervision during planner optimization and generating distinct future latent states for each trajectory candidate, DA-WAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on NAVSIM-v1 and NAVSIM-v2, demonstrating significant improvements in decision-informative future modeling. The approach effectively addresses the limitations of existing methods that decouple future representation from planning, enhancing the action-specific guidance in trajectory selection.
items.judge: The paper discusses driving world models, which are relevant to generative video and simulation.

items.title: Image-Guided Pavement Defect Recognition in GPR Data with novel 3D Deep Learning Architecture
items.details: Yuandong Pan, Linjun Lu, Mudan Wang, Florian Noichl et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: This study introduces a novel 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture specifically designed for Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) data, enhancing defect classification in pavement inspection. The proposed method integrates RGB imagery with 3D GPR scans to create a large-scale annotated dataset, significantly improving the efficiency of data annotation and achieving superior performance over baseline models in detecting pavement defects. The architecture incorporates advanced features such as residual connections and attention mechanisms, validated through extensive experimental results and ablation studies.
items.judge: The study addresses 3D deep learning architecture for pavement defect recognition, relevant to generative 3D models.

items.title: Frozen DINO Localizes Image Edits Without a Localizer
items.details: Zane Kumar, Vishal Jain, Bernhard Kainz · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces TRAIL, a method for localizing image edits using frozen DINO encoders without requiring a localizer, achieving a patch AUROC of 0.903 on the CocoGlide test set, compared to 0.912 for the mask-supervised Detective SAM. TRAIL utilizes patch-level perturbation responses to create localization maps from a single global Haar perturbation, demonstrating strong performance even when transferred to Poisson image interpolation. The authors highlight that the localization signal from DINO encoders is sensitive to perturbation context, with performance varying significantly based on the global versus local application of perturbations.
items.judge: Focuses on localized image edits and their detection, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Mise-en-Scène: Implicit Layout Emergence in Diffusion Transformers for Human-AI Design Co-Creation
items.details: Zipeng Xu, Ryan Murdock, Umberto Michieli · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper presents Mise-en-Scène, a novel two-stage framework that integrates implicit layout emergence within a pretrained image-editing diffusion transformer for graphic design synthesis. This approach significantly improves design fidelity and quality, outperforming existing methods on the PrismLayersPlus benchmark by a wide margin, while maintaining exact asset preservation and allowing for editable, layered outputs. The method requires minimal adaptation of the pretrained model, avoiding the need for specialized conditioning typically used in multi-element generation.
items.judge: The paper discusses implicit layout emergence in image editing, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
items.details: Zhu Zhang, Jixun Wang, Xiaoang Xu, Xiaorong Wang et al. · cs.LG cs.AI cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (GC-OPD), which improves long-context reasoning by addressing the misalignment between token-level teacher support and task-specific verifier rewards. GC-OPD normalizes verifier rewards and OPD scores within rollout groups, utilizing their differences to enhance credit assignment across tokens, resulting in significant performance gains on five benchmarks: raising Qwen3-4B scores from 29.08 to 40.47 and Qwen3-8B scores from 35.12 to 44.65, outperforming vanilla OPD. The code is available at https://github.com/SolereZhang/GC-OPD.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for on-policy distillation, which is relevant to generative media training techniques.

items.title: Pre-Compiled Pipeline Shards for Distributed LLM Inference on Intel AI PC Fleets
items.details: Tate Berenbaum, Muthaiah Venkatachalam · cs.DC cs.AI cs.SE
items.summary: The paper presents a novel approach for distributed inference of large language models (LLMs) using pre-compiled pipeline shards on Intel AI PCs, enabling models beyond the memory capacity of individual machines. By employing techniques such as optimized OpenVINO graph compilation, speculative decoding, and micro-batching for concurrent user requests, the proposed method achieves a throughput improvement of 1.79x for two users compared to single-user performance on the same hardware. The implementation is available as a self-contained package on GitHub, facilitating reproducibility and further exploration.
items.judge: The paper discusses distributed LLM inference, which is relevant for generative media applications.

items.title: Enhancing EBSD throughput of battery electrode materials using super-resolution generative adversarial networks
items.details: John Mangum, Andrew Glaws, Francois Usseglio-Viretta, Steven Spurgeon et al. · cs.LG cond-mat.mtrl-sci
items.summary: This work introduces a super-resolution generative adversarial network (SRGAN) that enhances the throughput of electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis for Li-ion battery electrode materials, achieving a practical 5x upscaling factor that corresponds to a 25x speed-up in acquisition time. The SRGAN outperforms classical interpolation methods in preserving small grains and realistic grain boundaries, with relative errors of +5.7%, +8.2%, and -14.6% for key microstructural metrics. This advancement enables EBSD to serve as a high-throughput characterization tool, facilitating more statistically robust microstructural datasets in materials research.
items.judge: This work demonstrates a super-resolution GAN for enhancing battery material analysis, linking to generative image techniques.

items.title: ReWEIGH the Evidence: Calibrating Token-Level Ordinal Visual Evidence to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
items.details: Jihae Jeong, Junha Choi, Hwanjo Yu · cs.CV cs.AI cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces ReWEIGH, a novel decoding intervention for large vision-language models that mitigates hallucinations by calibrating token-level ordinal visual evidence. By aggregating vocabulary ranks across visual positions and applying a bounded penalty to candidates that fall below a token-specific reference, ReWEIGH achieves a reduction in hallucinated object mentions by up to 21.3% on four 7B backbones, while maintaining or improving overall performance. The method incurs an average latency increase of only 1.33% per token and is effective across six architecture families up to 32B parameters.
items.judge: The paper addresses hallucinations in vision-language models, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation
items.details: Keyu Tu, Zhuowei Chen, Mengqi Huang, Yuxin Wang et al. · 151 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces SemComp-Bench, a novel benchmarking framework for Semantic Task Completion in video generation, which emphasizes outcome-oriented generation and semantic grounding rather than traditional appearance consistency. The framework includes the SemComp-Data dataset, featuring a four-stage curation pipeline for standardizing video instances across six domains, and employs a vision-language model to evaluate outcome achievement and generation reliability through structured binary questions. Initial experiments reveal that maintaining semantic grounding while achieving intended outcomes poses significant challenges for existing video generation models.
items.judge: The paper introduces a video generation task with semantic grounding, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Decision-Metric Alignment in Latent World Models: Diagnostics and Action-Conditioned Objectives for MPC Planning
items.details: Jiawei Wang, Ke Rui, Yushen Zuo, Yichun Feng et al. · 15 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces DA-LeWM, an enhancement to JEPA-style latent world models that improves decision-metric alignment in model-predictive control (MPC) planning by incorporating inverse-dynamics and demonstration-conditioned goal-action heads. This approach accelerates convergence and achieves higher online success rates compared to the baseline LeWM, while maintaining similar probe scores, demonstrating that action-conditioned objectives can effectively refine the geometry of Euclidean-cost, CEM-based latent MPC.
items.judge: The paper addresses latent world models and decision-metric alignment, relevant to generative video and planning.

items.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
items.details: Jiayi Song, Shijie Huang, Fangtai Wu, Yubo Huang et al. · 21 HF upvotes
items.summary: EditBridge introduces a novel diffusion bridge framework for ultra-high-resolution image editing, achieving resolutions up to 4K while significantly improving efficiency and fidelity. By employing a prior-guided block-wise sparse attention mechanism, it reduces computational overhead and enhances detail preservation, resulting in a 3.6 to 8.4 times speedup at 2K resolutions and enabling practical 4K editing in just 61 seconds. This approach addresses critical issues of information divergence and texture degradation prevalent in traditional two-stage editing pipelines.
items.judge: The paper addresses high-resolution image editing, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: ATH-MaaS/Pixelle-Video

The repository emphasizes modular design, allowing for easy customization and integration with existing workflows.

items.title: DiffusionGemma Technical Report

This work contributes to the ongoing advancements in generative modeling by optimizing both efficiency and output quality.

items.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
items.details: Jiayi Song, Shijie Huang, Fangtai Wu, Yubo Huang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: EditBridge introduces a novel diffusion bridge framework for ultra-high-resolution image editing, achieving resolutions up to 4K while significantly improving efficiency and fidelity. By employing a prior-guided block-wise sparse attention mechanism, it reduces computational overhead and enhances detail preservation, resulting in a 3.6–8.4× speedup at 2K resolutions and enabling practical 4K editing in just 61 seconds. This approach addresses critical issues of information divergence and texture degradation present in traditional two-stage editing pipelines.
items.judge: The paper addresses high-resolution image editing techniques, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Optimize Your Sampling: Tuned Diffusion Sampling with Bayesian Optimization
items.details: Travis Zhang, Christian Belardi, Justin Lovelace, Jin Peng Zhou et al. · cs.LG cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Optimizing Your Sampling (OYS), a method that utilizes Bayesian optimization to directly optimize sampling timesteps in diffusion models, significantly enhancing sample quality without additional training. OYS achieves a 10x reduction in inference cost while maintaining 89%-94% of the quality of a traditional 50-step schedule, outperforming both default schedules and the Align Your Steps method in text-to-image generation and other image tasks. This approach is applicable to various samplers, including Euler and DPM-Solver++, and even to distilled models.
items.judge: The paper addresses optimizing sampling in diffusion models, relevant to generative image/video models.

items.title: AViTS: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Token Selection for Efficient Dynamic-Resolution Generation
items.details: Haoran Qin, Zhengan Yan, Shikang Zheng, Xiaobing Tu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces AViTS, an adaptive spatiotemporal token selection framework that enhances dynamic-resolution generation in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) by prioritizing resolution refinement for critical tokens based on latent-text attention and token-level feature variation. This approach significantly reduces redundant high-resolution computation, achieving up to 6.34x efficiency improvements on FLUX and nearly 9x FLOPs reduction on Qwen-Image-Edit, with potential gains of 14.76x when applied to distilled models. The implementation is available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for efficient dynamic-resolution generation in image synthesis.

items.title: GS-Voxel: Fitting-Free Structured Latents for Large-Scale 3DGS Generation
items.details: Ming Qian, Zijian Wang, Minchao Sun, Jincheng Xiong et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: GS-Voxel introduces a fitting-free structured latent framework for large-scale aerial 3D Gaussian scene generation, improving upon existing methods by deterministically converting pre-optimized 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructions into sparse active voxels without per-scene optimization. This approach utilizes a factorized VAE to encode voxel geometry and local Gaussian attributes, allowing latent capacity to scale with the number of occupied voxels, thus facilitating overlap-aware tiled inference for expansive scene generation. The method enhances the efficiency and scalability of 3D scene synthesis, particularly for applications requiring large-area coverage.
items.judge: GS-Voxel presents a novel framework for large-scale 3D generation, relevant to generative models.

items.title: LinCa: Accelerating Diffusion Models via Learnable Decomposed Feature Caching
items.details: Jinshan Liu, Haoran Qin, Xiaobing Tu, Jiacheng Liu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: LinCa introduces a novel feature caching framework for diffusion models that leverages learnable invertible networks to improve computational efficiency during image and video generation. By decomposing cached features into sub-components and employing differentiated prediction strategies, LinCa achieves 5-7x speedup with less than 0.2% additional parameters while maintaining near-lossless quality, outperforming existing uniform prediction methods. The implementation is available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The paper addresses acceleration techniques for diffusion models in image and video generation.

items.title: SFMformer: A Spatial-Frequency Modulation Transformer for Lightweight Image Super-Resolution
items.details: Chih-Hsiang Yang, Chia-Min Lin, Ching-Yu Tsai, Yung-Che Wang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces SFMformer, a lightweight image super-resolution model that employs a dual-branch spatial enhancement and wavelet-domain modulation to improve representation quality in sparse attention mechanisms. It achieves superior performance, ranking first in 28 of 30 PSNR/SSIM metrics across five benchmarks while maintaining under one million parameters, demonstrating practical deployment on resource-constrained devices like the Raspberry Pi 5. The study reveals that the joint gains from the model's components exceed the sum of their individual contributions, highlighting the importance of selection and aggregation quality in sparse attention networks.
items.judge: This work presents a novel transformer for lightweight image super-resolution, aligning with generative image models.

items.title: From Corpora to Co-Evolving Capabilities: Capability-Centric Data Design for Generalist Image Generation
items.details: Xingjian Wang, Zhao Wang, Taihang Hu, Jun Zheng et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces a capability-driven data infrastructure that enhances large-scale image generation by integrating capability-specific supervision with a curriculum scheduling approach. This framework curates a dataset comprising 440M images for text-to-image generation, 120M editing pairs, and over 27M image-entity pairs, enabling the training of multimodal diffusion models with 3B and 6B parameters. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in visual coverage, rendering versatility, and effective transfer across generative capabilities, as evaluated on CPI-Bench.
items.judge: The paper discusses a capability-driven data infrastructure for image generation, which is relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Towards Zero-Shot Task Transfer with Neurosymbolic World Models
items.details: Isidoro Tamassia, Lennert De Smet, Giuseppe Marra · cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel neurosymbolic world model that enables zero-shot task transfer by decoupling observation reconstruction from reward prediction, relying on structured symbolic components of the latent state. This approach enhances generalization capabilities compared to traditional task-dependent neural models, allowing for adaptation to new reward functions without additional environment interactions. The authors discuss the advantages and challenges of this method, demonstrating its superior performance in generalization over purely neural approaches.
items.judge: The paper discusses a new formulation of world models for zero-shot task transfer, relevant to generative video and world modeling.

items.title: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation
items.details: Minghui Guo, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei · 15 HF upvotes
items.summary: V-RAE introduces a novel video representation autoencoder that leverages frozen vision foundation model representations to create compact generative latents, significantly enhancing semantic organization in video generation. It achieves a remarkable 2.13 rFVD on K600, outperforming existing large-scale pretrained video VAEs, and demonstrates improved generation speed, converging up to 6x faster. Additionally, V-RAE introduces tFVD, a new metric for assessing temporal coherence, which correlates better with downstream generation quality than traditional reconstruction metrics.
items.judge: The paper proposes a new video representation autoencoder, directly related to video generation.

items.title: PixRestore: Unified Image Restoration via Pixel Diffusion Transformer
items.details: Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu, Xiangtao Kong, Jixin Zhao et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: PixRestore introduces a novel VAE-free pixel-space Diffusion Transformer for unified image restoration, achieving superior fidelity and perceptual quality with only 50M parameters and single-step inference. By training from scratch and employing a DINO-based feature reliability prediction mechanism, it effectively preserves fine-grained details and adapts to various degradations, outperforming existing UIR models on public benchmarks and real-world datasets. The design emphasizes efficiency and scalability, with larger variants available for enhanced performance.
items.judge: The paper focuses on image restoration using generative models, which aligns with generative image tasks.

items.title: CoinVE-200K: A Large-Scale High-Quality Dataset for Compositional Instruction-Guided Video Editing
items.details: Fuchen Long, Cong Wang, Zitao Gao, Wenhao Zhong et al. · 13 HF upvotes
items.summary: CoinVE-200K introduces a large-scale dataset for compositional instruction-guided video editing, featuring 1080p video-editing pairs with 2 to 5 atomic editing operations across diverse scenarios. The dataset is complemented by CoinVE-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating compositional editing tasks, and CoinVE-Edit, a 22B parameter model that utilizes region-aware attention to enhance multi-region editing while maintaining visual quality and temporal coherence. Experiments demonstrate that CoinVE-Edit significantly improves instruction following and compositional editing accuracy compared to existing methods.
items.judge: The introduction of a large-scale dataset for compositional instruction-guided video editing is highly relevant to video generation.

items.title: Energy-Guided Flow Matching
items.details: Haoyang Tong, Yu He, Fang Li, Lichen Ma et al. · 8 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Energy-Guided Flow Matching (EG-FM), a novel approach that enhances pixel-space generative models by explicitly modeling a coarse-to-fine generative trajectory through a heat-kernel-filtered endpoint, which evolves from low-frequency to clean images. This method achieves lower Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores, reaching 1.55 at 200 epochs and 1.45 at 600 epochs on the ImageNet class-conditional image generation task, while requiring no adaptation of the backbone or training data. The framework also demonstrates strong performance in text-to-image generation, achieving a GenEval score of 0.85 and a DPG-Bench score of 83.9. Code is available at https://github.com/ysng123/EG-FM.
items.judge: The paper introduces a novel generative model technique relevant to image generation.

items.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training
items.details: Kyle Chickering, Wei-An Lin, Swayam Bhanded, Dan Saunders et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper "Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training" presents a systematic study of scaling laws for text-to-image diffusion models, revealing that optimal training occurs at approximately 200 image tokens per parameter—ten times the requirement for language models. The authors demonstrate that diffusion models exhibit predictable scaling behavior similar to language models but necessitate significantly more data, and they emphasize that overtraining is less of a concern, suggesting practitioners prioritize data quantity over model size. The findings extend to generative quality metrics and training curve characteristics, indicating a universal form for these metrics.
items.judge: The paper presents a systematic study on scaling laws for text-to-image diffusion models.

items.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization
items.details: Tong Zhang, Motasem Alfarra, Carlos Hinojosa, Christos Louizos et al. · 12 HF upvotes
items.summary: DiSCO introduces a novel black-box defense mechanism for text-to-image generation that addresses the benign adversarial problem, where linguistically safe prompts still lead to harmful outputs. By employing distribution-guided suffix expansion through contrastive scoring on generated images, DiSCO reduces the attack success rate (ASR) by 37.7% for undefended models and 25.13% for defended models on the I2P benchmark, all while preserving semantic fidelity and improving image coherence. This approach is architecture-agnostic and requires no model retraining, making it a versatile plug-and-play solution for enhancing safety in generative models.
items.judge: The paper addresses safety in text-to-image generation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding
items.details: Bonan Zhang, Shiyu Dong, Quan Hung Tran, Katharina Gschwind et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents MoE-ViE, a Mixture-of-Experts vision encoder that significantly improves image and video understanding by utilizing fine-grained MoE topologies, achieving performance gains over dense and standard MoE architectures. The largest MoE-ViE model matches the zero-shot performance of a state-of-the-art encoder 1.7 times its size while operating at only 76% of its latency, and it outperforms all compared encoders when aligned with an LLM on various benchmarks. The implementation includes an auxiliary-loss-free balancing variant and a specialized MoE kernel to enhance expert utilization and reduce inference latency.
items.judge: The work explores efficient vision encoders for image and video understanding, relevant to multimodal models.

items.title: PTXBench: Benchmark and Adapt LLMs for GPU Kernel Optimization with Architecture-specific PTX
items.details: Genghan Zhang, Yixin Dong, Chengze Fan, Zhichen Zeng et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: PTXBench is a novel benchmark designed to evaluate and adapt large language models (LLMs) for GPU kernel optimization using architecture-specific PTX, focusing on functional correctness and performance speedup across GEMM and attention workloads on H100 and B200 GPUs. The study reveals that while architecture-specific PTX can enhance performance, success rates are inconsistent, particularly in complex attention backward workloads, and no model consistently outperforms frontier libraries. Additionally, the adaptation of Qwen3.6-27B through supervised fine-tuning shows improvements in several tasks, though generalization remains variable, highlighting the importance of data quality and coverage.
items.judge: The paper discusses optimizing LLMs for GPU kernels, relevant for inference acceleration in generative media.

items.title: DrewThomasson/ebook2audiobook

items.title: Microgpt in pure C hits 10M tps on Apple m5

items.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
items.details: Dengyang Jiang, Ruoyi Du, Zhennan Chen, Dongyang Liu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: This paper presents a novel latent-to-pixel training strategy for pixel-space diffusion models, demonstrating that this approach can achieve 3.18 to 4.75 times faster end-to-end inference compared to traditional latent-space models. The authors systematically analyze key design choices such as weight initialization and decoder architecture, ultimately providing a practical recipe that allows pixel-space models to match or exceed the performance of their latent-space counterparts. This work addresses the slow convergence of direct large-scale pre-training in pixel space, offering valuable insights for future research in generative modeling.
