items.title: Unlocking the Potential of Image Editing via Concept Scaling and Dense Supervision
items.details: Long Cui, Xiaoqian Liu, Qi Qin, Yi Xin et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel image editing framework that leverages a hierarchical taxonomy of over 1,000 fine-grained edit concepts and a dataset of 12 million high-quality editing pairs, known as ConceptEdit-12M. By implementing a dense supervision training strategy that combines multiple non-interfering concepts into single image pairs, the authors report significant improvements in training efficiency and model performance compared to existing methods. Additionally, they present ConceptEdit-Bench, an evaluation suite designed to assess model capabilities across diverse real-world scenarios.
items.judge: Addresses image editing through a novel approach in generative models.

items.title: PixRestore: Unified Image Restoration via Pixel Diffusion Transformer
items.details: Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu, Xiangtao Kong, Jixin Zhao et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: PixRestore introduces a VAE-free pixel-space Diffusion Transformer for unified image restoration, achieving superior fidelity and perceptual quality with only 50M parameters and single-step inference. By training the diffusion model from scratch and employing a novel feature reliability prediction mechanism, it effectively preserves fine-grained details and adapts to various degradations. Experiments demonstrate that PixRestore outperforms existing UIR models in robustness and efficiency, with potential for further performance enhancement in larger variants. Code is available at https://github.com/csslc/PixRestore.
items.judge: This paper presents a unified approach to image restoration using generative models, relevant to image generation.

items.title: VicEdit: Learning to Edit Videos from Visual In-Context Examples
items.details: Yuji Wang, Teng Hu, Yuheng Chen, Ran Yi et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: VicEdit introduces a novel paradigm for video editing that leverages Visual In-context Editing, allowing for multi-modal visual guidance instead of relying solely on textual instructions. The framework is supported by the VicEdit-400K dataset, which consists of 400,000 high-quality samples across ten task types, enhancing visual fidelity and semantic consistency. VicEdit achieves state-of-the-art performance in both basic instruction editing and visual in-context editing tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of its Modality-Adaptive Semantic Distillation and Dual-Context Injection techniques.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel approach to video editing using visual in-context examples, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: SplatGuide: Geometric Priors from 3D Gaussians for Pose-Free Novel View Synthesis
items.details: Yejun Zhang, Zihan Wang, Xu Ji, Yihao Wang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: SplatGuide introduces a novel approach to pose-free novel view synthesis by leveraging a single 3D Gaussian scene representation across three complementary roles: pixel-aligned geometric conditioning, occlusion-aware reference selection via per-Gaussian visibility, and feature-level guidance through cross-attention. This method addresses the information disconnect in prior pipelines, resulting in state-of-the-art performance on datasets such as RealEstate10K, DL3DV, Tanks-and-Temples, and Mip-NeRF 360, notably surpassing the ground-truth-pose baseline on RealEstate10K with a moderate number of input views.
items.judge: The paper discusses generating novel views from unposed images, relevant to 3D generation and image synthesis.

items.title: CaliBench: Are the Stochastic Dynamics of Video World Models Physically Calibrated?
items.details: Jonathan Sadeghi, Jenny Seidenschwarz, Jesse Allardice, Sirish Srinivasan et al. · cs.LG cs.AI
items.summary: CaliBench introduces a novel benchmarking framework for evaluating the calibration of video world models by scoring outcomes in a physically interpretable discrete space, rather than a learned feature space. This approach allows for precise calibration tests against known reference distributions, revealing that existing models, such as Veo 3.1, often exhibit significant miscalibration and low scorability across various scenes. The authors provide a new metric, mean normalized total variation (mnTV), and a detailed protocol for future model comparisons, highlighting that no single model excels across all tested scenarios.
items.judge: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating video world models based on physical outcomes.

items.title: GenRouter: Unified Workflow Routing for Agentic Image Generation
items.details: Harold Haodong Chen, Zhiyu Hou, Wen-Jie Shu, Weilin Ruan et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: GenRouter introduces a unified workflow routing framework for agentic image generation, significantly improving efficiency by reducing execution costs by over 95% and latency by 65% compared to traditional static pipelines. It standardizes diverse agentic workflows through GenCanvas, allowing for adaptive routing of prompts based on demand profiling, experience matching, and Pareto filtering. This system not only enhances visual alignment but also enables continuous self-evolution for robust zero-shot generalization, effectively optimizing resource usage in generative tasks.
items.judge: The paper discusses a unified workflow for agentic image generation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: Orbit-Planner: Towards Latent World Models for On-Orbit Obstacle Avoidance of Satellite Agents
items.details: Zhijian Li, Chao Ren, Peijin Wang, Xian Sun · cs.RO cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces Orbit-Planner, a two-stage latent world model designed for on-orbit obstacle avoidance in satellite navigation, which improves adaptability by learning action-conditioned spacecraft dynamics for future-state rollouts in latent space. Notably, it employs a Physics Probe to decode physical state changes from imagined trajectories, achieving a 91.7% success rate in closed-loop navigation tasks within Isaac Sim. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhijianLi2003/Orbit_Planner.
items.judge: Proposes a latent world model for satellite navigation, relevant to generative world models.

items.title: GRNEdit: Efficient General Video Editing from a New Binary-Evidence Perspective in Generative Refinement Networks
items.details: Feng Xie, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Zepeng Wang et al. · 13 HF upvotes
items.summary: GRNEdit introduces a lightweight two-stage framework for general video editing that significantly reduces resource requirements by using only 0.6M training pairs and less than 3% of the conditioning parameters compared to existing methods. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance, with GRNEdit-2B scoring 4.03 and GRNEdit-8B scoring 4.18 on OpenVE-Bench, outperforming several 14B open-source editors and matching the performance of leading models. Notably, it employs a novel binary-evidence perspective to refine editing semantics through local retain-or-flip decisions, enhancing content preservation and evidence utilization.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel framework for efficient video editing, aligning with generative video models.

items.title: WorldRover: A Scalable Synthetic Video Data Engine for World Exploration with Rich Annotations
items.details: Xiaojie Xu, Zhengyuan Lin, Runyi Li, Yihao Liu et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: WorldRover introduces a scalable synthetic video data engine that generates richly annotated explorations of artist-built environments, significantly enhancing the availability of paired RGB, metric depth, camera trajectories, and action signals for training generative models. The WorldRover-Engine, built on Unreal Engine, allows for minute-scale route rendering from multiple viewpoints and environmental states, resulting in the WorldRover-10M dataset, which includes dense optical flow and long-range 2D/3D point tracks. This approach transforms long-horizon world exploration into a manageable data-generation task, facilitating the development of models that can create and maintain coherent representations of explorable worlds.
items.judge: The paper discusses a synthetic video data engine for world exploration, relevant to generative video and world models.

items.title: AnyTalk: Speech Animation for Arbitrary Characters Leveraging a Video Generation Model
items.details: Kwan Yun, Serin Yoon, Sunjin Jung, Jung Eun Yoo et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: AnyTalk introduces a novel approach for generating 3D speech animations for arbitrary characters without the need for specific animation data, improving upon existing methods that require character-specific training. By utilizing a pre-trained video diffusion model and a Character-specific Fine-tuning (CsF) technique, it allows for lip-synced animations across various face meshes while significantly reducing manual effort and data requirements. The method also includes a real-time variant, AnyTalk_{RT}, enhancing usability for practical applications. The code is publicly available at https://serin-yoon.github.io/projects/anytalk/.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for generating 3D speech animations using video generation models, aligning with generative media.

items.title: MOSS-VL Technical Report
items.details: Pengyu Wang, Chenkun Tan, Shaojun Zhou, Qirui Zhou et al. · 37 HF upvotes
items.summary: MOSS-VL introduces a novel open vision-language model that enhances real-time interaction capabilities by employing gated cross-attention in its language decoder, allowing it to perceive incoming frames while generating text. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on three out of four streaming benchmarks, notably outperforming the best baseline by 28.5 points on the OmniMMI Proactive Alerting task. With 11.3B parameters, MOSS-VL demonstrates a significant improvement in time-to-first-token, increasing its advantage over a comparable model from 2.8x to 5.1x as visual context expands. The model, along with its training curriculum and inference code, is available at https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-VL.
items.judge: The paper discusses a vision-language model with real-time interaction capabilities, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding
items.details: Fan Zhang, Guangming Yao, Jinyang Wu, Hao Wu et al. · 9 HF upvotes
items.summary: VideoGAIA introduces a novel benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on agentic video understanding, moving beyond traditional single-turn tasks to a multi-turn, tool-augmented interaction framework. This benchmark includes 271 co-designed tasks that require models to iteratively analyze videos and integrate multimodal evidence, with leading models like GPT-5.5 and Kimi-K3 achieving under 60% accuracy, indicating the benchmark's potential to assess advanced MLLMs effectively. The rigorous task design, verified by human experts, ensures a challenging and relevant evaluation of next-generation AI capabilities.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models in video understanding.

items.title: StreamOPD: A Post-Training Recipe with Spatio-Temporal Cue Gating for Streaming Video Understanding
items.details: Keming Wu, Baoyi Wang, Kaichen Zhang, Xiang An et al. · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces StreamOPD, a novel post-training approach for streaming video understanding that combines on-policy distillation with spatio-temporal cue gating, achieving a significant performance improvement on StreamingBench from 77.9% to 83.9%. This method also enhances OVO-Bench by 9.1 points while maintaining unchanged inference, demonstrating that effective post-training strategies can yield substantial gains without additional memory or retrieval mechanisms. The approach is designed to be transparent and reproducible, providing a valuable resource for open-source streaming video research.
items.judge: The paper presents a post-training method for streaming video understanding, relevant to video generation.

items.title: A Plug-and-Play 2D Motion Interface for Real-World Motion Language Models
items.details: Kaname Yokoyama, Norimichi Ukita · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces a Plug-and-Play 2D Motion Interface that allows 3D-pretrained Motion Language Models (MoLMs) to process 2D motion inputs without requiring modifications or fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves performance on par with 3D motion inputs and surpasses the performance of MoLMs trained from scratch on 2D motions. Additionally, the authors provide a new monocular real-world video motion evaluation dataset and a real-video adapter, highlighting the practical advantages of using 2D motions for real-world applications. Code is available at https://github.com/irajisamurai/2D-Motion-Interface.
items.judge: The introduction of a 2D Motion Interface for 3D motion models relates to generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: DumpsterCluster: From Dumpster Diving to Serving LLaMA-70B on $60 GPUs
items.details: Zeyu Cao, Xuan Guo, Cheng Zhang, Cheuk Hang Lau et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents the DumpsterCluster, a 128-GPU system built from second-hand components that serves LLaMA-70B with competitive throughput, achieving significant cost savings (approximately $22K vs. $600K for a new system). While the system demonstrates economic viability through pipeline-parallel optimizations, it also highlights critical environmental concerns, revealing that older GPUs can produce up to 40x higher carbon emissions per token compared to modern hardware, emphasizing the need for strategic deployment in regions with low-cost, clean energy to ensure sustainability.
items.judge: The paper discusses repurposing retired GPUs for LLM inference, relevant to inference acceleration.

items.summary: CPI-Bench introduces a novel benchmark for real-world image editing that significantly improves performance differentiation among models by addressing limitations of existing benchmarks, which primarily focus on single-image tasks. It comprises three subsets: CPI-General-Bench for diverse and multi-image editing tasks, CPI-Practical-Bench for high-frequency user scenarios, and CPI-Intelligent-Bench for reasoning-based editing, thereby providing a comprehensive evaluation framework. Notably, CPI-Bench aligns closely with the Arena Image Edit Leaderboard, enhancing its reliability as a proxy for real-world user experience.

items.title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination
items.details: Shuo Liang, Yixing Ma, Pengfei Zhou, Xingyan Chen et al. · 253 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces RA-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI-generated video detection, comprising 17,886 videos with 1,830 real-video anchors across ten social-risk categories and 16,056 generated clips from various generators. The evaluation reveals that existing detectors, including traditional and zero-shot multimodal models, fail to generalize consistently across different instances of RA-Bench, indicating that current detection methods are inadequate against realistic AI-generated videos, particularly as social dissemination complicates detection efforts. This highlights an urgent need for more robust detection systems that can adapt to evolving generative models.
items.judge: The paper evaluates video generation and detection in crisis scenarios, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
items.details: Zian Meng, Zhen Li, Chuanhao Li, Qiang Li et al. · 22 HF upvotes
items.summary: Marionette introduces a novel approach to world modeling in interactive games by explicitly predicting a 276-dimensional 3D world state, which includes articulated skeletons and root trajectories, while utilizing a zero-parameter renderer for geometric computations. This method enhances controllability, as evidenced by a 31% reduction in joint error when actions are mismatched, and significantly reduces issues like ground penetration by 66% through the application of terrain colliders and separation constraints. The model maintains high fidelity in photorealistic RGB observations, achieving a Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) of 831, comparable to 799 for recorded poses.
items.judge: The paper presents a model for predicting world states and rendering geometry, relevant to world models.

items.title: Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction
items.details: Zhongbin Guo, Jiahao Xie, Dongling Xiao, Qianle Wang et al. · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces GAS, a novel training framework that leverages visual generation as auxiliary supervision to enhance multimodal understanding in MLLMs without incurring inference overhead. By employing a decoupled Mixture-of-Transformers architecture and Next Embedding Prediction, GAS improves spatial comprehension and perception across various model scales, demonstrating significant gains in visual representation learning while maintaining a shared lower trunk to optimize training efficiency. The framework's design allows for the integration of generation tasks that require deep cognitive grounding, ultimately leading to improved multimodal understanding without additional inference costs.
items.judge: The work enhances visual understanding in multimodal models, linking generation and understanding in a meaningful way.

items.title: UniProbe: A Learnable Token-Level Hallucination Detector for Large VLMs using Multi-Structural Internal Representations
items.details: Dvir Samuel, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Ethan Fetaya et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: UniProbe introduces a novel, learnable token-level hallucination detector for large vision-language models (LVLMs), improving hallucination detection by up to 55% while maintaining a latency of 1.06 times that of standard generation. It utilizes a directed graph structure to model the relationships between image patches, query tokens, and generated tokens, employing a combination of graph neural networks, vision transformers, and GRUs to effectively integrate spatial, relational, and sequential evidence. This approach allows for targeted intervention during generation, enhancing the reliability of LVLM outputs without the need for extensive fine-tuning.
items.judge: Addresses hallucination in vision-language models, relevant to inference in generative contexts.

items.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
items.details: Hunar Batra, Lachin Naghashyar, Ashkan Khakzar, Philip Torr et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces MMDiff, a multimodal model-diffing framework that utilizes sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to isolate and control features in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). MMDiff enables feature isolation, task-specific feature detection, and feature-level control, achieving an average degradation of 12% on spatial tasks and 17% on OCR when specific features are removed, while also improving spatial and OCR accuracy by 3.6% and 1.8%, respectively, compared to a standard steering baseline. This framework enhances interpretability and control over MLLM behaviors, contributing to safer and more effective model outputs.

The model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on WBench and competitive results on VBench-Long and VBench-2.0, generating 1.5-second chunks in 2.11 seconds on a single H200.

The framework also clarifies the conditions under which the components of a world model can be identified from data, contributing to a deeper understanding of causal reasoning in AI systems.

items.summary: The paper introduces Reduced Matrix Multiplication (RMM), a novel input-adaptive inference method that optimizes matrix products in Transformer models by selecting informative slices, achieving a balance between accuracy and efficiency without altering model weights. RMM demonstrates significant runtime improvements, particularly for longer sequences, across various language models (1B to 70B parameters) and tasks, while revealing that attention-side computations are more amenable to reduction than MLP components. This approach positions RMM as a scalable solution for enhancing inference efficiency in both language and multimodal vision-language tasks.

items.title: SCULPT: Subtractive Composition for 3D Part Generation
items.details: Sikuang Li, Chen Yang, Jiemin Fang, Jiazhong Cen et al. · cs.CV cs.GR
items.summary: The paper introduces SCULPT, a novel framework for part-aware 3D generation that utilizes subtractive composition to iteratively extract parts from a complete object in a structured 3D latent space. Unlike traditional methods that either segment pre-generated shapes or synthesize parts from fixed layouts, SCULPT employs a joint split predictor that simultaneously generates an extracted part and updates the remaining object, resulting in improved geometry and coherence. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on the PartObjaverse dataset, achieving fine-grained textured part decomposition while maintaining strong complete-object reconstruction.
items.judge: The paper on 3D part generation has relevance to generative 3D models.

Notably, it allows for retrospective input editing of blanking-period records and does not require follow-up MRI intensities at inference, enhancing its practical applicability in clinical settings.

items.title: Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation
items.details: Hmrishav Bandyopadhyay, Xuanchi Ren, Zijian Huang, Jay Zhangjie Wu et al. · 5 HF upvotes

CMD replaces bidirectional full-clip scoring with a causal teacher that evaluates targets without future context, leading to state-of-the-art performance on both short- and long-video benchmarks and enhanced adherence to time-varying camera controls. The framework's design choices, including Prefix Scoring and Prefix Corruption, stabilize training and extend its applicability to various generation tasks.

items.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence
items.details: Haokai Zhang, Yuhang Ding, Yunshu Zhou, Xinze Du et al. · 30 HF upvotes
items.summary: The Spatial Memory Agent (SMA) introduces a novel framework for enhancing the spatial reasoning capabilities of frozen vision-language models (VLMs) without requiring parameter updates or external spatial tools during inference. By leveraging experience-grounded learning, SMA distills transferable lessons from verified spatial experiences and assigns a Transfer Reliability Score (TRS) to guide inference, achieving superior performance across five spatial benchmarks and four base VLMs, with the highest macro average and best accuracy in most evaluations. This approach establishes a new parameter-update-free method for spatial self-evolution in VLMs.
items.judge: The paper addresses spatial intelligence in VLMs, which has some relevance to multimodal generation.

items.title: MakazhanAlpamys/Soup
items.details: 1,512★ · 303 stars today
items.summary: The repository "Soup" enables fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) using a single YAML configuration file, streamlining the process for users. It employs layer streaming techniques to efficiently train an 8 billion parameter model on a GPU with only 4 GB of memory, significantly lowering hardware requirements for LLM training. This approach enhances accessibility for researchers with limited computational resources.
items.judge: The project involves fine-tuning LLMs, which is relevant to generative media.

items.title: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
items.details: Kaixin Ding, Xi Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhiyuan Xu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces PlayWorld, a benchmark designed to evaluate video world models through multi-modal Agent Players interacting with specified long-horizon objectives across 171 scenarios. This approach addresses the limitations of fixed action-conditioned evaluations by assessing models on geometry consistency, interaction fidelity, out-of-sight evolution, and insight evolution, revealing that current state-of-the-art models struggle with maintaining spatial consistency and persistent state evolution. The benchmark aims to provide a more comprehensive evaluation framework for comparing generative models in interactive settings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/kxding/PlayWorld.
items.judge: The paper benchmarks world models with agent players, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation
items.details: Minghui Guo, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei · cs.CV
items.summary: V-RAE introduces a novel video representation autoencoder that leverages frozen vision foundation model representations to create compact generative latents, significantly enhancing semantic organization in video generation. It achieves a reconstruction FVD (rFVD) score of 2.13 on K600, outperforming existing large-scale pretrained video VAEs, and demonstrates improved generation metrics with gFVD scores of 117.86 and 19.16 on UCF101 and K600, respectively, while converging up to 6x faster. Additionally, V-RAE introduces a new temporal-coherence diagnostic (tFVD) that better correlates with generative utility, highlighting the importance of semantic representation in video modeling tasks.
items.judge: The paper proposes a new video representation autoencoder for improved latent space generation.

items.title: AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling - Full Technical Report (v1.1)
items.details: AlayaWorld Team, Kaipeng Zhang, Chuanhao Li, Yifan Zhan et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: The report presents an updated version of AlayaWorld, enhancing long-horizon world modeling through significant revisions in conditioning signal representation and integration. Key improvements include the introduction of a streaming 3D point-cache renderer, replacing the previous depth-warping spatial memory, and a redesigned conditioning pipeline that encodes visual conditions in a causal-VAE latent space, ensuring better alignment with generated video temporal statistics. These changes aim to improve the model's coherence and responsiveness in generating interactive environments.
items.judge: This report focuses on interactive long-horizon world modeling, relevant to generative video and world models.

items.title: SNM-VFI: Symmetric Nonlinear Motion-Guided Generative Video Frame Interpolation
items.details: Jisoo Jeong, Hong Cai, Jamie Menjay Lin, Hanno Ackermann et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces SNM-VFI, a training-free framework for generative video frame interpolation that leverages pre-trained optical flow and video diffusion models to enhance motion control and perceptual realism. By utilizing a symmetric nonlinear motion model to create multi-frame flow-based intermediate frames and confidence maps, SNM-VFI significantly improves output quality, achieving competitive results on benchmarks like DAVIS, Sintel, and KITTI, with enhanced temporal coherence and reconstruction accuracy.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel framework for motion-controllable generative video frame interpolation.

items.title: Evaluation of Clinically Steerable Retinal Image Generation from Foundation Model Latent Spaces
items.details: Zuzanna A. Wakefield-Skórniewska, Bartłomiej W. Papież · cs.CV
items.summary: This study evaluates four retinal foundation models for their ability to generate clinically relevant images while preserving demographic and clinical information in latent representations. The authors demonstrate that these models outperform conventional latent diffusion methods on downstream prediction tasks, although a significant synthetic-to-real representation gap is identified when classifiers are applied to real images. This highlights the potential of foundation model latent spaces for controllable retinal image synthesis, while also emphasizing the need for improved alignment with real-world data.
items.judge: The paper evaluates controllable image generation from medical foundation models, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation
items.details: Hmrishav Bandyopadhyay, Xuanchi Ren, Zijian Huang, Jay Zhangjie Wu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Context-Matched Distillation (CMD), a novel framework for autoregressive video generation that improves teacher-student alignment by employing a causal teacher for supervision, which evaluates targets without future frame access. This approach enhances the consistency of causal information across training and inference, leading to state-of-the-art performance on short- and long-video benchmarks, with significant improvements in adherence to time-varying camera controls. CMD's design choices, including Prefix Scoring and Prefix Corruption, further stabilize training and align supervision with the student's rollout context.
items.judge: The paper discusses autoregressive video generation and distillation techniques relevant to generative media.

items.title: Sign Language Video Synthesis via Loss-Guided Multi-Expert GANs
items.details: Dingzhan Nong, Zhihao Ren, Ziqi Li, Tim Lo · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: This report introduces a novel framework for sign language video synthesis using a loss-guided multi-expert GAN, which employs three specialized discriminators to enhance feature specialization without explicit diversity losses. The proposed United Loss mechanism stabilizes training dynamics, while a dual-pathway convolutional-transformer design optimizes performance, achieving PSNR scores of 29.8 and 30.7 for 0.2B and 1.3B parameter variants, respectively, on a custom dataset. The system's architecture allows for deployment on consumer-grade hardware, with a focus on improving communication for individuals with hearing impairments.
items.judge: Presents a framework for sign language video synthesis using GANs.

items.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
items.details: Yuanyang Yin, Gongxuan Wang, Yifan Zhan, Chuanhao Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Alaya-EVOKE, a generative model that externalizes persistent world state and redesigns the teacher for long-horizon interactive generation, achieving linear growth in memory and compute. By utilizing a camera-indexed world state bank and a novel sparse attention mechanism, Evoke improves long-term coherence and responsiveness in generated sequences, achieving state-of-the-art performance on WBench and competitive results on VBench-Long and VBench-2.0. The model generates 1.5-second video chunks in 2.11 seconds on a single H200 GPU at a resolution of 384x640, enabling open-ended, evolving generation.
items.judge: The paper discusses interactive world models with long-horizon generation capabilities.

items.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
items.details: Yuxuan Zhang, Haozhong Xiong, Jiayi Song, Jinpeng Yu et al. · 11 HF upvotes
items.summary: UniSwap introduces a novel framework for streaming joint audio-visual identity replacement in talking videos, achieving improved audio-visual consistency by integrating appearance and vocal timbre transfer within a single audio-visual diffusion transformer. The method employs a swap-and-reconstruct pipeline to address the lack of aligned training pairs and utilizes techniques such as In-context Pretraining and Efficient Self-forcing DMD to reduce denoising steps from 30 to 3 per block, enhancing efficiency and synchronization. Experiments show that UniSwap maintains strong identity preservation and supports stable long-form generation.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for audio-visual identity swapping in talking videos, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
items.details: Yuxuan Zhang, Haozhong Xiong, Yubo Huang, Jiayi Song et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: LiveAnimate introduces a novel approach for real-time, long-form human animation using a 14B-parameter video Diffusion Transformer, achieving 19.63 FPS streaming inference on two NVIDIA H100 GPUs. The system employs a two-stage training pipeline and a Pose-Retrieval Sink Attention mechanism to maintain consistent appearance and identity over extended streams without excessive memory usage, significantly improving upon prior methods that require hours of computation and suffer from quality degradation over time. This work sets a new standard for interactive full-body animation in terms of quality, latency, and duration.
items.judge: The paper presents a real-time human animation system, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
items.details: Vsevolod Skorokhodov · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: PixSDS introduces a novel gradient repair method to address the issue of structured color artifacts and high-frequency texture noise in latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) for text-to-3D generation. By leveraging a VAE-consistent decoding step, PixSDS effectively reduces pixel-space motion in VAE-inconsistent directions, leading to a significant decrease in visible artifacts while maintaining semantic integrity. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in both 2D optimization and text-to-3D generation tasks, with the code available for public use.
items.judge: The work addresses issues in text-to-3D generation, which is a primary focus area.

items.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
items.details: Dingyi Rong, Yue Shi, Chaofan Ma, Jiezhang Cao et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: H2R-Bench introduces a novel benchmark for evaluating the generation of robot manipulation videos from human demonstrations, addressing the challenge of cross-embodiment transfer in video world models. It systematically assesses generated videos across five dimensions, including goal-state completion and embodiment correctness, revealing that existing models struggle with embodiment consistency and functional interaction. The benchmark facilitates the evaluation of eleven state-of-the-art video generation models, highlighting the limitations in their ability to effectively translate human manipulation into robotic contexts.
items.judge: The paper discusses benchmarking video generation in world models, relevant to generative video.

items.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
items.details: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: The AVA-Encoder introduces a novel framework for agent-native video representation learning by transforming videos into knowledge graph representations, which are then reconstructed back into video. This approach improves video reconstruction accuracy by 20.7 percentage points over the best existing baseline and reduces system-prompt token usage by 74.3% in a controlled policy setting. The framework, along with a benchmark for agentic video reconstruction and a dataset of high-quality film KG representations, is made publicly available.
items.judge: The paper discusses a framework for learning video representations, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: An AI4AI Framework for Visual Token Pruning
items.details: Zhen Liu, Wenli Huang, Wei Song, Yuhan Liu et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces AutoPrune, a training-free framework for LLM-driven visual-token pruning that significantly enhances the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). By utilizing a Token Pruning Domain-Specific Language (TPDSL) with 131 reusable components, AutoPrune achieves a 9.9x reduction in FLOPs and a 6.4x decrease in prefill latency while maintaining over 99% performance with 94.4% of visual tokens removed across 14 benchmarks and three MLLM architectures. This approach addresses the challenges of manual design in pruning by leveraging LLMs to automate the creation of effective pruning policies.
items.judge: The paper discusses visual-token pruning for multimodal models, relevant to inference in generative contexts.

items.title: ReRound: Reconstructive Rounding to Resolve Midpoint Ambiguity in Calibration-Free LLM Quantization
items.details: He-Yen Hsieh, H. T. Kung · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: ReRound introduces a novel post-training quantization method that leverages a conditional diffusion model to resolve midpoint ambiguity in standard round-to-nearest quantization for low-bit weights in LLMs. By integrating a tolerance metric to guide the rounding direction based on proximity to quantization midpoints, ReRound consistently outperforms traditional RTN methods for 3-bit and 4-bit quantization across various smaller LLMs, achieving superior accuracy compared to both calibration-free and calibration-dependent approaches while maintaining offline operation without additional inference overhead.
items.judge: The paper presents a quantization method that could be relevant for improving inference in generative models.

items.title: upscayl/upscayl
items.details: `typescript` · 48,246★ · 180 stars today
items.summary: Upscayl is a free and open-source AI image upscaler that operates on Linux, MacOS, and Windows, designed to enhance image resolution while preserving detail. It utilizes advanced generative techniques to improve image quality, making it a practical tool for researchers and developers in the field of generative models. Notable design choices include a user-friendly interface and support for multiple AI backends, allowing for flexibility in processing.
items.judge: This is an open-source AI image upscaler, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo

items.title: Qwen 3.8 27B is out: open weights, best local dense model yet

items.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
items.details: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun et al. · cs.CV cs.CL
items.summary: The AVA-Encoder introduces a novel framework for learning agent-native video representations by transforming videos into knowledge graph (KG) representations, achieving a 20.7 percentage point improvement over existing baselines. It employs a textual-gradient optimization framework that allows for natural-language feedback to refine video reconstructions, while also reducing system-prompt token usage by 74.3% compared to human-tuned policies. The authors provide the complete AVA-Encoder framework and a new dataset of high-quality film KG representations for further research.
items.judge: The proposed AVA-Encoder focuses on agent-native video representation learning, which is crucial for generative video models.

items.title: XYZFlow:Scaling Multi dimensional Shortcut Flows for Efficient Generative Modeling
items.details: Jinxiu Liu, Xuanming Liu, Kangfu Mei, Yandong Wen et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: XYZFlow introduces a novel framework for efficient generative modeling by employing multidimensional scaling of flow matching, significantly enhancing expressivity and learnability of probability paths. It achieves state-of-the-art performance with 7.2-8.5X speedups over teacher models while maintaining competitive FID scores. The method incorporates temporal scaling through non-Markovian conditioning and spatial scaling via Next Shortcut Prediction, which improves quality-latency trade-offs compared to traditional model scaling or step reduction approaches.
items.judge: The paper introduces XYZFlow, a framework for efficient generative modeling, focusing on image generation.

items.title: GeoFlow: Efficient Driving Video Generation via Geometry-Aligned Priors
items.details: Jiazheng Liu, Hang Li, Jiawei Zhang, Jiahe Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: GeoFlow introduces a novel framework for efficient driving video generation by utilizing Geometry-Aligned Priors (GAP) instead of the conventional Gaussian noise initialization. This approach leverages multi-view geometry and spatially-adaptive noise injection, resulting in a significantly shorter sampling trajectory and improved efficiency in both training and inference. Experiments show that GeoFlow enhances few-step generation quality after only a few hours of fine-tuning and reduces the number of inference steps required for state-of-the-art video generation.
items.judge: This work addresses efficient video generation using generative models, directly related to generative media.

items.title: TGRHuman: Text-Guided Realistic 3D Human Generation via Diffusion Renderer
items.details: Muxin Zhang, Chaohui Yu, Yuanwang Yang, Min Wei et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: TGRHuman introduces a novel method for generating realistic 3D humans from text by decoupling geometry and texture generation, which improves both quality and efficiency compared to existing NeRF-based approaches. The method employs explicit multi-view observation generation and a diffusion renderer, achieving high-quality, consistent 3D human geometry and texture synthesis. Experimental results demonstrate that TGRHuman significantly outperforms prior text-to-3D human generation methods in both aspects.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for generating realistic 3D humans from text, aligning with generative image and 3D generation.

items.title: Avatar-Forever: Decoupled Parallel Training for High-Quality Real-Time Infinite Avatars
items.details: Ruibin Li, Tao Yang, Zhiyuan Ma, Fangzhou Ai et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: Avatar-Forever introduces a decoupled parallel training framework that enhances real-time infinite avatar generation by independently optimizing generation efficiency and long-horizon robustness. This approach utilizes full-parameter distillation for high-quality output and a lightweight long-horizon adapter via Recovery-oriented Rollout Training (RRT), resulting in improved robustness during extended inference. The system achieves an end-to-end throughput of 27.2 FPS for high-resolution 768x512 videos on a single H100 GPU, significantly advancing the capabilities of digital human generation.
items.judge: The paper addresses long-video generation and training techniques relevant to generative video models.

items.title: StateFlow: Building, Evolving, and Accessing 3D World States for Previsualization
items.details: Yuyang Yin, Zixiang Li, Longxuan Deng, Hongkai Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: StateFlow introduces a state-centric framework for generative previsualization that enhances controllability and iterative editing in 3D scene creation. By maintaining a persistent structured 3D state of scene elements and camera configurations, it allows for efficient state construction, evolution, and access, significantly improving the quality of generated 3D worlds for video and game prototyping. The framework employs dual-view initialization and structured state transitions to minimize full-scene regeneration, leading to more coherent and visually feasible outputs.
items.judge: The paper discusses building and evolving 3D world states for previsualization, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: Agentic Optimization for Image-to-Video Adherence
items.details: Aman Tyagi, Hemanth Boinpally, Jonathan Chen, Douglas Gebert et al. · cs.CV cs.AI cs.MM
items.summary: The paper introduces the "Agentic Self-Improvement" framework for Image-to-Video (I2V) synthesis, which enhances control and reliability in video generation by employing a two-stage optimization process. This approach utilizes a multimodal Large Language Model for iterative prompt refinement and Bayesian optimization for co-optimizing stochastic seeds and CFG scales, resulting in a significant improvement in user preference, with generated videos achieving win rates of up to 69% over baseline methods. The framework aims to transition I2V models from trial-and-error processes to a more systematic, goal-directed optimization, making them more suitable for professional applications.
items.judge: The paper addresses challenges in Image-to-Video models, focusing on improving control and reliability in generative workflows.

items.title: Understanding Why Foundation Models Work for Diffusion-Generated Image Detection
items.details: Davide Cozzolino, Giovanni Poggi, Luisa Verdoliva · cs.CV
items.summary: This study investigates the mechanisms behind the effectiveness of foundation models in detecting diffusion-generated images, revealing that detection relies on non-semantic low-to-mid frequency distributional discrepancies rather than high-frequency artifacts. The authors employ a novel analysis protocol using DDIM inversion to demonstrate that subtle traces from diffusion synthesis significantly influence detector scores, despite semantic similarity. Their findings highlight the reduced variance and effective dimensionality in regenerated images, suggesting that current generative models do not fully capture the variability of real data, thus informing future forensic methods.
items.judge: The paper investigates the effectiveness of foundation models for detecting AI-generated images, relevant to generative image evaluation.

items.title: AutoWorldModel-Bench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Automated World-Model Research
items.details: Marjan Moodi, Xuankang Zhu, Fernando De Mesentier Silva, Harold Chaput et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces AutoWorldModel-Bench, a novel closed-loop benchmark designed for automated world-model research, enabling coding agents to autonomously enhance a starter world model within a fixed compute budget across eight game environments. Notably, the benchmark utilizes a unified structured-state representation to decouple dynamics modeling from perception, allowing for rapid iterations; results show that Codex-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 improved their models in 63 out of 64 sessions, with 91% of successful modifications being significant research-style changes rather than mere hyperparameter adjustments. This framework facilitates the evaluation of coding agents on open-ended research challenges, contrasting with traditional engineering-focused benchmarks.
items.judge: Introduces a benchmark for world modeling, directly relevant to generative models.

items.title: From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection
items.details: Zepeng Wang, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Yuxuan Chen et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces a novel closed-loop framework for video reflection removal, combining physics-grounded reflection simulation with a diffusion-based dereflection model. The S2R-Synthesis pipeline generates paired reflected and reflection-free videos, effectively modeling glass-related effects, while the S2R-Removal model achieves state-of-the-art performance in video reflection removal with faster inference than non-diffusion methods. Additionally, the authors present S2R-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating video reflection removal, facilitating both full-reference and perceptual assessments.
items.judge: Presents a framework for video reflection removal, relevant to video generation and editing.

items.title: 360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents
items.details: Kenta Watanabe, Atsuyuki Miyai, Mizuki Takenawa, Kiyoharu Aizawa et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: The 360CityArena benchmark introduces a photorealistic urban navigation environment for evaluating embodied agents, constructed from 602 360-degree video segments of Tokyo's Akihabara district. It features 175 human-crafted tasks across Environment Understanding, Path Reasoning, and Spatial Reasoning, highlighting significant challenges in urban exploration, as evidenced by the performance gap between human navigators (77.3%) and the best model tested, Gemini 2.5 Flash (17.1%). This benchmark aims to bridge the gap between existing outdoor benchmarks and real-world urban complexity, providing a rigorous testbed for future advancements in embodied navigation.
items.judge: The benchmark for urban exploration capabilities of embodied agents relates to world models and evaluation.

items.title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.details: Guiyu Zhao, Longteng Guo, Yanghong Mei, Zilin Zhu et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: AtlasVLA introduces a dual-memory architecture for Vision-Language-Action models that enhances performance in partially observable and long-horizon tasks by transitioning from reactive to proactive reasoning. It employs a 4D Persistent World State Memory and an Ego-Working State Memory to mitigate perception and task-progress forgetting, achieving state-of-the-art results with a single wrist-mounted camera. Notably, AtlasVLA outperforms multi-view baselines, achieving absolute success rate improvements of 9.4% on LIBERO-Long and 17.5% in real-world long-horizon tasks.
items.judge: The paper discusses a framework for vision-language-action models, which is relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: Self-Geometry: GT-Free and Plug-and-Play Test-Time Adaptation for Geometrically Consistent 3D Vision Foundation Models
items.details: Seokhyun Youn, Dahyeon Kye, Sung-Ho Bae, Jihyong Oh · 11 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Self-Geometry, a test-time adaptation pipeline that enhances Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) by imposing explicit multi-view geometric constraints using 2D pixel correspondences as pseudo ground-truth. This method integrates Geometric Disentanglement Optimization and Frame Angular-Neighbor sampling, resulting in consistent improvements in pose and geometry estimation across six VFMs and four benchmarks, addressing limitations of previous implicit self-consistency approaches.
items.judge: This work on 3D vision foundation models relates to generative 3D media.

items.title: NVIDIA-NeMo/Automodel

items.summary: NVIDIA-NeMo's Automodel is a PyTorch-based distributed training library designed for large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), offering out-of-the-box (OOTB) support for Hugging Face models. It enhances training efficiency and scalability by integrating advanced parallelism techniques, enabling researchers to leverage multi-GPU setups effectively. The library aims to streamline the training process, making it more accessible for users familiar with the Hugging Face ecosystem.

items.title: index-tts/index-tts

Notably, it leverages advanced neural architectures to achieve industrial-level performance, making it suitable for diverse applications while maintaining low computational overhead. items.title: MirrorWorld: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Mirror Reflection Generation
items.details: Youjun Zhao, Alex Warren, Gary K. L. Tam, Rynson W. H. Lau · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces MirrorWorld, a novel video inpainting framework specifically designed for generating mirror reflections in video diffusion models (VDMs). It employs two key techniques: Semantic Relation Distillation (SRD) for modeling the content to be reflected and Geometric Transformation Alignment (GTA) for spatial arrangement, resulting in improved reflection reconstruction quality compared to existing image-based methods and video inpainting baselines. The authors also provide a benchmark for video mirror reflection generation by unifying four existing datasets into a single task.
items.judge: The paper addresses video diffusion models for generating mirror reflections, a significant contribution to generative video models.

items.title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
items.details: Daeun Lee, Jaeah Lee, Woosung Kim, Haebeom Jung et al. · 32 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents a novel approach for articulated object reconstruction from a single closed configuration, addressing the challenge of recovering 3D geometry and kinematic structures without observable motion. By integrating a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses and employing an explicit mesh for cross-model verification, the framework achieves accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, outperforming existing motion-observing and generation-based methods. The results demonstrate competitive performance against various baselines, indicating significant advancements in reconstructing articulated objects in static settings.
items.judge: The reconstruction of articulated objects relates directly to 3D generation techniques.

items.title: Ex-Omni-2D: Expressive Omni-Modal Dialogue Models with Native Visual Presence
items.details: Haoyu Zhang, Zhipeng Li, Xiaoying Tang, Tianshu Yu et al. · 9 HF upvotes
items.summary: Ex-Omni-2D introduces a novel omni-modal dialogue framework that generates coordinated responses integrating text, personalized speech, and reference-conditioned video, significantly enhancing the visual presence of dialogue models. The model employs a structured Visual Thought Plan (VTP) to predict scene, emotion, and motion, and utilizes a shared acoustic-temporal interface for real-time alignment of speech and video, achieving an end-to-end real-time factor (RTF) of 1.293 with a four-step inference process. This design allows for efficient incremental generation without extensive supervision across modalities, leveraging a distilled Streaming Student model for improved performance.
items.judge: This work introduces an omni-modal dialogue framework that generates coordinated responses including video, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds
items.details: Zihao Liu, Xiaolong Shen, Zhenglin Zhou, Ruijie Quan et al. · 99 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Latent-to-4D, a novel method for synthesizing dynamic 3D scenes directly from video latents using a shared variational autoencoder (VAE), which improves upon existing methods by eliminating distribution mismatch and error propagation. Trained on approximately 1,000 reconstruction clips, Latent-to-4D achieves a significant performance boost over matched Wan+4RC cascades, with improvements of 2.88–3.45 points on Text4D-200 and 5.81 points on I4D-200 in projection-based DINO-F1 metrics, while also receiving higher preference ratings from human evaluators for geometry and temporal stability.
items.judge: The paper addresses 4D generation of dynamic 3D scenes, relevant to generative video and 3D models.

items.title: Beyond Starry Night: Shortcut-Aware Control-State Planning for Artist-Grounded Text to Image Generation
items.details: Kuan Xing, Ye Wang, Changyi Gan, Yuheng Li et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Atelier, a novel shortcut-aware control-state planning framework for artist-grounded text-to-image generation, which enhances the fidelity of artist-specific styles and reduces shortcut substitutions in generated images. By translating underspecified artistic intent into explicit control states and leveraging artist-level knowledge, Atelier significantly improves performance over existing methods, as demonstrated through the ArtIntentBench benchmark. The framework shows marked improvements in style fidelity and structural preservation across various generative models, addressing key limitations in current artist-grounded generation techniques.
items.judge: The paper introduces a framework for artist-grounded image generation, directly related to generative image models.

items.title: AdvFD: Boosting Visual Generation via Adversarial Fr'echet Distance Loss
items.details: Mingju Gao, Jingkai Zhou, Kun Gai, Changqian Yu et al. · 16 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Adversarial Fréchet Distance (AdvFD), a novel approach that enhances visual generation by integrating a learnable adversarial representation with the traditional Fréchet distance loss. This method addresses the limitations of static pretrained feature spaces, leading to improved visual quality and alignment in generated samples. Experimental results demonstrate that AdvFD significantly enhances one-step generator post-training across various model architectures and scales, outperforming conventional methods.

items.title: World Tokens: Enhancing Embodied Policies with Training-Time World Modeling

items.summary: The paper introduces World Tokens, a novel embodied policy architecture that integrates world modeling during training to enhance action prediction while maintaining efficient deployment. The architecture achieves competitive performance using a 2B backbone without requiring embodied action pretraining, enabling action generation at VLA-level latency.

items.title: Open Evaluation Agent: Efficient and Promptable Evaluation of Visual Generative Models

The framework demonstrates effective performance across various text-to-image and text-to-video benchmarks, showcasing partial cross-family transfer of learned policies.

items.title: Energy-Structured Latent World Models with Neural Time Fields for Physically Constistent Open-World Motion Planning

This approach, combined with Physics-Conditioned Neural Time Fields (PC-NTF), achieves a 19.4% improvement in navigation success (from 81.3% to 89.7%) and reduces motion-prediction NRMSE from 0.36 to 0.29, while significantly lowering the physical collision rate from 12.1% to 5.8%. items.title: MedPixel: A Unified Pixel-Language Model for Medical Reasoning and Segmentation

The model employs joint multi-task supervised fine-tuning and Pixel-Level Preference Optimization, resulting in improved performance across various tasks such as explicit grounding and medical visual question answering, with demonstrated robustness to imperfect spatial prompts. items.title: Perception Before Supervision: Self-Contained Visual Distillation from Counterfactual Blind Spots

This method operates without reliance on external annotations or stronger models, marking a significant advancement in self-improvement techniques for MLLMs.

items.title: Enfold: Folding World Model Imagination into Predictive Representations for Ultra-Efficient Embodied Control
items.details: Weili Zeng, Yitong Xing, Fulong Liu, Chengqun Yang et al. · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents Enfold, a novel approach that internalizes the computation of world generative models into predictive representations, enabling ultra-efficient embodied control. By leveraging multi-level states from a generator during training, Enfold reduces action latency by 3.7 times compared to Fast-WAM and achieves up to 10.1 times reduction with Enfold-Flash, while effectively adapting to changes in the current scene without relying on fixed trajectory replay. This method enhances control performance across various tasks, demonstrating that the internal structure of a world generator can be utilized for predictive control without materializing future states at every step.

items.title: What to Edit Next: Visually Aligned Image-Editing Follow-Up Suggestions in Conversational Systems

This approach combines human-reviewed intents, user feedback optimization, and a visual verifier to improve the quality of recommendations significantly.

items.title: MMOOC: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Out-of-Context Evaluation in Multimodal Large Language Models

Initial evaluations reveal that current MLLMs struggle with balancing answerability and refusal in these contexts, highlighting the need for further improvements through post-training techniques.

The model employs learnable bridge tokens to represent candidate correspondences and outputs text and image masks along with correspondence presence scores.

items.title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching

This approach allows for efficient handling of long-context workloads, maintaining performance with a reduced memory footprint.
