items.judge: This study on self-distillation methods for LLMs has potential applications in generative media.

items.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
items.details: ZhiYan Hou, Xinyu Tang, Hongyan An, Jianjin Zhang et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons (DASH), which enhances on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by adapting token-level supervision weights based on the temporal context of local divergences during autoregressive generation. This approach allows for more effective utilization of the temporal structure of rollouts, leading to improved reasoning capabilities across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with consistent performance gains observed at all model scales without requiring additional forward passes. The implementation is available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The paper addresses reinforcement learning techniques that could be applicable to generative media.

items.title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models
items.details: Andrey Shutkin, Denis Parkhomenko, Ivan Kirillov, Kirill Chernyshev et al. · 14 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces a family of KVAE tokenizers designed for multimodal generative models, including KVAE-Audio, KVAE-3D, and KVAE-2D, which improve the efficiency and quality of text-conditioned generation across audio, image, and video modalities. Notably, these tokenizers achieve superior reconstruction and generation metrics compared to leading open-source alternatives, with specific enhancements in PSNR, LPIPS, and subjective evaluations. The authors provide comprehensive training details and model selection methods, making the code available for community use at their GitHub repositories.
items.judge: The report on KVAE tokenizers for multimodal generative models is highly relevant to generative media.

items.title: GaussianSelector: Lightweight Human-Guided Object Selection in 3D Gaussian Splatting with Graph Optimization
items.details: Baihan Yang, Tiexin Li, Yuheng Liu, Xin Lin et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: GaussianSelector introduces a training-free framework for lightweight human-guided object selection in 3D Gaussian splatting, achieving competitive selection quality compared to state-of-the-art multi-view methods while significantly reducing the need for dense viewpoint coverage and computational resources. By utilizing sparse user scribbles and a continuity-weighted graph for global energy minimization, it allows for iterative refinement of selections, making it particularly effective for real-world applications in 3D scene editing and asset extraction. The method demonstrates improved efficiency with fewer interaction views required for high-quality results.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for interactive 3D object selection, relevant to generative 3D models.

items.title: SmartMage: Dynamic Modality Orchestration for 3D Scene Understanding
items.details: Yue Zhang, Yingzhao Jian, Yunqiu Xu, Xiaoxiao Sun et al. · 18 HF upvotes
items.summary: SmartMage introduces a novel approach to 3D scene understanding by dynamically orchestrating heterogeneous modalities based on semantic relevance, significantly improving performance on five 3D scene understanding benchmarks. It features a Semantic-guided Modality Adaptive Routing (SMART) module for selecting relevant modalities and a Modality-Aware Gating Expert (MAGE) module for adaptive specialization, leading to state-of-the-art results and competitive performance in RGB-only video understanding tasks. The design allows for more efficient computation and enhanced reasoning by minimizing semantic noise from irrelevant modalities.
items.judge: The paper discusses dynamic modality orchestration for 3D scene understanding, aligning well with generative media.

items.title: FactorJEPA: Factorizing Monolithic Futures into Layout-Agent-Interaction Channels for Crowded and Chaotic Global South Urban Worlds
items.details: Kapil Wanaskar, Gaytri Jena, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: FactorJEPA introduces a novel approach to predictive modeling in densely populated urban environments by decomposing future predictions into layout, entities, and interactions, significantly enhancing future-latent accuracy and robustness to visual evidence. This method achieves a correlation coefficient (rho) between 0.895 and 0.978 across different JEPA backbones, addressing challenges in agent heterogeneity and occlusion. The authors also release the DENSEWORLD-115k dataset, comprising 1,000 hours of diverse urban video data, and provide surgery-trained FactorJEPA checkpoints for further research.
items.judge: The study on world models in urban environments is relevant to generative video and simulation.

items.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
items.details: Yuhao Pan, Haosong Peng, Zhengshen Zhang, Zhengyang Yan et al. · 20 HF upvotes
items.summary: The World-to-Wrist VLA (W2-VLA) model introduces a novel approach to fine-grained robot manipulation by integrating task-conditioned future wrist modeling, which enhances the prediction of wrist movements based on multi-view observations and task instructions. This method significantly improves manipulation accuracy in both single-arm and bimanual settings, achieving over 80 Hz action-generation rates, and is supported by a structured annotation pipeline (W2-CoT) that enriches the model's contextual understanding. Experiments on datasets like LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 validate its effectiveness in contact-sensitive tasks.
items.judge: The paper presents a vision-language-action model for robot manipulation, which has implications for world modeling.

items.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.details: Zishan Xu, Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Chen, Yifu Guo et al. · 33 HF upvotes
items.summary: EnvACE introduces a novel agentic reinforcement learning method that replaces traditional external environment interactions with a technique called world rehearsal, allowing the policy to generate tool calls and simulate environment responses internally. This approach leads to improved decision-making and policy learning, achieving superior performance across multiple benchmarks (BFCL-v4, tau^2-Bench, VitaBench, and FinMCP-Bench) compared to environment-scaling baselines. The method demonstrates significant gains in training efficiency and effectiveness, particularly under a moderate rehearsal budget, and the code is available at https://github.com/Within-yao/EnvACE.
items.judge: The paper introduces a reinforcement learning method that involves world rehearsal, relevant to generative models.

items.title: GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?
items.details: Qifeng Zhang, Kaixiang Huang, Heng Dong, Huang Fang et al. · 36 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces the Global-Spatial-Temporal Benchmark (GST-Bench), a novel video question-answering benchmark designed to evaluate global spatial awareness in visual language models (VLMs) using 6,790 minutes of synthetically generated video. It reveals a significant performance gap, with the best zero-shot VLM achieving only 42.68 compared to a human score of 79.08, highlighting the models' inability to integrate long-horizon observations into a coherent global scene representation. Additionally, the authors provide GST-Train, a dataset aimed at enhancing global spatial reasoning capabilities in future research.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark for global spatial awareness in video understanding, relevant to vision-language models.

items.title: Learning from Failures: Retrieval-Centric CoT via Hard Negatives for Unified Multimodal Retrieval
items.details: Zelong Sun, Jun Wang, Kaicheng Yang, Tiancheng Gu et al. · 30 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces UniME-R1, a novel embedder-adviser framework for unified multimodal retrieval that enhances retrieval performance by generating Retrieval-Centric Chain-of-Thought (RC-CoT) based on feedback from initially retrieved candidates. By employing hard negatives to simulate realistic retrieval failures and optimizing both direct and RC-CoT-augmented retrieval, UniME-R1 significantly improves retrieval accuracy on benchmarks like MMEB-V2, outperforming existing strong baselines.
items.judge: The paper discusses multimodal retrieval using vision-language models, which is relevant to generative media.

items.title: heygen-com/hyperframes
items.details: `typescript` · 40,052★ · 158 stars today
items.summary: The Hyperframes repository provides a framework for generating videos from HTML content, specifically designed for use in agent-based applications. It allows for the seamless integration of web technologies with video rendering, enabling dynamic content creation. Notably, it emphasizes modular design choices to facilitate easy customization and scalability for various use cases in generative media.
items.judge: This item involves rendering video, which relates to generative video models.

items.title: jordanrendric/claude-video-vision
items.details: `typescript` · 1,157★ · 22 stars today
items.summary: The repository "jordanrendric/claude-video-vision" introduces a plugin for Claude that enables video comprehension through frame extraction and multimodal audio analysis. This enhancement allows the model to process and interpret video content, potentially improving its performance in tasks requiring understanding of dynamic visual and auditory information. Notable design choices include the integration of both visual and audio modalities, which may lead to richer contextual understanding compared to traditional text-based models.
items.judge: This project involves multimodal analysis of videos, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: MASS: Multiplayer World Models with Authoritative Shared State
items.details: Ziqi Cai, Siqi Yang, Yimu Wang, Zixian Gao et al. · cs.CV cs.HC
items.summary: The paper introduces MAS (Multiplayer World Models with Authoritative Shared State), which improves scalability and consistency in multiplayer environments by disentangling world dynamics from view-dependent visual latents. This approach utilizes a learned Logic Engine for managing a global authoritative state and a Rendering Engine for generating consistent views, achieving superior state accuracy and reduced cross-view inconsistency compared to existing multi-view models on a multiplayer Snake benchmark with 1,024 concurrent players over 10,000 steps. This framework provides a robust foundation for scalable multi-agent world simulation.
items.judge: The paper proposes a multiplayer world model that addresses limitations in video world models, aligning with generative media.

items.title: PRISM: Distribution-Gated Flow Matching for Controllable Unpaired Image Translation
items.details: Elad Yoshai, Natan T. Shaked · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: PRISM introduces a GAN-free flow-matching framework for unpaired image-to-image translation that utilizes a learned per-feature gate to control content preservation and appearance modification, improving upon traditional methods that rely on a single global noise value. This approach allows for more nuanced control during both initialization and transport timing in ODE integration, resulting in superior performance on five benchmarks, achieving the best Inception FID and KID scores on four of them, while also closely matching ideal nuclei counts in histopathology tasks. The framework's flexibility enables local overrides at inference without retraining, enhancing its applicability for various translation tasks.
items.judge: The paper presents a flow-matching framework for controllable image translation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: EmoWorld: A Decoupled Affective Field for Controllable Emotional Video Generation
items.details: Bingyuan Wang, Baistan Zhyldyzbekov, Kunyu Feng, Zeyu Wang · cs.CV
items.summary: EmoWorld introduces a novel framework for controllable emotional video generation by decoupling global atmosphere, semantic cues, and temporal progression within a frozen flow-matching video diffusion transformer (Video DiT). The framework employs Visual Atmosphere Steering (VAS), Semantic Affective Steering (SAS), and Temporal Affective Steering (TAS), achieving significant improvements: VAS enhances target-emotion alignment by 19% and reduces temporal fluctuation by 48%, while SAS boosts alignment by 37% and increases affect-bearing cues by 36%. The method is evaluated across 27 emotion categories and demonstrates compatibility with various Video-DiT backbones, allowing for camera-conditioned composition without altering generator parameters.
items.judge: The EmoWorld framework focuses on controllable emotional video generation, aligning with generative video models.

items.title: TLNM: Externally Validated Tooth Detection, Numbering and Segmentation from Smartphone Photographs Using Mask R-CNN
items.details: Arash Nedaei, Henna Tiensuu, Elina Väyrynen, Saujanya Karki et al. · cs.CV eess.IV
items.summary: The study presents TLNM, a customized Mask R-CNN pipeline for tooth detection and segmentation from smartphone photographs, achieving an instance-mask AP@50 of 0.901 on an external dataset, significantly improving upon the internal test set score of 0.818. The model incorporates domain-informed mechanisms, including a masked gray-world white-balancing algorithm and an anatomically constrained detection layer, to enhance accuracy and reduce false positives. The inference pipeline is available as an open-source, containerized API, facilitating remote dental screening in resource-limited settings.
items.judge: The study involves a model for tooth detection from images, relevant to generative image tasks.

items.title: iARCS: Iterative Agentic RL for Controllable 3D Scene Generation
items.details: Saugat Adhikari, Ashok Prasad Neupane, Pramish Paudel, Ajad Chhatkuli et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces iARCS, an iterative agentic reinforcement learning framework that enhances a pretrained scene generator by aligning it with natural-language task requirements, significantly improving constraint fidelity in synthetic 3D scene generation. The two-stage approach—universal-reward pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning using LLM-generated reward programs—demonstrates effective optimization for walkability, reachability, and clearance tasks, resulting in a more practical tool for generating synthetic data that meets functional constraints. Experimental results indicate that iARCS not only improves constraint adherence but also maintains competitive scene diversity.
items.judge: Involves 3D scene generation using reinforcement learning, relevant to generative media.

items.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
items.details: Sarvesh Baskar, Zikui Cai, Shayan Shabihi, Anirudh Satheesh et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces trace-grounded parametric profiling for event counting in video tasks, addressing the limitations of existing benchmarks that entangle multiple event characteristics. Evaluating 2,190 videos, the authors find that while Gemini 3.6 Flash can reliably count persistent state transitions up to 12 events at 0.5 and 1.0 Hz, it fails to accurately count transient events, achieving only 0.2% correct counts in high-count, high-frequency scenarios. This approach shifts evaluation from aggregate accuracy to a detailed analysis of temporal reasoning failures, highlighting the need for improved event representation in video language models.
items.judge: This work introduces a method for event counting in video tasks, relevant to video generation evaluation.

items.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
items.details: Chenglong Wang, Ziming Zhu, Yifu Huo, Bei Li et al. · cs.LG cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces Ranking-based Reward Construction (RRC), a novel approach that enhances the effectiveness of generative reward models in reinforcement learning by deriving rewards from relative preference rankings rather than scalar scores. RRC employs two strategies: self-competitive ranking, which leverages comparisons among sampled responses, and anchor-guided ranking, which facilitates scalable reward construction using a small set of reference responses. Experimental results show that RRC significantly improves RL training outcomes, outperforming existing reward construction methods across various benchmarks. The implementation is available at https://github.com/wangclnlp/RRC.
items.judge: The paper addresses generative reward models in reinforcement learning, relevant to generative media.

items.title: BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians
items.details: Johann Birnick, Rayan Saab · cs.LG cs.AI
items.summary: BaKron introduces an efficient quantization method for neural networks that leverages two-sided Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations, significantly improving computational efficiency. It reduces the total computational complexity from \(O(m^2n^2)\) to \(O(mn(m+n))\) while maintaining the cubic scaling of existing methods like GPTQ, thus enabling richer curvature information to be utilized in the quantization process. The method is modular, allowing flexibility in the choice of quantizers and Hessian estimators, and includes practical benchmarks demonstrating its effectiveness.
items.judge: The paper discusses quantization techniques that could be relevant for inference acceleration in generative models.

items.title: ContextMaster: Interactive Multi-Shot Video Creation via Fixed-Budget Sparse Context Routing
items.details: Xu Guo, Zhengxuan Wei, Xinghui Li, Hanzhuo Huang et al. · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: ContextMaster introduces a unified model for interactive multi-shot video creation (IMVC) that effectively manages context across multiple operations—generation, reference conditioning, and editing—while maintaining a fixed budget for context routing. It employs a two-stage privileged context distillation framework to enhance task fulfillment and consistency, achieving 16 FPS on a single GPU, outperforming specialized baselines in user studies. The model's design includes reusable clean context states and a ConstraintSink to maintain task constraints, addressing the challenges of sparse context access during inference.
items.judge: The paper presents a unified model for interactive multi-shot video creation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
items.details: Chunchao Guo, Jinpeng Li, Yang Li, Zilong Huang · 42 HF upvotes
items.summary: WorldClaw introduces a novel coarse-to-fine framework for generating large-scale, agentic 3D open worlds from text prompts, significantly enhancing spatial coherence and local content richness. By employing planning agents to create structured specifications and utilizing a combination of semantic layouts and generative materials, WorldClaw achieves coherent scene generation with editable assets, addressing challenges in global terrain consistency and local detail. The system demonstrates improved performance in producing visually compelling and editable 3D environments compared to existing methods.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for generating 3D open-world environments, aligning with generative media.

items.title: Helping Music Co-Creation Agents 'Listen' Well: Hierarchical Self-Supervised World Models for Understanding and Generation
items.details: Scott H. Hawley · 1 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents a hierarchical self-supervised world model for symbolic music, utilizing a 2.55M-parameter Swin V2 encoder trained on MIDI piano-roll images with JEPA-style objectives. Notably, the model achieves a significant improvement in joint chord recovery from 0.18 to 0.54 and key detection from 0.16 to 0.70 through a small chord-supervision head, while also demonstrating high fidelity in pixel reproduction (F1 score of 0.996) and efficient processing times (2.8s on CPU, 0.6s on Apple MPS). This framework enables collaborative music creation agents to effectively understand and generate music while preserving human agency.
items.judge: This work presents a world model for music generation, aligning with generative media.

items.title: EffectLearner: World-Aware Object-Effect Reasoning for Real-World Video Object Removal
items.details: Feier Wu, Wanke Xia, Xu He, Zilang Zhou et al. · 12 HF upvotes
items.summary: EffectLearner introduces a novel framework for video object removal that enhances object-effect reasoning through a combination of a VLM-based Object-Effect Reasoner and a DiT-based Video Eraser. This approach significantly improves the removal of complex object-induced effects in real-world videos, achieving superior performance on the ROSE-Bench and EffectWorld datasets, particularly in challenging scenarios, by employing structured effect-analysis prompts and motion-aware guidance. The framework's design includes a progressive training curriculum that integrates common and complex-effect data, enhancing generalization across diverse scenes.
items.judge: This work addresses video object removal with a focus on high-fidelity restoration, relevant to generative video techniques.

items.title: SIGNPOST-Bench: Benchmarking Text-Vision Conflict Resolution in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.details: Sirun Li, Minghao Liu, Ling Dai, Yong Li et al. · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces SIGNPOST-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate text-vision conflict resolution in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) through a controlled counterfactual approach. It features 5,111 counterfactual groups and 25,555 image variants, revealing that adversarial text variants increase median localization error from 282 km to 1,347 km (a 4.8-fold increase), while demonstrating distinct effects of text replacements on model predictions. This framework allows for a systematic assessment of how MLLMs arbitrate between conflicting visual and textual cues, enhancing understanding of their robustness in real-world applications.
items.judge: The introduction of a benchmark for multimodal models relates to generative media evaluation.

items.title: MameLoshnLM: Yiddish Language Model and Evaluation Benchmark
items.details: Uri Katz, Omer Goldman, Tomasz Limisiewicz, Reut Tsarfaty et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: MameLoshnLM is the first open-source 8B-parameter language model specifically designed for Yiddish, achieving superior performance on a newly introduced multi-task benchmark compared to existing open baselines of similar scale. The model leverages Oytser, a high-quality pretraining corpus that integrates contemporary and literary Yiddish sources, and Kashes, a benchmark that includes tasks such as translation and linguistic analysis. This work highlights the limitations of general-purpose multilingual models for low-resource languages and establishes a framework for advancing NLP in underrepresented linguistic contexts.
items.judge: The release of an open-source Yiddish language model is relevant to LLMs but not directly to generative media.

items.title: Task-Conditional Flow Matching for Balanced Multilingual Text Embedding Adaptation
items.details: Tirth Bhatt, Naren Kumar S, Mayank Singh · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Task-Conditional Flow Matching (TCFM), a novel framework for multilingual text embedding adaptation that optimizes different tasks with tailored objectives, improving embedding quality across diverse multilingual tasks. Evaluated on the Indic Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, TCFM achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating significant enhancements in generalization across embedding model families. The authors plan to release the codebase and datasets upon acceptance.
items.judge: The introduction of a multilingual embedding adaptation framework is relevant to RLHF techniques but not specifically to generative media.

items.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
items.details: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang et al. · 44 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces OSReward, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) as judges of computer-using agent (CUA) trajectories, revealing that even state-of-the-art models exhibit a systematic leniency bias. The authors present OS-Shepherd, an open reward model trained on their newly released OS-Shepherd-100K dataset, which provides reliable reward signals at 30-60% lower costs compared to commercial alternatives. This work aims to enhance the scalability and reliability of reward models in reinforcement learning for CUAs.
items.judge: The paper evaluates computer-using agents with vision-language models, relevant to multimodal evaluation.

items.title: HelloWorld: Enabling Socially Interactive Characters in Video World Models
items.details: Liangyang Ouyang, Ruicong Liu, Xuangeng Chu, Kaipeng Zhang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: HelloWorld introduces a novel video world model that enables real-time social interactions between users and in-world characters, significantly enhancing user engagement. It employs a self-distillation pipeline to finetune video generation on self-synthesized data, allowing for natural interactions without compromising quality. The model outperforms existing baselines in interaction quality and maintains state-of-the-art visual aesthetics, supported by the HelloWorldBench, a comprehensive 400-sample benchmark for evaluation.
items.judge: The paper presents a video world model enabling social interaction, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: OmniEdit-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Instruction-based Video Editing
items.details: Chenxuan Miao, Yutong Feng, Yi Lu, Yunfeng Yan et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces OmniEdit-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for instruction-based video editing (IVE) that addresses limitations in existing benchmarks by incorporating video-specific dimensions such as spatial, temporal, audio, and reference-based editing. It features a novel evaluation framework that assesses editing quality across accuracy, preservation, realism, and consistency, while implementing an accuracy-aware penalty mechanism to enhance instruction fidelity. Extensive experiments reveal that current IVE models are still inadequate, highlighting the need for further advancements in the field.
items.judge: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark for instruction-based video editing, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models
items.details: Bohai Gu, Yueyang Yuan, Taiyi Wu, Dazhao Du et al. · cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: WorldCycle introduces a self-verifiable reinforcement learning framework that utilizes reversible action cycles to mitigate compounding errors in long-horizon video world models. By optimizing spatial closure and temporal consistency rewards, it reduces state returning drift by up to 44% and improves composite-action accuracy nearly 4x compared to the base model. Additionally, the authors provide CycleBench, a benchmark for evaluating state-returning capabilities under complex action sequences, enhancing the robustness of physically grounded world models.
items.judge: The paper addresses reinforcement learning for video world models, relevant to generative video.

items.title: ContextMaster: Interactive Multi-Shot Video Creation via Fixed-Budget Sparse Context Routing
items.details: Xu Guo, Zhengxuan Wei, Xinghui Li, Hanzhuo Huang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: ContextMaster introduces a unified model for interactive multi-shot video creation (IMVC) that effectively manages context across various operations such as generation, reference conditioning, and editing. It employs a role-aware context representation combined with fixed-budget sparse context routing and a two-stage privileged context distillation framework, achieving improved task fulfillment and consistency across shots compared to specialized baselines, while maintaining a processing speed of 16 FPS on a single GPU. This approach addresses the challenges of context access and inference efficiency, making it suitable for practical video creation workflows.
items.judge: The paper presents a model for interactive multi-shot video creation, directly related to generative video.

items.title: VQ-VAD: Vector-quantized Motion Representation Learning for Human-centric Video Anomaly Detection
items.details: Narges Rashvand, Ghazal Alinezhad Noghre, Shanle Yao, Gabriel Maldonado et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces VQ-VAD, a novel framework for Video Anomaly Detection that utilizes vector-quantized motion representations to improve the detection of anomalies in human-centric video data. By adapting Vector-Quantized GAN techniques to keypoint sequences, VQ-VAD constructs a motion codebook based on normal behavior, achieving an in-domain accuracy of 81.83% and effective cross-domain transfer with 76.69% accuracy without retraining. The approach addresses challenges in existing pose-based methods by learning discrete motion patterns, enhancing robustness against visual variability in surveillance footage. The code is available at https://github.com/TeCSAR-UNCC/VQ-VAD.
items.judge: This work on video anomaly detection relates to generative video models through motion representation learning.

items.title: Unleashing the Potential of Vision-Language Models for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
items.details: Weihan Cai, Hao Tan, Zichang Tan, Jun Wan et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Semantic Prototype Calibration (SPC), which enhances the Perception Encoder (PE) for AI-generated image detection, achieving a 4.1% improvement over the DINOv3 baseline in challenging in-the-wild scenarios. By leveraging language-aligned representations to construct category prototypes, PE-SPC demonstrates superior generalization across various benchmarks, establishing itself as the new state-of-the-art in this domain.
items.judge: The study explores the potential of vision-language models for image detection, linking to generative image tasks.

items.title: CoCo-IR: Contextual Composed Image Retrieval
items.details: Shengcao Cao, Tanmaya Shekhar Dabral, Zhongli Ding, Madhuri Shanbhogue et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Contextual Composed Image Retrieval (CoCo-IR), a novel task that allows users to iteratively refine image search results through multi-turn interactions. The authors propose a Large Multimodal Model (LMM) that generates Transformable Image Embeddings (TIE) based on the entire interaction history, achieving state-of-the-art performance with 39.4 mAP@5 on the single-turn CIRCO benchmark and 44.1 R@1 on their new CoCo-IR benchmark for 4-turn dialogues, significantly surpassing existing methods that only support single-turn queries. The model training is enhanced by a scalable data engine that autonomously generates high-quality contextual retrieval data without costly human annotations.
items.judge: The paper discusses a multimodal model for image retrieval, which relates to generative tasks.

items.title: Objects as Audio-Visual Modal Sound Fields
items.details: Zisen Shao, Zihao Wei, Derong Jin, Ruohan Gao · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces the Audio-Visual Modal Sound Field (AV-MSF), a novel representation that reconstructs object-level acoustic properties using only a few impact sound recordings and multi-view images, significantly improving upon existing methods that rely on extensive datasets or costly simulations. AV-MSF leverages 3D Gaussian Splatting and dense visual features to provide a geometry-aware prior, achieving state-of-the-art performance in impact sound rendering on two real-world datasets. The approach also facilitates downstream tasks such as contact localization and object sound editing.
items.judge: The introduction of audio-visual sound fields relates to 3D modeling and generative tasks.

items.title: UniWorld-View: Large-Baseline View Synthesis via Video Diffusion Models
items.details: Haiyang Zhou, Wangbo Yu, Chaoran Feng, Xunyu Zhou et al. · 6 HF upvotes
items.summary: UniWorld-View introduces a novel framework for large-baseline view synthesis from monocular inputs by integrating explicit 3D guidance with generative diffusion modeling, significantly improving geometrical consistency and camera control. The method employs an occlusion-aware point cloud rendering strategy to resolve visibility ambiguities, enabling high-fidelity novel view generation even under extreme camera motions. Experimental results on the WorldScore benchmark demonstrate enhanced controllability and visual fidelity compared to existing reconstruction-based and generative methods.
items.judge: The paper discusses video diffusion models for view synthesis, directly relating to generative video and 3D generation.

items.title: Poly-OPD: Heterogeneous Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability-Selectable Flow Models
items.details: Siming Fu, Haojun Xu, Ruizhe He, Zheming Fu et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Poly-OPD, a novel framework for on-policy distillation that consolidates the strengths of heterogeneous text-to-image models into a single compact flow-matching student model. By utilizing a pixel bridge to reconcile incompatible latent spaces and employing a gradient compatibility diagnostic for adapter organization, Poly-OPD achieves significant performance improvements, raising GenEval scores from 67.3 to 73.3 and DrawBench HPSv3 from 9.34 to 11.35, effectively merging the capabilities of multiple teachers into a switchable model.
items.judge: This work on distillation for flow models directly relates to improving generative image capabilities.

items.title: AVE-Compass: Towards Holistic Evaluation for Audio-Video Editing Abilities
items.details: Yuqing Wen, Yukai Huang, Qianqian Xie, Jiangtao Wu et al. · 15 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces AVE-Compass, a novel benchmark for evaluating audio-video editing capabilities, featuring 145 curated videos and 196 editing instructions that assess Instruction Following, Fidelity Preserving, Realism, and Editing Intent through a comprehensive checklist and automated metrics. The proposed AVE-Agent framework enhances the execution of complex cross-modal editing tasks by decomposing instructions into subtasks and iteratively refining results, demonstrating improved fidelity and audio-visual alignment while maintaining competitive perceptual quality.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark for audio-video editing, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: ToolArtist: Tool-Using Unified Multimodal Models for Agentic Image Generation
items.details: Jiahao Zhao, Xiaomin Yu, Zhongxiang Sun, Fengwei Teng et al. · 45 HF upvotes
items.summary: ToolArtist introduces a fully agentic image generation model that integrates reasoning, external tool use, and image generation into a single unified policy, significantly improving the performance of text-to-image models on open-world tasks. By employing a novel Reason-Act-Draw GRPO (RAD-GRPO) reinforcement learning framework, ToolArtist outperforms existing methods that rely on fixed workflows or partial agent control, demonstrating enhanced semantic understanding and multi-step reasoning capabilities. The authors provide access to the training data and the complete post-training infrastructure, facilitating further research in this area.
items.judge: The paper discusses a multimodal model for agentic image generation, relevant to generative image models.

items.title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report
items.details: Eunbi Choi, Kibong Choi, Sehyun Chun, Seokhee Hong et al. · 10 HF upvotes
items.summary: K-EXAONE 2.0 is a multilingual foundation model developed by LG AI Research, featuring a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 750 billion parameters, significantly increasing capacity by over three times compared to its predecessor. items.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance

items.title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation

items.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit: Real-Time Open-Ended Video Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion

items.title: UniWorld-Design: From Pixel Generation to Layer-Native Design

items.judge: The framework for structured visual composition relates directly to generative image models.

items.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
items.details: Zhen Fang, Yu Zeng, Wenxuan Huang, Yiming Zhao et al. · cs.CV cs.AI

The authors also present Video-DR-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating complex multi-hop visual question answering tasks.

items.title: When and Where to Look: Adaptive Visual Evidence Scheduling for Efficient Long Video Understanding

items.summary: The paper introduces EcoFrame, a training-free framework for adaptive visual evidence scheduling that enhances long video understanding by optimizing frame selection based on output uncertainty and attention-guided proposals. EcoFrame achieves an average accuracy of 64.4 on Qwen2.5-VL, surpassing BOLT's 63.5 while providing a 1.85x speedup over existing methods like AKS and BOLT, and up to a 13.5x speedup compared to agent-based approaches. This framework improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for vision-language models without the need for extensive retraining.
items.judge: Proposes a framework for efficient long-video understanding, relevant to video generation.

items.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment
items.details: Yuanshen Guan, Zipeng Feng, Zhiwei Xiong, Peiqin Sun · cs.LG cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Latent Reward Registers, a novel mechanism for aligning diffusion models with human preferences by estimating terminal rewards from intermediate noisy latents using learnable register tokens. This approach improves the efficiency of reward-guided updates, achieving up to 33x reduction in GPU hours compared to standard policy gradients while enhancing alignment and perceptual metrics. The method demonstrates superior performance at high noise levels, achieving the highest pairwise accuracy among latent reward models and establishing a new state-of-the-art for training-free methods. Code and weights are available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The paper discusses a method for aligning diffusion models with human preferences, relevant to generative media.

items.title: CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement

items.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs

items.title: Assessment of Conditional Diffusion Model for Synthetic Histopathology Image Generation
items.details: Seyed Kahaki, Shijie Li, Weijie Chen, Nicholas Petrick · cs.LG
items.summary: This study introduces modified evaluation metrics for assessing synthetic histopathology images generated by conditional denoising diffusion models, addressing limitations of conventional metrics like FID and IS when applied to medical data. The authors demonstrate that their modified Inception Score shows a significantly higher correlation with downstream nuclei segmentation performance (r=0.6096, p=0.0122) compared to the original IS (r=0.0708, p=0.7944), suggesting that pathology-specific metrics enhance the evaluation of synthetic data quality. Additionally, the findings indicate that increasing the diversity of generated training data is more beneficial for segmentation model performance than merely enhancing the visual fidelity of individual images.
items.judge: The paper addresses evaluation methodologies for synthetic image generation in a medical context.

items.title: MiniWorld: Democratizing the Training of Video World Models from Scratch
items.details: Yian Zhao, Ruochong Zheng, Hongcan Guo, Yu Yan et al. · 9 HF upvotes
items.summary: MiniWorld introduces a novel framework for training video world models from scratch, utilizing a block-causal Video Diffusion Transformer and Flow Matching in the latent space of a pretrained Video VAE. This approach enhances temporal modeling and stability through a chunk-wise non-decreasing noise schedule and two-stage continued training, allowing for efficient streaming generation on modest computational resources, with the entire model trainable in several days on a single 8-GPU server. The release of the training and inference codebase, along with pretrained checkpoints, aims to democratize access to video world modeling research.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for training video world models, which is directly related to generative video models.

items.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?

The authors categorize these proxies into six functional forms and demonstrate their utility across three levels of agent improvement: inference-time guidance, training-time optimization, and agent-proxy co-evolution. This framework aims to enhance the adaptability and learning efficiency of agents by enabling more versatile and dynamic interactions with their environments.
items.judge: The paper discusses world modeling, which is relevant to generative media and agent interaction.

items.title: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0: A Unified Multimodal Model for Scalable 3D Generation, Understanding, and Editing

items.judge: This work presents a unified multimodal model for scalable 3D generation and editing.

items.title: PosterMELD: Multi-Agent Paper-to-Poster Generation for Controllable Design Diversity with Editable Print-Ready Outputs

items.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

PCSD demonstrates effectiveness without requiring inference-time skills, maintaining competitiveness on other benchmarks like WebShop.

Empirical results demonstrate that Coverage is a stronger predictor for understanding tasks, while Precision is more relevant for generation tasks, providing a nuanced framework for optimizing captioning models based on specific downstream applications.

items.title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity

Spanning 1,474 cases across four diagnostic levels, the benchmark reveals a significant capability split among 20 evaluated models: camera-driven models excel in camera control but lack dynamic interaction, action-driven models offer precise subject control but often leave the world unresponsive, and language-driven models perform better in interactions but struggle with complex controls. This highlights the need for models that combine broad task coverage with strong performance across all evaluation dimensions.
items.judge: The paper discusses benchmarking world models in controllable video generation.

This approach enhances the spatial grounding of dynamics tokens, enabling a more effective integration of geometric supervision in action-relevant contexts.
items.judge: The paper discusses world modeling in a geometry-aware policy space, relevant to generative models.

items.title: RL^2-VLA: Adaptive RL Latent Compositional Steering with Test-Time Scaling for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.details: Derek Ming Siang Tan, Shailesh Shailesh, Srikrishna Iyer, William Wei Jie Teo et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces RL^2, an adaptive inference-time steering framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that enhances performance on challenging out-of-domain tasks by up to 17.3% in success rates. It employs a lightweight offline reinforcement learning policy to dynamically adjust action strategies based on predicted success or failure states, optimizing action diversity and mitigating correlated failure modes. This approach combines large-scale imitation learning with adaptive steering, making RL^2 a practical and modular solution for VLA deployment in real-world scenarios.
items.judge: This work on Vision-Language-Action models includes techniques relevant to generative media.

items.title: invoke-ai/InvokeAI

items.summary: InvokeAI is an advanced creative engine for Stable Diffusion models that enhances the generation of visual media through a robust WebUI. It provides a streamlined interface for professionals and artists, facilitating the creation of high-quality images while serving as a foundational tool for various commercial applications. Notably, it emphasizes user accessibility and integration with existing workflows in the creative industry.

items.title: antirez/ds4
items.details: 20,261★ · 385 stars today

Notably, it emphasizes performance improvements in inference speed and resource utilization, making it suitable for real-time applications in generative models. The design choices focus on cross-platform compatibility and leveraging hardware acceleration to enhance computational efficiency.
items.judge: This project involves a local inference engine which may be applicable to generative media.

items.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
items.details: 93 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49154228)
items.summary: AirLLM is an open-source repository that enables inference of a 70 billion parameter language model using a single 4GB GPU, significantly reducing hardware requirements for large model deployment. The implementation leverages quantization techniques and optimized memory management strategies to achieve this efficiency, making it feasible for researchers and developers with limited resources to utilize large-scale LLMs.
items.judge: This item discusses inference acceleration for LLMs, which is relevant to generative media.

items.title: Emily2040/seedance-2.0

items.summary: Seedance 2.0 is a comprehensive production pipeline designed for quad-modal AI filmmaking, integrating generative models for image, video, audio, and text. It enhances the filmmaking process by streamlining the workflow and improving the coherence of multimodal outputs, making it easier for creators to produce high-quality content. The repository includes notable design choices such as modular components for each modality and support for real-time collaboration.
