items.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
items.details: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang et al. · cs.AI cs.CL cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces OSReward, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) as judges of computer-using agent (CUA) trajectories, revealing that even state-of-the-art models exhibit a systematic leniency bias. It presents OS-Shepherd, a set of open reward models (9B and 35B parameters) that provide reliable reward signals at 30-60% lower cost than commercial alternatives. The authors also release a comprehensive dataset of reasoning-annotated trajectory judgments to enhance the reliability of CUA evaluations.
items.judge: The paper discusses vision-language models for evaluating computer-using agents, relevant to multimodal evaluation.

items.title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
items.details: Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Letian Cheng, Zhuoran Zhang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Beacon, a novel agentic visual reasoning model that enhances multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by improving Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect. Beacon employs a Necessity-Aware Adaptive Reward and a Hint-Guided Capability Expansion mechanism during reinforcement learning, leading to significant performance gains on complex tasks while minimizing errors on simpler tasks. Experimental results indicate that Beacon outperforms existing models, demonstrating a more efficient and effective approach to tool use in visual reasoning.
items.judge: The work focuses on improving multimodal reasoning in LLMs, which is relevant to generative media.

items.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
items.details: Kangning Zhang, Yixing Li, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li et al. · cs.CV cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD), a novel counterfactual target-reconstruction algorithm that enhances multimodal on-policy distillation by isolating visually attributable corrections from a teacher model. VAD significantly improves performance across six fine-grained visual benchmarks at 4B and 9B scales, outperforming traditional methods like direct privileged-view distillation and visual-advantage weighting. The method effectively enriches task-relevant visual corrections, leading to stronger target shifts, particularly when visual evidence contradicts incorrect predictions.
items.judge: The paper discusses a multimodal distillation technique, relevant to generative models.

items.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
items.details: Md. Mehrab Hossain Opi, Robiul Islam Ryad, Md. Umar Faruk · cs.CV cs.LG
items.summary: MixFrag introduces a fragility-guided mixed-precision post-training quantization (PTQ) framework for Vision Transformers, significantly improving precision allocation by estimating component-level quantization fragility through KL divergence. This method formulates bit allocation as a Multiple-Choice Knapsack Problem, achieving state-of-the-art performance with up to a 9.6 AP improvement over previous mixed-precision PTQ methods on COCO object detection and instance segmentation tasks. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of MixFrag across various Vision Transformer architectures, demonstrating its competitive classification performance under practical mixed-precision settings.
items.judge: The proposed quantization method is applicable to Vision Transformers, which are relevant for generative image models.

items.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
items.details: Jiawei Xu, Minghui Liu, Juzheng Zhang, Tom Goldstein et al. · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces $β$-OPSD, a novel approach that enhances on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by treating the KL penalty as a controllable parameter rather than a fixed value, allowing for a more flexible trade-off between reference policy adherence and teacher guidance. This method improves optimization stability and downstream reasoning performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, outperforming vanilla OPSD. The authors demonstrate that by mixing token-level logits from the reference and teacher policies, they can efficiently approximate the costly policy optimization process, thus maintaining OPSD's practical efficiency.
items.judge: The paper discusses self-distillation techniques that could be relevant for generative models.

items.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.details: Jiacheng Tao, Qingyun Sun, Haonan Yuan, Ziwei Zhang et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces DualG-MRAG, a novel framework for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation that decouples macro-reasoning and micro-matching through separate Macro and Micro Graphs. This architecture enhances the ability to handle complex multi-hop reasoning tasks by reducing retrieval noise and improving evidence recall, achieving superior performance in complex question answering tasks compared to existing methods. The approach employs a GNN Retriever for dynamic relevance propagation and a dynamic programming decoding mechanism to extract reasoning paths, significantly improving accuracy in multimodal scenarios.
items.judge: The paper addresses multimodal retrieval-augmented generation, which relates to generative models.

items.title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
items.details: Jinsen Su, Yongdong Luo, Yuexiao Ma, Yibo Hu et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: OmniScope introduces a novel token compression framework for omnimodal large language models that decouples relevance estimation for audio and video, addressing the limitations of existing methods that rely on unidirectional guidance. By employing a shared query as a semantic anchor and allocating modality-specific token budgets, OmniScope achieves a 3.53x prefill speedup and over 15% GPU memory reduction at 25% token retention, with only a 0.35-point drop in accuracy across multiple benchmarks. The implementation is available at https://github.com/MAC-AutoML/OmniScope.
items.judge: The paper addresses token compression in omnimodal models, relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes
items.details: Tianyu Wang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenbin Wang, Heng Li et al. · 4 HF upvotes
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of lossy verification in Speculative Decoding (SD) for large language models, revealing that existing methods can lead to significant degradation in generation quality due to distributional distortions. The authors classify lossy verification approaches into truncation-based and collaborative verification methods, identifying critical pitfalls and principles that affect performance. They also introduce a diagnostic evaluation framework to assess these methods across benchmarks, providing insights that could enhance the stability and quality of generative outputs.
items.judge: The focus on inference acceleration techniques is relevant but not directly tied to generative media.

items.title: abus-aikorea/voice-pro
items.details: 11,641★ · 53 stars today
items.summary: The repository "abus-aikorea/voice-pro" provides a Gradio WebUI designed for developers and creators, integrating advanced text-to-speech (TTS) capabilities using Edge-TTS and kokoro, alongside zero-shot voice cloning with E2 & F5-TTS and CosyVoice. It also incorporates Whisper for audio processing, YouTube downloading functionality, Demucs for vocal isolation, and supports multilingual translation, enhancing accessibility and usability for diverse audio generation tasks.
items.judge: The project involves TTS and voice cloning, which relates to generative audio but is not focused on image or video generation.

items.title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers
items.details: Chongjian Ge, Hanwen Jiang, Tianyu Wang, Jiuxiang Gu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: Chimera introduces a hybrid visual diffusion architecture that significantly improves computational efficiency for high-resolution image and video generation by achieving a 1.7x increase in compute efficiency over a baseline model and a 7.3x improvement for the complete system. It employs Kimi Delta Attention for long-context tracking, interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention for global interaction, and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts layers to optimize capacity while controlling compute. The novel HeteroP scaling method allows for effective hyperparameter transfer across model dimensions, facilitating the training of an 11B-parameter model with only 2B activated parameters, while maintaining performance across varying video lengths with minimal degradation.
items.judge: The paper presents a hybrid visual diffusion model for high-resolution image and video generation.

items.title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language
items.details: Shuyao Shang, Yuqi Wang, Ruopeng Gao, Xu Chen et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: PhiZero introduces a novel physical world model that utilizes a compact discrete representation of world-state transitions based on physical language, improving upon traditional pixel-space predictions by explicitly reasoning about physical dynamics. This model employs a reason-then-render paradigm, first generating a sequence of physical-language descriptions to infer future world evolution before rendering these transitions into videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in modeling physically coherent world evolution and highlight its capabilities for realistic interactive simulations and zero-shot motion transfer.
items.judge: The introduction of a physical world model for explicit reasoning is highly relevant to generative media.

items.title: ROAD: Reciprocal-Objective Alignment of Discriminative Semantics for 3D Shape Generation
items.details: Xiao Luo, Mingyang Du, Xin Zhou, Tianrui Feng et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces ROAD, a framework that enhances 3D shape generation by integrating discriminative priors from 3D foundation models into diffusion transformers, significantly reducing training costs. ROAD achieves competitive performance compared to the industrial baseline Step1X-3D using only 1.5% of the training data, while also eliminating additional inference costs by utilizing the foundation model solely for training-time supervision. The framework employs a reciprocal-objective alignment strategy to address semantic-structural differences between generative and discriminative latents, ensuring both global coherence and precise geometric alignment.
items.judge: The paper focuses on 3D shape generation, which is a primary focus area.

items.title: MIND: Multimodal Intent-Driven Network via Diffusion Transformers for Medical Image Fusion
items.details: Yunzhan Fu, Xiangyu Shen, Yifei Sun, Yuhan Chen et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces MIND, a Multimodal Intent-Driven Network utilizing Diffusion Transformers for medical image fusion, which enhances fusion quality by integrating intent-driven fusion texts generated by BioMedGPT. Key innovations include a Multi-scale Latent Adapter that preserves 2D spatial continuity and a medical semantic consistency loss that aligns fused images with diagnostic intents. Experimental results demonstrate that MIND significantly improves brain tumor segmentation accuracy across multiple datasets, indicating its potential for advanced clinical decision support systems.
items.judge: The paper presents a multimodal network for medical image fusion, relevant to image generation.

items.title: What to Remove, What to Preserve: Dual-Ambiguity Rectification for All-in-One Image Restoration
items.details: Cencen Liu, Wen Yin, Dongyang Zhang, Dongmin Li et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces DAR-Net, a Dual-Ambiguity Rectification Network designed for all-in-one image restoration, which addresses the dual ambiguity challenge in existing methods by decoupling degradation-related cues from scene content. It employs a Degradation Archetype Representation module for structured degradation modeling and utilizes Semantic and Spatial Ambiguity Rectification modules to enhance channel-wise conditioning and reduce spatial interference, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that DAR-Net outperforms the leading competitor by an average PSNR improvement of 0.14 dB and 0.34 dB across three-degradation and five-degradation settings.
items.judge: This work addresses image restoration, which is relevant to generative image models.

items.title: ViewMind3D: Modular View-Aware Inference for Training-Free 3D-QA
items.details: Ping-Kun Chiang, Kun-Ru Wu, Po-han Li, Sandeep Chinchali et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: ViewMind3D introduces a modular, training-free framework for 3D question answering (3D-QA) that enhances spatial reasoning using multi-view observations without the need for complete 3D reconstruction. The framework decomposes the task into four components, achieving competitive performance with 50.8% accuracy on SQA3D and 73.4 CIDEr on ScanQA, particularly excelling in spatially grounded questions. This approach leverages general-purpose LLMs and VLMs, facilitating robust reasoning for robotic perception in real-world scenarios.
items.judge: The paper presents a training-free framework for 3D question answering, relevant to 3D generation and multimodal reasoning.

items.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
items.details: Yao Xiao, Reuben Tan, Zhen Zhu, Yuqun Wu et al. · cs.CV cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: ReToken introduces a novel learnable embedding that enhances vision-language models by selecting a sparse set of relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled KV cache, addressing the challenges posed by long visual contexts. This approach leads to significant performance improvements, with gains of 13.4 points on Visual Haystacks for Qwen3VL-8B and 12.4 points for InternVL3.5, translating to over 20% relative improvement, as well as an 8.0-point zero-shot gain on long video tasks. The lightweight design allows both training and inference on a single H100 GPU, and the code is available at the provided GitHub repository.
items.judge: The paper presents a method to improve vision-language models, relevant to generative media.

items.title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
items.details: Jia Yu, Yan Zhu, Yili He, Zilong Wang et al. · cs.AI
items.summary: EndoCLIP is a vision-language foundation model specifically designed for colonoscopy, trained on 125,756 lesion-level image-text pairs derived from 280,476 routine reports. It significantly improves lesion-level image-text retrieval and structured report generation, outperforming both general-purpose and biomedical vision-language encoders in zero-shot and linear-probe settings. Notably, its linear probe for benign-versus-malignant classification nearly matches the performance of expert endoscopists, indicating its potential to enhance clinical documentation and supervision through improved finding-to-frame correspondence.
items.judge: The paper discusses a vision-language model for colonoscopy, which is relevant to multimodal applications.

items.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow
items.details: Jin Cao, Zian Meng, Kaipeng Zhang · 16 HF upvotes
items.summary: ShadowDancer introduces a novel method for frame-level control in interactive video world models by leveraging "shadow pairs" and cross-shadow prediction, allowing for precise action transfer across diverse dynamics without the need for action labels or fine-tuning. This approach significantly enhances action transfer and long action rollout, achieving an average blinded win rate of 86% against existing latent-action and interactive world model baselines. The method utilizes a scalable Shadow Library to construct video pairs that maintain consistent dynamics while varying appearances, enabling the reuse of demonstrated clips in new environments.
items.judge: This paper presents a novel approach to controlling video world models, aligning well with generative video and world model research.

items.title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing
items.details: Jiajia Lin, Mingxuan Du, Tuowen Zhou, Benfeng Xu et al. · 35 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces MPIE-Bench, a benchmark consisting of 2,500 video-mined editing triplets that evaluates multi-person interaction editing in generative models, addressing significant anatomical and geometric failures in current systems. It proposes MPIE-Eval, which scores contact-time geometry using a public multi-person mesh reconstruction, revealing that existing editors achieve a maximum score of 0.65 for anatomy and 0.72 for interaction, while VLM checklists overestimate performance at 0.95. A five-rater study demonstrates that the proposed evaluation axes align more closely with human judgment compared to zero-shot VLM assessments.
items.judge: The paper addresses anatomical issues in multi-person image editing, directly relevant to generative image models.

items.title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models
items.details: Junhan Sun, Hao Zhao, Guofeng Zhang · 11 HF upvotes
items.summary: INTACT introduces a novel end-to-end JEPA framework that enables search-free intent-to-action learning in world models, achieving up to 100% success on specific LeWM tasks with a single training epoch. By leveraging an isomorphic architecture that connects local and goal motion-intent representations, INTACT reduces the need for extensive search during action recovery, achieving a 23.44x reduction in candidate sequences while improving performance metrics significantly. The model's design facilitates robust action law distribution and efficient inference times of 2.9–5.5 ms, enhancing both representation learning and control capabilities.
items.judge: The paper introduces a method for intent-to-action learning in world models, relevant to generative media.

items.title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning
items.details: Tengfei Liu, Yang Shi, Yuran Wang, Xiaohan Zhang et al. · 24 HF upvotes
items.summary: RefCaptioner introduces a novel multi-reference image-grounded video captioning framework that enhances factual video descriptions by grounding local visual elements to multiple reference images. This two-stage post-training approach integrates mixed-data supervised fine-tuning with Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO, significantly improving reference selection and phrase-level binding while maintaining general video-captioning capabilities. The model outperforms existing open-source alternatives and is validated by a newly constructed dataset of 20,000 videos and 171,354 reference images, alongside the MRVBench benchmark for assessing caption factuality and grounding accuracy.
items.judge: The paper introduces a new task in video captioning that involves grounding visual elements to multiple reference images, linking it to generative video models.

items.title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?
items.details: Siyu Yan, Zhuoran Yan, Haiying Xu, Panhao Zhou et al. · 18 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces See2Think, a comprehensive evaluation framework that includes See2ThinkBench and Visual Action-of-Thought (VAoT), designed to assess the reliance of multimodal large language models on intermediate visual states during reasoning. It features 1,200 visually dependent problems across diverse task categories and reveals that visual reasoning effectiveness varies significantly by model and environment, with a notable bottleneck in faithful rendering impacting performance. The study demonstrates that under corrupted feedback conditions, models can experience over a 10 percentage point drop in accuracy, highlighting the critical role of visual states in multimodal reasoning tasks.
items.judge: The paper evaluates multimodal models, which is relevant to generative media.

items.title: Flux-OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Evolving Contexts
items.details: Yuran Wang, Zekun Wang, Bohan Zeng, Ruixu Zhang et al. · 35 HF upvotes
items.summary: Flux-OPD introduces an innovative on-policy distillation (OPD) paradigm that leverages evolving contexts as in-training supervision to better capture task preferences in open-ended domains. By analyzing the reverse KL objective, the authors reveal that the student model is distilled towards the geometric mean of context-conditioned teachers while addressing conflicts through a conflict term. Experimental results demonstrate that Flux-OPD significantly outperforms existing OPD methods, indicating its effectiveness in stabilizing training and enhancing performance in complex tasks.
items.judge: The paper discusses on-policy distillation techniques that could be applicable to generative media training.

items.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model
items.details: Zeyu Zhang, Ziliang Guo, Yihang Sun, Xichong Zhang et al. · 210 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Metis, a novel memory foundation model that integrates native memory capabilities directly into the architecture of foundation models, enhancing their efficiency and optimization. Metis allows for a persistent and dynamically evolving memory state, enabling historical information to be compressed and accessed via memory attention, with a gradient-free online memory maintenance process that requires only a forward pass during updates. Experimental results demonstrate Metis's native memory capabilities, and the authors provide detailed analyses of its performance, along with released project resources for further research.
items.judge: The introduction of memory foundation models relates to advancements in multimodal models, which can include generative aspects.

items.title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation
items.details: Alexi Gladstone, Heng Ji, Yilun Du · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Explorative Modeling (XM), a novel paradigm that factors the training loop instead of the generation procedure, allowing for end-to-end training in generative models. This approach significantly enhances performance, yielding improvements in exploration efficiency—4.1x in FLOP efficiency, 6.2x in sample efficiency, and 47% in parameter efficiency—while achieving a near-state-of-the-art FID score of 1.43 on ImageNet. Additionally, XM enables reconstructive generative modeling that matches diffusion methods with 16-256x fewer inference steps, establishing it as both a new pretraining axis and a standalone generative modeling framework.
items.judge: The paper discusses generative modeling but lacks a clear focus on generative media applications.

items.title: I 4x'd a 367x479 stamp-sized photo through 8 upscaling models
items.details: 6 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49082198)
items.summary: The article compares the performance of eight upscaling models on a 367x479 pixel stamp-sized photo, demonstrating that one model achieved a 4x increase in image quality over others. The analysis highlights differences in detail preservation and artifact reduction, providing quantitative assessments of each model's output. This evaluation can inform ML researchers about the effectiveness of various upscaling techniques in generative image tasks.
items.judge: The work involves upscaling images through multiple models, relevant to generative image processing.

items.title: FreqForcing: Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Spectral Self-Anchoring
items.details: Jiatong Li, Leo Liang, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces FreqForcing, a training-free framework for long video generation that addresses error accumulation by utilizing Spectral Self-Anchoring (SSA). This method effectively stabilizes long-horizon visual quality by anchoring low-frequency components while maintaining dynamic motion through high-frequency components, achieving a 24x extrapolation from 5-second clips to 2-minute videos. Experimental results demonstrate that FreqForcing surpasses existing training-free methods in both quantitative and qualitative measures, while remaining competitive with training-based approaches.
items.judge: The paper focuses on autoregressive video generation, which is a primary topic of interest.

items.title: Mitigating Compounding Error via Video Representation Regularization
items.details: Taiye Chen, Qi Zhang, Yisen Wang · cs.CV cs.LG
items.summary: This paper introduces video representation regularization, a novel training constraint that mitigates compounding error in video diffusion-based world models, which is critical for long autoregressive video generation. The authors demonstrate that their method improves Aesthetic Quality and Imaging Quality metrics on VBench from 38.65 to 55.56 and 44.37 to 72.08, respectively. Additionally, they establish a connection between autoregressive video drifting and the degradation of internal representations, challenging existing paradigms around training data scaling.
items.judge: The paper addresses video representation regularization for improving long autoregressive video generation.

items.title: Mental World Modeling
items.details: Hao Fei, Yiran Zhao · cs.CL
items.summary: The paper introduces Mental World Modeling (MWM), a framework that integrates mental variables into world models, enhancing the predictive accuracy of agent behavior by accounting for beliefs, intentions, and social norms. The authors demonstrate that MWM significantly improves decision prediction in situated scenarios when applied to eight modern LLM-based world models, emphasizing the necessity of incorporating mental states for accurate action forecasting. The framework is instantiated in MENTIS, which offers a training-free, inspectable approach that decomposes the modeling process into several key components, addressing limitations in current mental world modeling techniques.
items.judge: The work on mental world modeling relates to predictive models that can enhance generative capabilities.

items.title: What Can Latent World Models Know? Physical Parameter Identifiability in Multimodal Predictive Representations
items.details: Kaizhen Tan, Xin Xu, Siru Tao, Hanzhe Hong et al. · cs.LG cs.RO
items.summary: The paper presents a novel framework for understanding the identifiability of physical parameters in latent world models through controlled interventions in the POKEWORLD environment. It demonstrates that the ability of a latent representation to internalize physical quantities, such as stiffness and drag, is significantly influenced by the prediction targets used, with stiffness being retained only when touch is forecasted (R²=0.50) versus a null result when merely fused into the input. The findings reveal that objective structure critically determines which physical parameters are acquired, with multimodal objectives outperforming single-modality approaches in predictive accuracy.
items.judge: The paper explores latent world models and their ability to internalize physical parameters, relevant to generative media.

items.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?
items.details: Siyao Li, Jiawei Gu, Shuai Liu, Kairui Hu et al. · cs.CV cs.RO
items.summary: The paper introduces HumanCLAW, an evaluation framework that separates action decision-making from low-level motor execution in vision-language models (VLMs), allowing for the assessment of a model's action intelligence in physical environments. The framework includes HumanCLAW-Bench, which consists of 1,218 long-horizon episodes across 41 indoor scenes, revealing that current state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with embodied self-awareness, achieving a maximum success rate of only 16.8%. This highlights a critical gap in VLM capabilities, particularly in tracking their own physical presence and interactions with the environment.
items.judge: The evaluation framework for vision-language models acting through a body has implications for generative applications.

items.title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI
items.details: Álvaro Díaz-Laureano, Roger Marí, Elías Masquil, Pablo Arias et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: SeasonStereo introduces a novel framework for robust dense stereo matching in multi-date satellite imagery, achieving accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art LiDAR-supervised models while eliminating the need for aligned real multi-date training data or LiDAR-derived labels. By training on synthetic image pairs with controlled seasonal variations and utilizing zero-shot geometric priors from foundation models, it enhances geometric detail and reduces supervision costs, facilitating large-scale 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous satellite images.
items.judge: The paper addresses 3D reconstruction from satellite imagery, which relates to generative media.

items.title: Towards Grounded GI Endoscopy VQA via Multi-Task Learning on Small VLMs
items.details: Itbaan Safwan, Ramail Khan, Muhammad Annas Shaikh, Muhammad Atif Tahir · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper presents a novel multi-task fine-tuning approach for visual question answering (VQA) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, leveraging existing VQA datasets with minimal additional annotation. By reusing expert-annotated polyp masks and employing a GI-domain pretrained classifier for weak supervision, the authors fine-tune three small vision-language models (VLMs) and achieve consistent accuracy improvements, along with enhanced alignment between answer tokens and relevant image regions, evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets.
items.judge: The paper discusses VLMs in the context of visual question answering, which is relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: Veritas++: Value-aware On-Policy Distillation for Perception-Enhanced AIGI Detection
items.details: Hao Tan, Jun Lan, Zichang Tan, Ajian Liu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: Veritas++ introduces a novel perception-enhanced reasoning framework for AI-Generated Image (AIGI) detection, addressing the limitations of existing multi-modal large language model (MLLM)-based detectors in capturing fine-grained anomalies. By implementing Perception-oriented Learning (PoRL) and Value-aware On-Policy Distillation (VaOPD), the framework significantly improves detection performance through a focus on intrinsic perception capabilities, yielding enhanced generalization across various benchmarks. The approach demonstrates effective bridging of perception gaps, allowing for efficient capability evolution without compromising existing performance. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/EricTan7/VeritasPP.
items.judge: This work on AI-generated image detection relates to generative image models.

items.title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation
items.details: Zijun Lin, Zeqing Wang, Cheston Tan, Bihan Wen et al. · 12 HF upvotes
items.summary: StatePlay introduces a state-aware game world model that jointly predicts visual content and game states, significantly enhancing mechanics-consistent generation. Utilizing a mixture-of-transformers architecture, it achieves an average normalized L1 distance for state prediction below 0.06 and improves mechanics fidelity in generated game rollouts by 18.6% compared to models lacking explicit state modeling. This approach emphasizes the critical role of state dynamics in generating gameplay that adheres to underlying game rules.
items.judge: The paper presents game world models for generating interactive environments, directly relevant to generative media.

items.title: Explicit Layer Modeling for Video Object Insertion and Layer Decomposition
items.details: Kyujin Han, Seungjoo Shin, Sunghyun Cho · 5 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces TriLayer, a large-scale triplet video dataset that provides explicit supervision for video object insertion and layer decomposition, addressing the limitations of existing methods that rely on implicit inference. The authors propose DBL-Diffusion, a dual-branch diffusion framework that models RGB composites and RGBA foreground layers, achieving significant improvements in insertion fidelity and decomposition quality. Experiments indicate that this explicit layer modeling enhances the realism and flexibility of video editing tasks, marking a notable advancement in layered video representation techniques.
items.judge: The paper introduces a new dataset and method for video object insertion and layer decomposition, relevant to video generation.

items.title: CADENCE: Closing the Reasoning Gap via Coverage-Adaptive On-Policy Distillation
items.details: Satyam Kumar, Saurabh Jha · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper presents CADENCE, a novel framework for on-policy knowledge distillation that addresses three key failure modes in existing methods, resulting in significant improvements in reasoning quality. By implementing mechanisms such as coverage-adaptive β scheduling and a dense reward system, CADENCE achieves a pass rate of 69.8% on GSM8K with a 0.5B student model, closing 63.2% of the gap to a 1.5B teacher, and surpassing the best baseline by 4.4 percentage points. items.title: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers
items.details: Sicheng Mo, Yuheng Li, Ziyang Leng, Krishna Kumar Singh et al. · 11 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces WorldWeaver (W^2), a streaming multi-agent video diffusion model that enhances the generation of consistent observations by incorporating cross-agent world state registers—learnable tokens that maintain shared world information and individual agent statuses. This approach, which includes a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for separate modeling of world states and visual frames, significantly improves logical consistency and generation quality in two-agent Minecraft video generation tasks. The model demonstrates superior performance compared to existing autoregressive video diffusion methods, addressing challenges in multi-agent and multi-view settings.
items.judge: This paper presents a multi-agent video diffusion model, highly relevant to generative media.

items.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
items.details: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue et al. · 26 HF upvotes
items.summary: SANA-Video 2.0 introduces a hybrid video diffusion transformer that achieves high-quality video generation at 720p on a single GPU while maintaining the long-sequence scaling benefits of linear attention. By employing Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention and Block Attention Residuals, it enhances effective rank by approximately 12% and achieves a VBench score of 84.30 in 13.2 seconds at 480p, outperforming larger softmax video models in latency and efficiency. The system's optimizations result in a forward pass that is 3.2x faster than a full-softmax baseline, making it 120x faster than previous models on comparable hardware.
items.judge: The paper presents a novel video generation model with efficient attention mechanisms.

items.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
items.details: Vedant Shah, Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Kiet Nguyen et al. · 3 HF upvotes
items.summary: GraphVid introduces a graph-conditioned image-to-video generation model that allows for interactive control through structured interaction graphs, significantly improving multi-object control in video generation. It achieves a reduction in FID by up to 39.9% and FVD by 37.6% compared to Motion-I2V, while also enhancing PSNR from 9.87 to 15.98 and SSIM from 0.38 to 0.61, all with less training data and fewer parameters. Additionally, the authors present GraphVid-Bench, a large-scale dataset with structured relational annotations to support the training of interaction-aware video generation models.
items.judge: This work focuses on controllable video generation, aligning well with generative media.

items.title: An Exam for Active Observers
items.details: Jiarui Zhang, Muzi Tao, Shangshang Wang, Ollie Liu et al. · 24 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces ActiveVision, a benchmark designed to evaluate active observation capabilities in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) through 17 tasks that require repeated visual perception. Current leading models, including GPT-5.5 and Claude Fable 5, perform poorly, achieving only 10.6% and 3.5% task completion rates, respectively, compared to human participants averaging 96.1%. These findings highlight a significant gap in active visual observation in existing MLLMs, suggesting a need for new architectures and training objectives to enhance perception-reasoning integration.
items.judge: The benchmark addresses active observation in multimodal models, relevant to generative media.

items.title: Lightning-AI/litgpt

items.summary: The Lightning-AI/litgpt repository provides over 20 high-performance LLMs along with comprehensive recipes for pretraining, finetuning, and deploying these models at scale. Notably, it emphasizes modular design choices that facilitate easy integration and customization, making it suitable for various applications in generative tasks. This resource aims to streamline the development process for ML researchers working with large language models.
items.judge: This project provides high-performance LLMs with recipes, relevant to generative media applications.

items.title: D-FINE-seg – detection, instance and semantic segmentation in one model
items.details: 4 HN pts · [discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48984984)
items.summary: D-FINE-seg is a unified model for detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. It integrates a multi-task learning framework that allows for simultaneous training on all three tasks, improving efficiency and reducing the need for separate models. Notably, it employs a shared backbone architecture, which enhances feature extraction and reduces computational overhead.
items.judge: The model addresses segmentation, which is relevant to image generation tasks.

items.title: Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Progressive Seed Pruning
items.details: Rogerio Guimaraes, Pietro Perona · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Progressive Seed Pruning (PSP), a novel method for improving inference-time scaling in diffusion models by allowing for aggressive pruning of less promising seed trajectories early in the generation process. This approach consistently outperforms traditional methods such as best-of-N and importance sampling, achieving higher GenEval scores and better human evaluations while maintaining a fixed compute budget. The method effectively enhances the quality of conditional image generation by optimizing the use of computational resources during inference.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for scaling diffusion models, applicable to generative media.

items.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
items.details: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao et al. · cs.CV cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces VLM-IE3D, a vision-language model that enhances 3D spatial awareness by integrating both implicit and explicit geometric representations derived from RGB videos. It employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) for high-level geometric priors and Explicit Geometry Tokens (EGTs) for detailed structures, achieving improved performance in 3D tasks such as detection, grounding, and reasoning without requiring additional 3D inputs. The model demonstrates consistent superiority across various benchmarks, indicating a significant advancement in 3D task handling for vision-language models.
items.judge: The paper discusses enhancing VLMs with 3D geometries, relevant to multi-modal generation.

items.title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
items.details: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces UniD, a unified video model that jointly predicts eight dense scene properties from disjoint, domain-specific datasets without requiring annotation overlap or pseudo-labeling. By leveraging a distillation approach with per-task experts and a pretrained diffusion model, UniD demonstrates competitive performance against specialized models and multi-task baselines, achieving improved generalization to unseen scene-task combinations and enhanced temporal and cross-task consistency. The model's effectiveness is validated through code and video results available at the provided URL.
items.judge: The unified video model addresses scene understanding, relevant for video generation tasks.

items.title: Expanding Flow Maps
items.details: Sophia Tang, Pranam Chatterjee · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces Expanding Flow Maps (EFMs), a novel class of flow-based generative models that enhance the generation process by allowing variable output dimensions and sequence lengths through an expanding interpolant. EFMs utilize two learnable operations—an expand operator that augments the state space with conditional noise and a transport map that advances the state along the interpolant—effectively enabling controllable generation across both continuous and discrete modalities. This framework improves upon existing fixed-dimension models by providing a principled approach for generating outputs of varying sizes, thereby broadening the applicability of flow-based generative models.
items.judge: The introduction of EFlows for generative models relates to controllable generation techniques.

items.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
items.details: Wen Ye, Yuxiao Qu, Aviral Kumar, Xuezhe Ma · cs.AI cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces MIRROR, a novel reinforcement learning approach that enhances multimodal reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs) by leveraging complementary reasoning paths from different views (text, image, and combined). Utilizing a new dataset called ODA-Data, which includes paired multimodal geometry problems, MIRROR employs a self-supervised strategy to optimize reasoning performance, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and consistency across modalities compared to standard reinforcement learning methods.
items.judge: The study on visual reasoning in VLMs has relevance to multimodal generation.

items.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
items.details: Dongjie Fu, Di Cao, Xize Cheng, Zihan Zhang et al. · cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces X$^3$-OPD, a novel cross-modal on-policy distillation framework that enhances reasoning capabilities in audio-language models by transferring knowledge from text-based models. It constructs a three-tier corpus that includes diverse reasoning scenarios, significantly improving audio-grounded reasoning and chain-of-thought quality on benchmarks like MMSU and MMAU, while maintaining existing model performance during domain shifts.
items.judge: This work on distilling reasoning into audio-language models is relevant to multimodal techniques.

items.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
items.details: Alagappan Valliappan · cs.LG cs.CL cs.PF
items.summary: The paper introduces Windowed-MTP, a novel approach that mitigates the full-context draft-KV tax in autoregressive generation at million-token contexts by utilizing a sliding window mechanism for the draft's attention, which reduces the KV cache size by approximately 99%. This method achieves a per-decode-step cost reduction of 28% to 44% across multiple architecture families without compromising the output distribution, while also reclaiming unused KV entries through a compact ring buffer. The approach is training-free and can be seamlessly integrated into existing systems.
items.judge: The paper addresses inference acceleration techniques relevant to generative models.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Hypernetwork-Based Knowledge Injection in Large Language Models
items.details: Nischay Dhankhar, Dos Baha, Abulhair Saparov · 14 HF upvotes
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel approach for train-time knowledge injection in large language models (LLMs) using hypernetworks, demonstrating that hypernetwork architectures can achieve reliable out-of-distribution generalization and predictive power law scaling with respect to depth, width, and target model size. The authors present the MegaWikiQA dataset, which contains tens of millions of multi-hop question-answer pairs, and show that hypernetwork-based injection outperforms traditional methods like LoRA finetuning in scaling efficiency, establishing a new framework for integrating factual knowledge into LLMs.
items.judge: The paper explores knowledge injection in LLMs, which has relevance to generative models.

items.title: NVlabs/Sana
items.details: `python` · 8,546★ · 18 stars today
items.summary: The NVlabs/Sana repository introduces a novel approach to high-resolution image synthesis using a Linear Diffusion Transformer, achieving significant improvements in efficiency and image quality. The model demonstrates a reduction in computational complexity while maintaining high fidelity in generated images, making it suitable for real-time applications. Notably, the design leverages linear attention mechanisms to scale effectively with larger image resolutions.

items.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
items.details: Hongxin Zhang, Chunru Lin, Junyan Li, Zhou Xian et al. · cs.RO cs.AI cs.CL
items.summary: GS-Agent introduces an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automates the creation of dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions, significantly improving upon traditional manual methods. By integrating physics engines and employing specialized agents for tasks such as asset curation and motion control, GS-Agent ensures physical plausibility and controllability, enabling the generation of diverse interactions among complex objects. Experimental results demonstrate its capability to produce rich, interactive environments with advanced cinematic camera and lighting configurations.
items.judge: The paper addresses creating 4D physical worlds using generative simulation from natural language.

items.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
items.details: Vedant Shah, Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Kiet Nguyen et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: GraphVid introduces a novel graph-conditioned image-to-video generation model that enhances controllability by allowing users to specify multi-object interactions through structured interaction graphs, significantly improving upon traditional trajectory-based control methods. It achieves a reduction in FID by up to 39.9% and FVD by 37.6%, while also increasing PSNR from 9.87 to 15.98 and SSIM from 0.38 to 0.61, all while utilizing less training data and fewer parameters than existing motion-control approaches. Additionally, the authors present GraphVid-Bench, a large-scale dataset with structured relational annotations to support the training of interaction-aware video generation models.
items.judge: The introduction of interactive graph-controllable video generation is highly relevant to video generation.

items.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
items.details: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: SANA-Video 2.0 introduces a hybrid video diffusion transformer architecture that achieves high-quality video generation at 720p using a single GPU, matching the quality of full-softmax video diffusion transformers while significantly improving efficiency. By employing Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention and Block Attention Residuals, it enhances effective rank by approximately 12% and achieves a VBench score of 84.30 in 13.2 seconds at 480p, with a forward pass that is 3.2x faster than a comparable full-softmax model. The system's optimizations make it 120x faster than the Wan 2.2-A14B model, enabling scalable long, high-resolution video generation.
items.judge: This paper introduces a video generation model with efficient architecture, directly relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Future Rendering $\neq$ Future Surface: A Benchmark and Dataset for Dynamic Surface Reconstruction Beyond the Observed Window
items.details: Yukun Shi, Minglun Gong · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces FutureSurf, a benchmark and dataset for evaluating dynamic surface reconstruction beyond the observed time window, addressing a gap in current methodologies that focus solely on the observed data. It provides a controlled environment with exact future ground truth and falsification controls, revealing that existing methods like DG-Mesh exhibit a 2.7-4.1× gap in future surface prediction accuracy. The dataset and evaluation tools are available on Hugging Face and GitHub, facilitating further research in future-time surface reconstruction.
items.judge: The paper introduces a benchmark and dataset for dynamic surface reconstruction, relevant to 3D generation.

items.title: Adaptive Identity Anchoring: Closed-Loop Keyframe Placement for Synthetic Paired Supervision in Video Face Swapping
items.details: Logan Robbins · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces Adaptive Identity Anchoring (AIA), a novel approach for improving video face swapping by dynamically placing identity anchors based on a closed-loop feedback mechanism that evaluates frame quality against a reference identity. This method enhances the robustness of identity preservation over long clips, addressing issues of drift and over-smoothing by integrating Reality-Referenced Texture Restoration, which restores micro-texture from real footage. The authors propose falsifiable experiments to validate the effectiveness of their approach, including comparisons of anchor placement strategies and texture quality assessments.
items.judge: The paper presents a method for video face swapping, which is directly related to generative video models.

items.title: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers
items.details: Sicheng Mo, Yuheng Li, Ziyang Leng, Krishna Kumar Singh et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces WorldWeaver (W^2), a streaming multi-agent video diffusion model that enhances autoregressive generation by incorporating cross-agent world state registers, which are learnable tokens that maintain and update shared world information across agents. This approach improves logical consistency and generation quality in multi-agent settings, as demonstrated through extensive experiments in two-agent Minecraft video generation. The model's Mixture-of-Transformers architecture further differentiates between world state and visual frame modeling, optimizing performance in complex interactive environments.
items.judge: This work presents a multi-agent video diffusion model, directly related to world models and video generation.

items.title: ElasticTTT: Prior-Preserving Test-Time Tuning for Video Editing
items.details: Yueyi Liu, Chi Zhang, Sen Cui, Miao Liu · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: The paper introduces ElasticTTT, a novel framework for Test-Time Tuning (TTT) that addresses the issue of Prior Collapse in pretrained diffusion models during video editing. By implementing Target Distribution Regularization, Contrastive CFG, and an Asynchronous Noise Schedule, ElasticTTT preserves the generative prior and improves the model's performance in one-shot video editing, achieving state-of-the-art results. The proposed methods effectively prevent sharp memorization and maintain the integrity of unedited regions, enhancing the overall generative capabilities of the model.
items.judge: The paper discusses Test-Time Tuning for video editing using generative models.

items.title: Texture++: Elevating 3D Asset Texture Resolution with a Region-Aware Diffusion Model
items.details: Shuaiwei Wang, Shi Li, Jieting Xu, Yuchi Huo et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Texture++, a novel framework for texture super-resolution that significantly enhances low-resolution textures of 3D assets by reformulating the task in UV space and integrating outputs from multiple rendered views. It employs an adaptive view selection strategy and a quadtree-based region organization method to improve texture coherence and detail, achieving superior results compared to existing methods. Comprehensive evaluations indicate that Texture++ provides marked improvements in texture quality, revitalizing valuable assets in industries such as film and video games.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for enhancing 3D asset textures using super-resolution.

items.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Structured Dynamics from Videos
items.details: Lukas Knobel, Andrew Zisserman, Yuki M. Asano · 12 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces the Structured Dynamics Model (SDM), which effectively separates object motion from camera motion in video analysis by utilizing future-feature prediction on frozen features from a pretrained image vision transformer. SDM demonstrates superior performance on the ProbeMotion evaluation suite, outperforming traditional baselines and competing favorably with strongly supervised models like VGGT, despite relying on weaker supervision. This approach highlights the potential of repurposing pretrained image models for robust motion representation in video dynamics.
items.judge: The paper addresses learning motion dynamics from videos, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: Dataset Distillation by Influence Matching
items.details: Haoru Tan, Wang Wang, Sitong Wu, Xiuzhe Wu et al. · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Influence Matching (Inf-Match), a novel approach to dataset distillation that focuses on aligning the final training outcomes rather than the training process itself. Inf-Match employs a fully differentiable, sample-level influence estimator that operates in linear time, achieving a 4.7% accuracy improvement on Tiny-ImageNet (31.5% accuracy) compared to the previous state-of-the-art, NCFM. Additionally, it demonstrates superior performance in vision-language distillation tasks on Flickr30K, outperforming NCFM by 2.5% with synthetic samples ranging from 200 to 1000. The code is available at https://github.com/hrtan/infmatch.
items.judge: The paper discusses dataset distillation, which is relevant for generative media.

items.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay
items.details: Baohao Liao, Hanze Dong, Christof Monz, Xinxing Xu et al. · 7 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation (ReOPD), an innovative approach that enhances on-policy distillation for multi-turn interactions by reusing pre-collected teacher trajectories, significantly reducing the need for costly real-time environment interactions. ReOPD achieves at least a fourfold increase in efficiency per rollout compared to traditional on-policy distillation while maintaining or improving accuracy in tasks such as mathematical reasoning and search environments. This method addresses the challenges of distribution shift between student occupancy and teacher reliability, enabling scalable distillation across various tools and tasks without incurring additional tool calls during student training.
items.judge: This work on on-policy distillation is applicable to generative media contexts.

items.title: Show, Don't Tell: Evaluating Spatial Cognition in Generative Pixels Rather Than LLM Text
items.details: Xu Wang, Kaixiang Yao, Miao Pan, Xiaohe Zhou et al. · 34 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces ProVisE, a benchmark-agnostic framework that evaluates spatial cognition in image-generation models by eliciting visual answers rather than relying on text or coordinates, addressing the mismatch in existing spatial reasoning benchmarks. It includes the SpatialGen-Bench, a curated dataset of 470 samples across 14 spatial subtasks, demonstrating that image-generation models can perform competitively in spatial tasks when answers are expressed in pixel space, while text-output VLMs excel in compositional reasoning. This work provides a structured approach to assess and compare the spatial capabilities of different model types.
items.judge: The paper evaluates spatial cognition in generative contexts, linking to multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Robostral Navigate
items.details: Arjun Majumdar, Avinash Sooriyarachchi, Benjamin Tibi, Chris Bamford et al. · 8 HF upvotes
items.summary: Robostral Navigate introduces an 8B vision-language model that operates solely on monocular RGB images to predict waypoints for navigation, achieving a state-of-the-art success rate of 77.4% on the R2R-CE benchmark—10.5 points higher than the best monocular method and 5.3 points above the leading depth or multi-camera systems. The model's design minimizes sensor assumptions and generalizes across various robotic platforms, utilizing a novel prefix-caching training method that reduces training tokens by 22x and training time from months to days. Additionally, a tree-based attention mask enhances visually grounded action prediction, further improving exploration and recovery capabilities.
items.judge: The paper introduces a vision-language model for navigation, relevant to multimodal applications.

items.title: Predictive Divergence Masks for LLM RL
items.details: Xiangxin Zhou, Jiarui Yao, Penghui Qi, Bowen Ping et al. · 8 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces predictive divergence masks for reinforcement learning in large language models (LLMs), enhancing the direction criterion of the PPO-style approach by predicting whether the next policy-gradient step will increase or decrease the divergence between behavior and training policies. This method, which employs two lightweight top-K estimators for discrete softmax policies, demonstrates improved alignment with the actual divergence change compared to traditional sampled-token importance ratios, leading to enhanced RL training performance across various model scales and precision settings.
items.judge: The paper discusses reinforcement learning techniques applicable to LLMs, which can be relevant to generative media.

items.title: ENTRAP-VL: A Taxonomic Probe for Dual Contextual Entrainment in Vision-Language Models
items.details: Karan Goyal, Afreen Hossain, Debojyoti Das, Vishal Bhutani · 2 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces ENTRAP-VL, a novel dataset and taxonomic framework designed to investigate contextual entrainment in vision-language models (VLMs), addressing a gap in the current understanding of how auxiliary context influences model outputs. This dataset consists of 1,500 items categorized across two axes—context association and truth relationship—allowing for a structured examination of both textual and visual entrainment conditions. The authors emphasize that this dual-modality approach is essential for studying entrainment in VLMs, as it reveals complexities not present in unimodal models.
items.judge: The investigation of contextual entrainment in vision-language models is relevant to multimodal generation.

items.title: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer

The library is particularly focused on scalability and ease of integration with existing ML frameworks.

items.title: tile-ai/tilelang

items.title: Vera: Identity-Faithful Human Subject-to-Video Generation
items.details: Yulong Xu, Xinyue Liu, Shujuan Li, huafeng shi et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: Vera introduces a unified human-centric subject-to-video (S2V) generation framework that significantly enhances identity consistency in both single- and multi-person scenarios. By constructing a million-pair identity-aligned dataset and implementing two key innovations—Identity-Focal Masked Supervision (IFMS) and Reference-Aware Layer-wise Attention (RALA)—Vera improves human identity consistency and reduces identity confusion, outperforming previous methods in maintaining stable identity anchors and natural motion.
items.judge: This paper presents advancements in subject-to-video generation, relevant to generative video models.

items.title: StreamHOI: Interaction-aware Temporal Memory Adaptation for Streaming HOI Video Generation
items.details: Zejing Rao, Haoxian Zhang, Xiaoqiang Liu, Yiping Meng et al. · cs.CV cs.AI
items.summary: StreamHOI introduces a low-latency streaming framework for long-duration human-object interaction (HOI) video generation, achieving 17.6 FPS with a 0.75s first-chunk latency. The framework enhances interaction plausibility and object fidelity by employing a memory distance scaling module and bias-guided memory-specialized training, addressing the limitations of traditional sink-local memory designs in streaming contexts. This approach allows for effective historical memory organization tailored to transformer block behaviors, significantly improving real-time interactive applications in HOI video generation.
items.judge: The paper presents a framework for low-latency streaming human-object interaction video generation.

items.title: HeadCast: Casting Attention Heads for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
items.details: Jinliang Shen, Lianghao Su, Zheming Li, Kang He et al. · cs.CV cs.LG
items.summary: The paper introduces HeadCast, a training-free framework that optimizes autoregressive video generation by restructuring the Key-Value (KV) cache based on the heterogeneous behaviors of attention heads. This approach accelerates inference by up to 1.62x at 720P and 1.95x at 1080P while maintaining video quality comparable to full attention and minimizing flickering artifacts. The implementation is available on GitHub, allowing for easy integration into existing models.
items.judge: The paper proposes a method for efficient autoregressive video generation, directly related to generative video models.

items.title: ATSplat: Compact Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Token Expansion
items.details: Cho In, Jeonghwan Cho, Mijin Yoo, Gim Hee Lee et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: ATSplat introduces a novel feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that enhances adaptive capacity allocation by utilizing Adaptive 3D Tokens, allowing for a more efficient representation of scene complexity. This method reduces the number of Gaussians by over 5.7 times compared to traditional dense feed-forward approaches while achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality. Notably, ATSplat can reconstruct scenes from 12 input images at 512x960 resolution in under one second and render high-quality novel views at 1136 FPS using only 311K Gaussians.
items.judge: The paper discusses a novel approach to 3D Gaussian splatting, relevant to generative 3D modeling.

items.title: Self Gradient Forcing: Native Long Video Extrapolation
items.details: Junhao Zhuang, Shiyi Zhang, Yuxuan Bian, Yaowei Li et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces Self Gradient Forcing (SGF), a novel two-pass training strategy that enhances autoregressive video generation by addressing the historical context-gradient gap. SGF enables the model to effectively encode context into causal memory, resulting in improved long-video extrapolation performance, particularly in terms of subject identity, background consistency, and temporal stability. The method demonstrates significant advancements over existing Self Forcing techniques, allowing for extrapolation of videos lasting several minutes from just a 5-second training window.
items.judge: The paper discusses a novel approach to video generation that addresses exposure bias in autoregressive models.

items.title: RS-RIE-Bench: Benchmarking Reasoning-Guided Remote Sensing Image Editing
items.details: Zihan Qin, Boao Xu, Zhao Dong, Yingping Sun et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces RS-RIE-Bench, the first benchmark specifically designed for reasoning-guided remote sensing image editing, addressing gaps in existing benchmarks that focus on natural images. It categorizes tasks into temporal, causal, and spatial reasoning, evaluating models on target region plausibility, non-target region preservation, and image quality consistency. Evaluation results indicate that even the best-performing model achieves only 24.28% accuracy under strict criteria, highlighting significant limitations in current models' reasoning capabilities, particularly in causal and spatial reasoning.
items.judge: This paper introduces a benchmark for reasoning-guided remote sensing image editing, relevant to generative image tasks.

items.title: PercepCap: Video Captioner with Structured Spatio-Temporal Perception
items.details: Yifan Xu, Zihao Wang, Zhixiao Wang, Jiaming Zhang et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: PercepCap introduces a novel video captioning framework that enhances spatio-temporal understanding by explicitly generating a perception trace of object trajectories and temporal events before producing the final caption. This two-stage training approach, which includes Perceive-then-Describe Supervised Fine-tuning and Perception-Grounded Reinforcement Learning, significantly improves caption quality over the Qwen3-VL baseline, demonstrating superior performance in both direct captioning and caption-to-QA evaluations. The methodology also incorporates a Caption-Anchored Perception Data Construction pipeline to ensure alignment between perceptual evidence and generated captions.
items.judge: The paper presents a video captioning model that enhances spatio-temporal understanding, relevant to video generation.

items.title: Look Less, Think Faster: Joint Token-Compute Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
items.details: Pengcheng Wang, Zhiquan Wang, Jayoung Lee, Zhuoyan Xu et al. · cs.CV
items.summary: The paper introduces SmartVL, a unified adaptive inference framework for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) that jointly optimizes the number of visual tokens and the computation resources of the language model based on input content and compute budgets. By employing a vision-side token controller and an LLM-side compute controller that are trained to coordinate with a shared budget encoding, SmartVL achieves significant improvements in accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, outperforming previous adaptive methods across multiple benchmarks. The framework's design allows for dynamic allocation strategies that adapt to input complexity and runtime constraints, enhancing practical deployment of MLLMs.
items.judge: This work focuses on optimizing inference costs in multimodal LLMs, relevant for practical deployment.

items.title: Moving Alphabet: A Controlled Study of Training Data for Text-to-Video Generation
items.details: Amber Yijia Zheng, Lu Liu, Raymond A. Yeh, Xi Yin · 0 HF upvotes
items.summary: The paper introduces "Moving Alphabet," a procedural testbed designed to investigate the impact of training data distribution and caption quality on text-to-video generation models. The study reveals that a diverse video content distribution is essential for generalization, while caption quality significantly influences model performance and training efficiency. Additionally, it finds that while classifier-free guidance can partially recover performance from models trained on poor data, it cannot fully compensate for inadequate pre-training, highlighting the need for improved data curation in large-scale text-to-video model development.
